[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/data-sources.html "Data Sources — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/catalog/index.html "datafusion.catalog — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[4]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html "datafusion.context — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[5]: https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/custom-table-providers.html "Custom Table Provider — Apache DataFusion  documentation"

# DataFusion Advanced — 10) Data source registration and table ingestion

This section follows the dense, agent-facing technical-reference style of the Cyclopts source material. 

## 10.0 Version anchor

Current package anchor: **`datafusion==54.0.0`**, released **June 29, 2026**, requiring **Python >=3.10**. DataFusion Python is the Python binding to Apache Arrow DataFusion and supports SQL/DataFrame execution against file and Arrow-compatible sources, query optimization, Python UDFs, PyArrow/Pandas-compatible exchange, and Substrait plan serialization. ([PyPI][1])

```bash id="uwdfpw"
python -m pip install "datafusion==54.0.0"
```

```python id="sg9s9h"
import datafusion
assert datafusion.__version__ == "54.0.0"
```

---

## 10.1 Core ingestion invariant

`read_*` APIs return **anonymous lazy `DataFrame` handles**. `register_*` APIs mutate the `SessionContext` catalog and create a **named table** addressable by `ctx.table("name")` and SQL. `SessionContext` is the main interface for executing queries and creating DataFrames, and it maintains the session state between Python code and the DataFusion engine. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```text id="kbqdpw"
read_*:
  path/object -> DataFrame
  no catalog side effect
  no SQL table name
  useful for one-off pipelines

register_*:
  name + path/object/provider -> None
  catalog side effect
  SQL-visible table/view
  reusable across multiple DataFrames/queries
```

```python id="wsrirj"
from datafusion import SessionContext

ctx = SessionContext()

# Anonymous DataFrame.
df = ctx.read_parquet("events.parquet")

# Registered table.
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")
df2 = ctx.table("events")
df3 = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events")
```

The Parquet guide shows this exact read-vs-register distinction: `ctx.read_parquet("file.parquet")` returns a DataFrame, while `ctx.register_parquet("file", "file.parquet"); ctx.table("file")` queries a registered table. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 10.2 Registration API map

| API                       | Input type                                | Return | SQL-visible | Primary use                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -----: | ----------: | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `register_csv`            | CSV path or path list                     | `None` |         yes | named CSV table                                        |
| `register_parquet`        | Parquet path                              | `None` |         yes | named Parquet table                                    |
| `register_json`           | line-delimited JSON path                  | `None` |         yes | named JSON table                                       |
| `register_avro`           | Avro path                                 | `None` |         yes | named Avro table                                       |
| `register_arrow`          | Arrow IPC path                            | `None` |         yes | named Arrow IPC table                                  |
| `register_dataset`        | `pyarrow.dataset.Dataset`                 | `None` |         yes | PyArrow-discovered dataset                             |
| `register_record_batches` | `list[list[pyarrow.RecordBatch]]`         | `None` |         yes | partitioned in-memory test/runtime table               |
| `register_batch`          | one `pyarrow.RecordBatch`                 | `None` |         yes | simple in-memory test table                            |
| `register_table`          | `Table`, provider, `DataFrame`, `Dataset` | `None` |         yes | generic provider/table registration                    |
| `register_view`           | `DataFrame`                               | `None` |         yes | logical view over existing plan                        |
| `register_listing_table`  | file/object-store path                    | `None` |         yes | multi-file table assembled from object-store locations |

`SessionContext` exposes all of these registration APIs in its method inventory. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

# 10.3 `read_*` vs `register_*`

## 10.3.1 Anonymous path

```python id="ibpwjk"
df = (
    ctx.read_parquet("warehouse/events/")
       .filter("amount > 0")
       .select("user_id", "amount")
)
```

Use when:

```text id="e0w6qu"
source is one-off
no SQL table name required
no catalog mutation desired
function should be side-effect-free
pipeline is local to one caller
```

## 10.3.2 Registered path

```python id="4yxk55"
ctx.register_parquet("events", "warehouse/events/")

df = ctx.sql("""
    SELECT user_id, amount
    FROM events
    WHERE amount > 0
""")
```

Use when:

```text id="6cjiz9"
dataset is reused across queries
SQL should address source by name
query builders should operate over stable logical names
source setup belongs to application bootstrap
catalog state is intentional
```

## 10.3.3 Agent rule

```text id="035734"
Data source setup:
  register_*

Query construction:
  ctx.table(...)
  ctx.sql(...)
  DataFrame transformations

Never mix source registration side effects inside pure query-builder helpers.
```

---

# 10.4 CSV registration: `register_csv`

## 10.4.1 Signature

```python id="fdz0cg"
ctx.register_csv(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path | list[str | Path],
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    has_header: bool = True,
    delimiter: str = ",",
    schema_infer_max_records: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INFER_SCHEMA,
    file_extension: str = ".csv",
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
    options: CsvReadOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_csv` registers a CSV file or list of paths as a SQL-referenceable table. If `schema=None`, DataFusion infers schema from file data; for headerless files, inferred schemas get default column names. It supports delimiter, schema-inference row limit, file-extension selection, text compression, and advanced `CsvReadOptions`; `options` cannot be combined with the other method options. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.4.2 Production schema

```python id="g78lc5"
import pyarrow as pa

events_schema = pa.schema([
    ("user_id", pa.int64()),
    ("country", pa.string()),
    ("amount", pa.float64()),
    ("event_ts", pa.timestamp("us")),
])

ctx.register_csv(
    "events_csv",
    "warehouse/events_csv/",
    schema=events_schema,
    has_header=True,
    file_extension=".csv",
)
```

## 10.4.3 Compressed CSV

```python id="ryred5"
ctx.register_csv(
    "events_csv_gz",
    "warehouse/events_csv_gz/",
    schema=events_schema,
    has_header=True,
    file_extension=".gz",
    file_compression_type="gzip",
)
```

## 10.4.4 Advanced CSV options

```python id="1nopm4"
from datafusion import CsvReadOptions

options = (
    CsvReadOptions()
    .with_schema(events_schema)
    .with_has_header(True)
    .with_delimiter(";")
    .with_quote('"')
    .with_escape("\\")
    .with_comment("#")
    .with_null_regex(r"^(null|NULL|N/A)$")
    .with_file_extension(".csv")
    .with_file_compression_type("")
)

ctx.register_csv("events_csv", "warehouse/events_csv/", options=options)
```

## 10.4.5 CSV deployment rules

```text id="qmrc3r"
CSV production defaults:
  - explicit pyarrow.Schema
  - explicit has_header
  - explicit delimiter when non-comma
  - explicit file_extension for directory scans
  - explicit file_compression_type for compressed inputs
  - CsvReadOptions for quote/escape/comment/null handling
  - avoid schema inference in production multi-file feeds
```

---

# 10.5 Parquet registration: `register_parquet`

## 10.5.1 Signature

```python id="d87mjh"
ctx.register_parquet(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    parquet_pruning: bool = True,
    file_extension: str = ".parquet",
    skip_metadata: bool = True,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_sort_order: Sequence[Sequence[SortKey]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_parquet` registers a Parquet source as a SQL-referenceable table. It supports partition columns, predicate-based row-group pruning, file-extension filtering, metadata skipping to avoid schema conflicts, explicit schema, and file sort order; sort keys may be column names, expressions, or `SortExpr` values. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.5.2 Standard Parquet registration

```python id="9qodde"
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "warehouse/events/",
    parquet_pruning=True,
    file_extension=".parquet",
    skip_metadata=True,
)
```

## 10.5.3 Partitioned Parquet

```python id="5dmra8"
import pyarrow as pa

ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "warehouse/events/",
    table_partition_cols=[
        ("dt", pa.string()),
        ("country", pa.string()),
    ],
    parquet_pruning=True,
    file_extension=".parquet",
)
```

## 10.5.4 Explicit schema

```python id="u7myun"
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "warehouse/events/",
    schema=events_schema,
    parquet_pruning=True,
)
```

## 10.5.5 File sort order

```python id="b2f1fm"
from datafusion import col

ctx.register_parquet(
    "events_sorted",
    "warehouse/events_sorted/",
    file_sort_order=[
        [col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True, nulls_first=False)]
    ],
)
```

## 10.5.6 Parquet deployment rules

```text id="edb6us"
Parquet production defaults:
  - prefer Parquet over CSV for stable analytical stores
  - keep parquet_pruning=True unless debugging
  - set table_partition_cols for directory-partitioned data
  - use explicit schema when reading mixed-writer directories
  - keep skip_metadata=True when file metadata conflicts occur
  - set file_sort_order only when upstream data is genuinely sorted
```

---

# 10.6 JSON registration: `register_json`

## 10.6.1 Signature

```python id="wxq37m"
ctx.register_json(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    schema_infer_max_records: int = 1000,
    file_extension: str = ".json",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_json` registers a JSON file as a SQL-referenceable table. It supports explicit schema, inference row limit, extension filtering, partition columns, and compression. JSON reads are for **line-delimited JSON** in the corresponding `read_json` API. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="l8qp9y"
ctx.register_json(
    "events_json",
    "warehouse/events_json/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".json",
)
```

Compressed JSON:

```python id="nkhxlh"
ctx.register_json(
    "events_json_gz",
    "warehouse/events_json_gz/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".gz",
    file_compression_type="gzip",
)
```

## 10.6.2 JSON deployment rules

```text id="0e1wz3"
JSON production defaults:
  - assume line-delimited JSON, not arbitrary JSON arrays
  - provide explicit pyarrow.Schema
  - use schema_infer_max_records only for exploration
  - set file_extension for directory scans
  - set file_compression_type for compressed JSON
  - migrate stable high-volume JSON feeds to Parquet
```

---

# 10.7 Avro registration: `register_avro`

## 10.7.1 Signature

```python id="uepxjj"
ctx.register_avro(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".avro",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_avro` registers an Avro file as a SQL-referenceable table and supports explicit schema, file-extension selection, and partition columns. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="p60l3s"
ctx.register_avro(
    "events_avro",
    "warehouse/events_avro/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".avro",
)
```

## 10.7.2 Avro deployment rules

```text id="3i1nq4"
Avro defaults:
  - use when upstream systems emit Avro
  - provide schema when consistency matters
  - use partition columns for directory partition data
  - consider Parquet for optimized analytical storage
```

---

# 10.8 Arrow IPC registration: `register_arrow`

## 10.8.1 Signature

```python id="ur73ts"
ctx.register_arrow(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".arrow",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_arrow` registers an Arrow IPC file as a SQL-referenceable table. It supports explicit schema override, non-default file extensions, and partition columns. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="pj3j77"
ctx.register_arrow(
    "events_arrow",
    "warehouse/events_arrow/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".arrow",
)
```

Non-default extension:

```python id="rlswnc"
ctx.register_arrow(
    "events_ipc",
    "warehouse/events_ipc/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".ipc",
)
```

The API docs explicitly show using `schema=` to override inference and `file_extension=".ipc"` for non-default Arrow IPC extensions. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

# 10.9 PyArrow Dataset registration: `register_dataset`

## 10.9.1 Signature

```python id="8zr9ey"
ctx.register_dataset(
    name: str,
    dataset: pyarrow.dataset.Dataset,
) -> None
```

`register_dataset` registers a `pyarrow.dataset.Dataset` as a table. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="c6msgq"
import pyarrow.dataset as ds

dataset = ds.dataset("warehouse/events/", format="parquet")

ctx.register_dataset("events_ds", dataset)

df = ctx.sql("""
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM events_ds
    GROUP BY country
""")
```

## 10.9.2 Dataset deployment rules

```text id="t2sxeo"
Use register_dataset when:
  - PyArrow already owns discovery/options
  - upstream code produces pyarrow.dataset.Dataset
  - the table must be SQL-visible
  - DataFusion should query an externally constructed dataset

Avoid when:
  - direct register_parquet/register_csv options are enough
  - you need provider-specific pushdown not exposed by PyArrow dataset
```

The data-source docs note that older Delta Lake interop through Arrow Dataset may lack features such as filter pushdown and can cause significant performance differences compared with native table-provider integration. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

# 10.10 RecordBatch ingestion: `register_record_batches` and `register_batch`

## 10.10.1 `register_record_batches`

```python id="toogev"
ctx.register_record_batches(
    name: str,
    partitions: list[list[pyarrow.RecordBatch]],
) -> None
```

`register_record_batches` converts provided `pyarrow.RecordBatch` partitions into a table and registers that table in the session. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="yxg74e"
import pyarrow as pa

batch0 = pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({
    "user_id": [1, 2],
    "amount": [10.0, 20.0],
})

batch1 = pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({
    "user_id": [3, 4],
    "amount": [30.0, 40.0],
})

ctx.register_record_batches(
    "events_mem",
    [
        [batch0],  # partition 0
        [batch1],  # partition 1
    ],
)

ctx.sql("SELECT sum(amount) AS total FROM events_mem").show()
```

Partition shape:

```text id="m3ut8k"
list[
  list[RecordBatch],  # partition 0
  list[RecordBatch],  # partition 1
  ...
]
```

## 10.10.2 `register_batch`

```python id="c0lnm3"
ctx.register_batch(
    name: str,
    batch: pyarrow.RecordBatch,
) -> None
```

`register_batch` registers a single `pyarrow.RecordBatch` as a table. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="ijhvgv"
batch = pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
ctx.register_batch("batch_tbl", batch)
```

## 10.10.3 RecordBatch deployment rules

```text id="5q3o0f"
Use record batches for:
  - deterministic unit tests
  - in-memory temporary tables
  - adapter tests without filesystem/object store
  - partitioning behavior tests

Avoid for:
  - bulk ingestion from Python row loops
  - large persistent datasets
  - data that should live as Parquet/Arrow IPC/object-store files
```

---

# 10.11 Generic provider/table registration: `register_table`

## 10.11.1 Signature

```python id="yzdwjz"
ctx.register_table(
    name: str,
    table: Table | TableProviderExportable | DataFrame | pyarrow.dataset.Dataset,
) -> None
```

`register_table` registers any object convertible into a DataFusion `Table`, and the registered table can be referenced from SQL statements executed against the same context. `register_table_provider(...)` is documented as deprecated in favor of `register_table(...)`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="zdfm3o"
ctx.register_table("events_table", some_table_or_provider_or_dataframe_or_dataset)
df = ctx.table("events_table")
```

## 10.11.2 Custom table provider

Custom data sources can be integrated by implementing the `TableProvider` interface in Rust, exposing an `FFI_TableProvider` through a PyCapsule, and then registering the provider with `ctx.register_table(...)`. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

```python id="f48j04"
ctx.register_table("capsule_table", provider)
ctx.table("capsule_table").show()
```

## 10.11.3 Generic table deployment rules

```text id="gdf3oz"
Use register_table for:
  - custom TableProvider exports
  - Delta/Iceberg/provider-backed sources
  - pyarrow.dataset.Dataset when generic table path is desired
  - DataFrame-as-table registration

Prefer format-specific register_* when:
  - the source is simple CSV/Parquet/JSON/Avro/Arrow IPC
  - you need format-specific options like pruning/compression/file_extension
```

---

# 10.12 View registration: `register_view`

## 10.12.1 Signature

```python id="oxvr6m"
ctx.register_view(
    name: str,
    df: DataFrame,
) -> None
```

`register_view` registers a `DataFrame` as a SQL-visible view under the supplied name. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="b8z7n5"
from datafusion import col, lit

positive_events = (
    ctx.table("events")
       .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
       .select("user_id", "country", "amount")
)

ctx.register_view("positive_events", positive_events)

ctx.sql("""
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM positive_events
    GROUP BY country
""").show()
```

PyPI’s project description also shows registering a DataFrame as a view using `SessionContext.register_view`. ([PyPI][1])

## 10.12.2 View deployment rules

```text id="u1ajjf"
Use register_view when:
  - a DataFrame API plan should become SQL-visible
  - a derived logical relation is reused
  - you want query composition without materializing intermediates

Do not use view registration when:
  - the derived DataFrame is used only once
  - catalog side effects are undesirable
  - tenant isolation requires ephemeral contexts
```

---

# 10.13 Listing table registration: `register_listing_table`

## 10.13.1 Signature

```python id="ge6n63"
ctx.register_listing_table(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".parquet",
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_sort_order: Sequence[Sequence[SortKey]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_listing_table` registers multiple files as a single table and creates a table that can assemble files from locations in an `ObjectStore`; it supports partition columns, file-extension filtering, explicit schema, and file sort order. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="zqns2o"
ctx.register_listing_table(
    name="events_listing",
    path="s3://bucket/events/",
    table_partition_cols=[
        ("dt", pa.string()),
        ("country", pa.string()),
    ],
    file_extension=".parquet",
    schema=events_schema,
)
```

## 10.13.2 Listing-table deployment rules

```text id="rpojqh"
Use register_listing_table when:
  - one table spans many files
  - files live behind an ObjectStore
  - extension filtering matters
  - directory partition columns must be surfaced
  - provider should discover/assemble files as one table

Prefer register_parquet when:
  - Parquet-specific options like parquet_pruning/skip_metadata are needed directly
  - simple local/path registration is sufficient
```

---

# 10.14 Schema inference vs explicit `pyarrow.Schema`

## 10.14.1 Inference-capable sources

```text id="x0m67y"
CSV:
  schema=None -> infer from data
  schema_infer_max_records controls inference sample size
  headerless inference creates default column names

JSON:
  schema=None -> infer from line-delimited JSON
  schema_infer_max_records controls inference sample size

Parquet:
  schema=None -> infer from file metadata/data
  skip_metadata can avoid conflicts due to schema metadata

Arrow IPC:
  file carries schema; explicit schema can override

Avro:
  source carries schema; explicit schema can override
```

CSV inference behavior and headerless default column names are documented in both `read_csv` and `register_csv`; JSON exposes `schema_infer_max_records`; Parquet exposes schema inference plus `skip_metadata` to avoid schema conflicts due to file schema metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.14.2 Production schema rule

```python id="hzsnxl"
import pyarrow as pa

events_schema = pa.schema([
    ("event_id", pa.string()),
    ("user_id", pa.int64()),
    ("event_type", pa.string()),
    ("amount", pa.float64()),
    ("event_ts", pa.timestamp("us")),
    ("country", pa.string()),
])
```

```python id="ncqt6t"
ctx.register_csv("events_csv", "warehouse/events_csv/", schema=events_schema)
ctx.register_json("events_json", "warehouse/events_json/", schema=events_schema)
ctx.register_parquet("events", "warehouse/events/", schema=events_schema)
```

## 10.14.3 Agent schema policy

```text id="p0jpbk"
Exploration:
  schema=None acceptable
  schema_infer_max_records acceptable
  inspect df.schema()
  add limit().show()

Production:
  explicit pyarrow.Schema for CSV/JSON
  explicit schema for mixed-writer Parquet directories
  stable partition column types
  schema assertions in tests
  no silent reliance on inferred headerless CSV names
```

---

# 10.15 Partition columns

## 10.15.1 Syntax

```python id="y0w2me"
table_partition_cols=[
    ("dt", pa.string()),
    ("country", pa.string()),
]
```

Partition columns appear across read/register APIs for CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, Arrow IPC, and listing tables, with naming differences between some read APIs such as `file_partition_cols` for `read_avro` / `read_arrow` and `table_partition_cols` for table registration. The context API documents partition-column parameters on these methods. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.15.2 Consistent partition policy

```python id="aa2cqm"
PARTITION_COLS = [
    ("dt", pa.string()),
    ("region", pa.string()),
]

ctx.register_parquet(
    "events_parquet",
    "warehouse/events_parquet/",
    table_partition_cols=PARTITION_COLS,
)

ctx.register_json(
    "events_json",
    "warehouse/events_json/",
    schema=events_schema,
    table_partition_cols=PARTITION_COLS,
)

ctx.register_listing_table(
    "events_listing",
    "warehouse/events_listing/",
    schema=events_schema,
    table_partition_cols=PARTITION_COLS,
)
```

## 10.15.3 Partition deployment rules

```text id="xs2y44"
Partition best practices:
  - define partition columns once as constants
  - reuse identical names/types across formats
  - match directory layout and query predicates
  - do not encode same semantic column with different types per source
  - document partition columns as virtual/source-derived columns
```

---

# 10.16 File extensions and compressed inputs

## 10.16.1 File-extension filtering

```python id="ji2n7r"
ctx.register_csv("events_csv", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".csv")
ctx.register_json("events_json", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".json")
ctx.register_parquet("events", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".parquet")
ctx.register_avro("events_avro", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".avro")
ctx.register_arrow("events_arrow", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".arrow")
ctx.register_listing_table("events_listing", "warehouse/events/", file_extension=".parquet")
```

File-extension parameters select files by extension on these APIs; the context reference documents this consistently for file-based read/register methods. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.16.2 Text compression

```python id="k0nql3"
ctx.register_csv(
    "events_csv_gz",
    "warehouse/events_csv_gz/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".gz",
    file_compression_type="gzip",
)

ctx.register_json(
    "events_json_gz",
    "warehouse/events_json_gz/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".gz",
    file_compression_type="gzip",
)
```

CSV and JSON registration expose `file_compression_type`; Parquet compression is handled internally by the Parquet reader and is not configured through a `file_compression_type` parameter on `register_parquet`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.16.3 Compression policy

```text id="efw1y8"
CSV/JSON:
  set file_extension to physical suffix
  set file_compression_type explicitly
  validate compressed input in tests

Parquet:
  no file_compression_type registration arg
  file compression handled by Parquet metadata/reader

Arrow IPC / Avro:
  no file_compression_type registration arg in current API
```

---

# 10.17 Table lifetime and scope

## 10.17.1 Session-scoped mutable catalog state

Registered tables and views live inside the `SessionContext` catalog state. The registered table can be referenced from SQL executed against the same context, as stated in the registration APIs. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="az4q83"
ctx = SessionContext()

ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

# Works in same context.
ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events").show()

ctx2 = SessionContext()

# ctx2 does not inherit ctx registrations.
# ctx2.sql("SELECT * FROM events").show()  # missing table
```

## 10.17.2 Deregistration

```python id="gj60nw"
ctx.deregister_table("events")
```

`deregister_table(name)` removes a table from the session. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 10.17.3 Lifetime policy

```text id="m8epxu"
Batch job:
  register at startup
  query
  context exits

Notebook:
  register ad hoc
  clear/recreate context when names drift

Service:
  one immutable bootstrap context only if safe
  otherwise context per request/session/tenant
  avoid per-request table leakage

Tests:
  fresh context per test
  register in fixture
  never rely on test order
```

---

# 10.18 Deployment archetypes

## 10.18.1 Production bootstrap registry

```python id="nwkjf3"
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
import pyarrow as pa
from datafusion import SessionContext


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceRegistry:
    events_path: str | Path
    users_path: str | Path


EVENTS_SCHEMA = pa.schema([
    ("event_id", pa.string()),
    ("user_id", pa.int64()),
    ("event_type", pa.string()),
    ("amount", pa.float64()),
    ("event_ts", pa.timestamp("us")),
])

USERS_SCHEMA = pa.schema([
    ("user_id", pa.int64()),
    ("country", pa.string()),
    ("signup_ts", pa.timestamp("us")),
])


def register_sources(ctx: SessionContext, sources: SourceRegistry) -> None:
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        sources.events_path,
        schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA,
        table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string())],
        parquet_pruning=True,
        file_extension=".parquet",
    )

    ctx.register_csv(
        "users",
        sources.users_path,
        schema=USERS_SCHEMA,
        has_header=True,
        file_extension=".csv",
    )
```

## 10.18.2 In-memory test registry

```python id="gl6hdb"
import pyarrow as pa
from datafusion import SessionContext

def test_context() -> SessionContext:
    ctx = SessionContext()

    events = pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({
        "event_id": ["e1", "e2"],
        "user_id": [1, 2],
        "amount": [10.0, 20.0],
    })

    ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[events]])
    return ctx
```

## 10.18.3 Provider-backed registry

```python id="b8z1kt"
def register_provider_sources(ctx: SessionContext, provider) -> None:
    ctx.register_table("external_source", provider)
```

Use provider registration for custom sources, Delta/Iceberg/provider-backed systems, or sources whose capabilities require more than file-format registration. Custom table providers are integrated through Rust `TableProvider` exposed via PyCapsule in current docs. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

# 10.19 Read/register compatibility helper

```python id="i7n0m0"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import pyarrow as pa
from datafusion import SessionContext


SourceKind = Literal["csv", "json", "parquet", "avro", "arrow"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceSpec:
    kind: SourceKind
    name: str
    path: str | Path
    schema: pa.Schema | None = None
    file_extension: str | None = None
    compression: str | None = None
    partition_cols: list[tuple[str, pa.DataType]] | None = None


def register_source(ctx: SessionContext, spec: SourceSpec) -> None:
    if spec.kind == "csv":
        ctx.register_csv(
            spec.name,
            spec.path,
            schema=spec.schema,
            file_extension=spec.file_extension or ".csv",
            file_compression_type=spec.compression,
        )
        return

    if spec.kind == "json":
        ctx.register_json(
            spec.name,
            spec.path,
            schema=spec.schema,
            file_extension=spec.file_extension or ".json",
            table_partition_cols=spec.partition_cols,
            file_compression_type=spec.compression,
        )
        return

    if spec.kind == "parquet":
        ctx.register_parquet(
            spec.name,
            spec.path,
            schema=spec.schema,
            file_extension=spec.file_extension or ".parquet",
            table_partition_cols=spec.partition_cols,
            parquet_pruning=True,
            skip_metadata=True,
        )
        return

    if spec.kind == "avro":
        ctx.register_avro(
            spec.name,
            spec.path,
            schema=spec.schema,
            file_extension=spec.file_extension or ".avro",
            table_partition_cols=spec.partition_cols,
        )
        return

    if spec.kind == "arrow":
        ctx.register_arrow(
            spec.name,
            spec.path,
            schema=spec.schema,
            file_extension=spec.file_extension or ".arrow",
            table_partition_cols=spec.partition_cols,
        )
        return

    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported source kind: {spec.kind}")
```

---

# 10.20 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: schema inference in production CSV

```python id="qb7qkd"
ctx.register_csv("events", "warehouse/events/")
```

Correct:

```python id="u3ykyj"
ctx.register_csv("events", "warehouse/events/", schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA)
```

CSV schema inference reads sample data and headerless files get default column names; that is acceptable for exploration, not stable production contracts. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: registration inside transformation helper

```python id="ktcaax"
def build_report(ctx):
    ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")
    return ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events")
```

Correct:

```python id="9vpm2k"
def register_sources(ctx):
    ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

def build_report(ctx):
    return ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events")
```

---

## Anti-pattern: inconsistent partition columns across formats

```python id="0ib2d2"
ctx.register_parquet("events_pq", "events_pq/", table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string())])
ctx.register_json("events_json", "events_json/", table_partition_cols=[("date", pa.date32())])
```

Correct:

```python id="l70au6"
PARTITIONS = [("dt", pa.string())]

ctx.register_parquet("events_pq", "events_pq/", table_partition_cols=PARTITIONS)
ctx.register_json("events_json", "events_json/", schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA, table_partition_cols=PARTITIONS)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: deprecated registration API

```python id="f0h88w"
ctx.register_table_provider("source", provider)
```

Correct:

```python id="tgt110"
ctx.register_table("source", provider)
```

`register_table_provider(...)` is documented as deprecated in favor of `register_table(...)`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: unbounded table lifetime in global context

```python id="dceye2"
ctx = SessionContext.global_ctx()
ctx.register_record_batches("tmp", [[batch]])
```

Correct:

```python id="kdvwmt"
ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_record_batches("tmp", [[batch]])
```

Use explicit contexts for table lifetime control, tenant isolation, and reproducible tests.

---

# 10.21 Test matrix

## 10.21.1 Registration visibility

```python id="s3mntx"
def test_registered_table_visible(ctx):
    ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[make_events_batch()]])

    assert ctx.table_exist("events")

    out = ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events").to_pydict()

    assert out["n"][0] > 0
```

## 10.21.2 Schema contract

```python id="wbiq0r"
def test_schema_contract(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.csv"
    write_csv(path)

    ctx.register_csv(
        "events",
        path,
        schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA,
        has_header=True,
    )

    assert ctx.table("events").schema() == EVENTS_SCHEMA
```

## 10.21.3 Partition-column presence

```python id="zluzp5"
def test_partition_columns(ctx):
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "tests/data/events_partitioned/",
        table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string())],
    )

    assert "dt" in ctx.table("events").schema().names
```

## 10.21.4 Compressed text registration

```python id="219jgn"
def test_gzip_csv(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.csv.gz"
    write_gzip_csv(path)

    ctx.register_csv(
        "events",
        path,
        schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA,
        file_extension=".gz",
        file_compression_type="gzip",
    )

    assert ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events").to_pydict()["n"][0] > 0
```

# 10.22 Deployment checklist

```text id="zkolyz"
Registration:
  [ ] Register reusable datasets as tables.
  [ ] Keep registration in bootstrap/setup layer.
  [ ] Use ctx.table("name") or SQL after registration.
  [ ] Avoid register side effects in pure transformation helpers.

Schemas:
  [ ] Prefer explicit pyarrow.Schema in production.
  [ ] Avoid CSV/JSON schema inference except exploration/tests.
  [ ] Use schema assertions in CI.
  [ ] Override Parquet schema for mixed-writer directories.

Partitions:
  [ ] Define partition columns once.
  [ ] Reuse names/types across CSV/JSON/Parquet/listing tables.
  [ ] Match partition columns to directory layout and query predicates.

Files:
  [ ] Set file_extension for directory scans.
  [ ] Set file_compression_type for CSV/JSON compressed inputs.
  [ ] Keep parquet_pruning=True for Parquet.
  [ ] Use skip_metadata=True for Parquet metadata conflict avoidance.

Table lifetime:
  [ ] Use explicit SessionContext.
  [ ] Fresh context per test.
  [ ] Tenant/session context for isolation.
  [ ] Deregister temporary tables when reusing long-lived contexts.

Providers:
  [ ] Use register_table for custom providers.
  [ ] Avoid deprecated register_table_provider.
  [ ] Use Rust TableProvider for hot/custom sources.
  [ ] Use register_dataset when PyArrow owns discovery.
```

---

## 10.23 Section compression for LLM agents

```text id="p72103"
read_*:
  returns DataFrame
  no table name
  no catalog mutation

register_*:
  returns None
  mutates SessionContext catalog
  table becomes ctx.table("name") and SQL-visible

APIs:
  register_csv(name, path, schema=None, has_header=True, delimiter=",",
               schema_infer_max_records=..., file_extension=".csv",
               file_compression_type=None, options=None)

  register_parquet(name, path, table_partition_cols=None,
                   parquet_pruning=True, file_extension=".parquet",
                   skip_metadata=True, schema=None, file_sort_order=None)

  register_json(name, path, schema=None, schema_infer_max_records=1000,
                file_extension=".json", table_partition_cols=None,
                file_compression_type=None)

  register_avro(name, path, schema=None, file_extension=".avro",
                table_partition_cols=None)

  register_arrow(name, path, schema=None, file_extension=".arrow",
                 table_partition_cols=None)

  register_dataset(name, pyarrow.dataset.Dataset)
  register_record_batches(name, list[list[pyarrow.RecordBatch]])
  register_batch(name, pyarrow.RecordBatch)
  register_table(name, Table | provider | DataFrame | pyarrow.dataset.Dataset)
  register_view(name, DataFrame)
  register_listing_table(name, path, table_partition_cols=None,
                         file_extension=".parquet", schema=None,
                         file_sort_order=None)

Best defaults:
  reusable source -> register_*
  one-off source -> read_*
  production schema -> explicit pyarrow.Schema
  text compression -> file_compression_type
  directory scan -> file_extension
  partitioned data -> table_partition_cols
  Parquet -> parquet_pruning=True
  custom provider -> register_table
  tests -> register_record_batches
  derived logical relation -> register_view
```

[1]: https://pypi.org/project/datafusion/ "datafusion · PyPI"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html "datafusion.context — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/io/parquet.html "Parquet — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"

# DataFusion Advanced — 11) IO deep dive: Arrow, CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet

This section follows the dense, agent-facing advanced-reference style used in the Cyclopts source material. 

## 11.0 Version anchor

Current PyPI anchor: **`datafusion==54.0.0`**, released **June 29, 2026**, requiring **Python >=3.10**. PyPI describes DataFusion Python as bindings to Apache Arrow’s in-memory DataFusion query engine, with SQL/DataFrame execution over CSV, Parquet, and JSON sources, optimizer-backed queries, Python UDF support, PyArrow/Pandas-compatible exchange, and Substrait plan serialization. ([PyPI][1])

```bash
python -m pip install "datafusion==54.0.0"
```

```python
import datafusion
assert datafusion.__version__ == "54.0.0"
```

---

## 11.1 IO invariant: anonymous reads, registered sources, streaming exports, terminal writes

```text
IO surfaces:
  Arrow import/export:
    ctx.from_arrow(...)
    df.__arrow_c_stream__(...)
    pa.table(df)
    pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)

  File reads:
    ctx.read_csv(...)
    ctx.read_json(...)
    ctx.read_avro(...)
    ctx.read_arrow(...)
    ctx.read_parquet(...)

  File registration:
    ctx.register_csv(...)
    ctx.register_json(...)
    ctx.register_avro(...)
    ctx.register_arrow(...)
    ctx.register_parquet(...)

  File writes:
    df.write_csv(...)
    df.write_json(...)
    df.write_parquet(...)
    df.write_parquet_with_options(...)
```

`read_*` methods return anonymous lazy `DataFrame` objects; `register_*` methods register named tables in the `SessionContext`; write methods execute the DataFrame and write results to files. The API docs state `write_csv`, `write_json`, and `write_parquet` execute the DataFrame, while context methods such as `read_csv`, `read_json`, `read_avro`, `read_arrow`, and `read_parquet` create DataFrames from sources. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

# 11.2 Arrow import/export

## 11.2.1 `ctx.from_arrow(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.from_arrow(
    data: ArrowStreamExportable | ArrowArrayExportable,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`from_arrow(...)` creates a DataFrame from any Arrow source implementing `__arrow_c_stream__` or `__arrow_c_array__`; if the source implements `__arrow_c_array__`, it must return a struct array. The docs name common sources such as PyArrow, Polars, and Pandas-compatible Arrow objects. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
import pyarrow as pa
from datafusion import SessionContext

ctx = SessionContext()

table = pa.table({
    "user_id": [1, 2, 3],
    "amount": [10.0, 20.5, 30.0],
})

df = ctx.from_arrow(table)
```

### Accepted Arrow-style sources

```text
from_arrow accepts:
  pyarrow.Table
  pyarrow.RecordBatch
  pyarrow.RecordBatchReader
  Arrow-compatible object with __arrow_c_stream__
  Arrow-compatible object with __arrow_c_array__ returning StructArray
```

The Arrow IO guide explicitly lists PyArrow Array, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, and Table as common import sources, with the caveat that Array input must return a struct array. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent value case

```text
Use from_arrow when:
  upstream already has Arrow memory
  schema is already Arrow-native
  Python object conversion should be avoided
  interop boundary is PyArrow / Polars / Pandas Arrow-backed
  source object exposes Arrow PyCapsule interface
```

---

## 11.2.2 Arrow C Data Interface / PyCapsule interface

DataFusion implements the Apache Arrow PyCapsule interface for importing and exporting DataFrames with zero-copy exchange where supported by the consumer/producer. The docs state that any Python project implementing this interface can share data with DataFusion with zero copy. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

```text
Producer side:
  object.__arrow_c_stream__() -> ArrowArrayStream PyCapsule
  object.__arrow_c_array__()  -> ArrowArray / ArrowSchema PyCapsule pair

DataFusion import:
  ctx.from_arrow(object)

DataFusion export:
  df.__arrow_c_stream__()
```

---

## 11.2.3 `df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None)`

### Signature

```python
df.__arrow_c_stream__(
    requested_schema: object | None = None,
) -> object
```

`DataFrame.__arrow_c_stream__()` exports a DataFrame as an Arrow C Stream. DataFusion executes the underlying query using streaming APIs and exposes `RecordBatch` output incrementally, so the full result set is not materialized in memory. If `requested_schema` is supplied, DataFusion supports simple projections such as selecting/reordering existing columns; it does not support column renaming, computed expressions, or type coercion through that interface. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
import pyarrow as pa

reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)

for batch in reader:
    # batch is pyarrow.RecordBatch
    process(batch)
```

```python
table = pa.table(df)  # triggers execution through Arrow stream interface
```

The Arrow IO guide states that invoking `__arrow_c_stream__` triggers execution, yields batches incrementally rather than materializing the whole result, and lets downstream readers pull batches on demand. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

### Agent rules

```text
Arrow export defaults:
  - prefer Arrow stream for large outputs
  - do not collect() before passing to Arrow-aware consumers
  - use requested_schema only for projection/reordering
  - do computed expressions before export via df.select(...)
  - use pa.table(df) only when full Arrow Table materialization is acceptable
```

---

# 11.3 Arrow IPC files

## 11.3.1 `ctx.read_arrow(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.read_arrow(
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".arrow",
    file_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`read_arrow(...)` creates a DataFrame for an Arrow IPC source and supports path, schema override, file-extension filtering, and partition columns. The docs show reading a `.arrow` IPC file, overriding schema, and using `file_extension=".ipc"` for non-default extensions. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
df = ctx.read_arrow("events.arrow")
```

```python
df = ctx.read_arrow(
    "events.ipc",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".ipc",
)
```

## 11.3.2 `ctx.register_arrow(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.register_arrow(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".arrow",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_arrow(...)` registers an Arrow IPC file as a SQL-referenceable table; the API examples show schema override and non-default extension handling for `.ipc`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
ctx.register_arrow(
    "events_arrow",
    "events.ipc",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".ipc",
)

df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events_arrow")
```

### Arrow IPC deployment rules

```text
Arrow IPC:
  - use read_arrow for anonymous one-off file scans
  - use register_arrow for SQL-visible table names
  - use schema override when producer metadata/schema must be normalized
  - use file_extension for non-.arrow suffixes such as .ipc
  - use from_arrow for in-memory Arrow objects; use read_arrow for persisted IPC files
```

---

# 11.4 CSV IO

## 11.4.1 `ctx.read_csv(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.read_csv(
    path: str | Path | list[str] | list[Path],
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    has_header: bool = True,
    delimiter: str = ",",
    schema_infer_max_records: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INFER_SCHEMA,
    file_extension: str = ".csv",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
    options: CsvReadOptions | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`read_csv(...)` reads one or more CSV files into an anonymous DataFrame. If `schema=None`, DataFusion tries to infer the schema from file data; if schema inference runs on a file without headers, default column names are created. The method supports header configuration, delimiter, inference row limit, file-extension filtering, partition columns, compression type, and `CsvReadOptions`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
df = ctx.read_csv(
    "events.csv",
    schema=events_schema,
    has_header=True,
    delimiter=",",
)
```

## 11.4.2 `ctx.register_csv(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.register_csv(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path | list[str | Path],
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    has_header: bool = True,
    delimiter: str = ",",
    schema_infer_max_records: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INFER_SCHEMA,
    file_extension: str = ".csv",
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
    options: CsvReadOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

The CSV user guide shows two equivalent ingestion paths: `ctx.read_csv("file.csv")` for a DataFrame, and `ctx.register_csv("file", "file.csv"); ctx.table("file")` for registered-table access. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

```python
ctx.register_csv(
    "events_csv",
    "events.csv",
    schema=events_schema,
    has_header=True,
)

df = ctx.table("events_csv")
```

---

## 11.4.3 `CsvReadOptions`

### Constructor

```python
CsvReadOptions(
    *,
    has_header: bool = True,
    delimiter: str = ",",
    quote: str = '"',
    terminator: str | None = None,
    escape: str | None = None,
    comment: str | None = None,
    newlines_in_values: bool = False,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    schema_infer_max_records: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INFER_SCHEMA,
    file_extension: str = ".csv",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_compression_type: str = "",
    file_sort_order: list[list[SortExpr]] | None = None,
    null_regex: str | None = None,
    truncated_rows: bool = False,
)
```

`CsvReadOptions` is a builder-style configuration object; all `with_*` methods return `self` for chaining. It controls header handling, delimiter, quote, terminator, escape, comments, multiline quoted values, schema, schema inference row count, extension filtering, partition columns, compression, file sort order, null regex, and truncated-row behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

```python
from datafusion import CsvReadOptions

options = (
    CsvReadOptions()
    .with_schema(events_schema)
    .with_has_header(True)
    .with_delimiter(";")
    .with_quote('"')
    .with_escape("\\")
    .with_comment("#")
    .with_null_regex(r"^(null|NULL|N/A)$")
    .with_truncated_rows(True)
    .with_file_compression_type("gzip")
    .with_file_extension(".gz")
)

df = ctx.read_csv("events.csv.gz", options=options)
```

The CSV guide shows this same `CsvReadOptions` pattern for headers, delimiter, comments, escape, null regex, truncated rows, gzip compression, and extension handling. ([Apache DataFusion][5])

---

## 11.4.4 CSV option semantics

```text
Header:
  has_header=True
  has_header=False -> schema inference creates default column names if no explicit schema

Delimiter:
  delimiter must be single ASCII character

Quote:
  quote must be single ASCII character

Terminator:
  terminator=None uses CRLF behavior
  terminator must be single ASCII character if set

Escape:
  escape must be single ASCII character if set

Comment:
  comment lines begin with the configured single ASCII character

Newlines in values:
  newlines_in_values=True supports quoted multiline values but may reduce performance

Null regex:
  null_regex matches values treated as NULL

Truncated rows:
  truncated_rows=True allows rows with fewer columns and fills missing values with nulls
  still errors if target schema field is non-nullable

Compression:
  supported CSV compression values:
    "gzip", "bz2", "xz", "zstd", "" for uncompressed

Extension:
  file_extension selects files by suffix in directory/listing scans
```

These semantics are documented in the `CsvReadOptions` parameter reference, including the performance note for `newlines_in_values`, supported compression values, and truncated-row behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][6])

---

## 11.4.5 CSV deployment advisory

```text
CSV exploration:
  schema=None acceptable
  schema_infer_max_records acceptable
  limit().show() before assumptions

CSV production:
  explicit pyarrow.Schema
  explicit has_header
  explicit delimiter
  explicit null_regex
  explicit file_extension
  explicit file_compression_type for compressed input
  CsvReadOptions for quote/escape/comment/newline/truncated-row control
  avoid schema inference in multi-file feeds
```

---

# 11.5 JSON IO

## 11.5.1 `ctx.read_json(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.read_json(
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    schema_infer_max_records: int = 1000,
    file_extension: str = ".json",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`read_json(...)` reads **line-delimited JSON** and returns a DataFrame. It supports schema override, schema-inference row limit, extension filtering, partition columns, and compression type. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
df = ctx.read_json(
    "events.json",
    schema=events_schema,
    schema_infer_max_records=10_000,
)
```

```python
df = ctx.read_json(
    "events.json.gz",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_extension=".gz",
    file_compression_type="gzip",
)
```

## 11.5.2 `ctx.register_json(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.register_json(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    schema_infer_max_records: int = 1000,
    file_extension: str = ".json",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_compression_type: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_json(...)` registers a JSON file as a table that can be referenced by SQL executed against the same context; it supports schema, inference row limit, file-extension filtering, partition columns, and compression. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
ctx.register_json(
    "events_json",
    "events.json",
    schema=events_schema,
)

df = ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events_json")
```

## 11.5.3 JSON deployment advisory

```text
JSON input contract:
  - DataFusion JSON reader expects line-delimited JSON
  - not arbitrary top-level JSON arrays
  - schema inference is available but should be exploration-only
  - compression requires file_compression_type
  - compressed directory scans require matching file_extension

Production defaults:
  - explicit schema
  - explicit file_extension
  - explicit file_compression_type for gzip/bz2/xz/zstd-style text feeds where supported
  - convert stable high-volume JSON feeds to Parquet for analytical storage
```

---

# 11.6 Avro IO

## 11.6.1 `ctx.read_avro(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.read_avro(
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".avro",
) -> DataFrame
```

`read_avro(...)` creates a DataFrame for an Avro data source and supports path, optional schema, partition columns, and file-extension selection. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
df = ctx.read_avro(
    "events.avro",
    schema=events_schema,
)
```

```python
df = ctx.read_avro(
    "warehouse/events_avro/",
    schema=events_schema,
    file_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string())],
    file_extension=".avro",
)
```

## 11.6.2 `ctx.register_avro(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.register_avro(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_extension: str = ".avro",
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_avro(...)` registers an Avro file as a table that SQL can reference in the same context. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
ctx.register_avro(
    "events_avro",
    "events.avro",
    schema=events_schema,
)

df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events_avro")
```

## 11.6.3 Avro deployment advisory

```text
Avro:
  - use when upstream source system emits Avro
  - provide explicit schema when cross-file consistency matters
  - use file_extension for directory scans
  - use partition columns consistently with other formats
  - prefer Parquet for stable analytical lakehouse-style storage when possible
```

# 11.7 Parquet read/register IO

## 11.7.1 `ctx.read_parquet(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.read_parquet(
    path: str | Path,
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    parquet_pruning: bool = True,
    file_extension: str = ".parquet",
    skip_metadata: bool = True,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_sort_order: Sequence[Sequence[SortKey]] | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`read_parquet(...)` reads a Parquet source into a DataFrame and supports partition columns, predicate row-group pruning, extension filtering, metadata skipping, schema override, and file sort order. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
df = ctx.read_parquet(
    "warehouse/events/",
    table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string())],
    parquet_pruning=True,
    file_extension=".parquet",
    skip_metadata=True,
    schema=events_schema,
)
```

The Parquet guide shows the simple direct-read path `ctx.read_parquet("file.parquet")`. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

---

## 11.7.2 `ctx.register_parquet(...)`

### Signature

```python
ctx.register_parquet(
    name: str,
    path: str | Path,
    table_partition_cols: list[tuple[str, str | pyarrow.DataType]] | None = None,
    parquet_pruning: bool = True,
    file_extension: str = ".parquet",
    skip_metadata: bool = True,
    schema: pyarrow.Schema | None = None,
    file_sort_order: Sequence[Sequence[SortKey]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

`register_parquet(...)` registers a Parquet source as a SQL-visible table. The Parquet guide shows `ctx.register_parquet("file", "file.parquet"); df = ctx.table("file")` as the registered-table alternative to direct reading. ([Apache DataFusion][7])

```python
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "warehouse/events/",
    table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string()), ("region", pa.string())],
    parquet_pruning=True,
    file_extension=".parquet",
    skip_metadata=True,
    schema=events_schema,
)

df = ctx.sql("""
    SELECT region, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    WHERE dt >= '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY region
""")
```

---

## 11.7.3 Row-group pruning

```python
ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "warehouse/events/",
    parquet_pruning=True,
)
```

`parquet_pruning=True` enables predicate-based row-group pruning for Parquet reads/registers. Keep it enabled for production unless debugging or comparing scan behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```text
Parquet pruning value case:
  fewer row groups scanned
  lower I/O
  lower CPU
  better predicate-heavy analytical query performance
```

---

## 11.7.4 Metadata handling: `skip_metadata`

```python
df = ctx.read_parquet(
    "warehouse/events/",
    skip_metadata=True,
)
```

`skip_metadata=True` is documented as an option on Parquet read/register APIs and is intended to avoid schema conflicts due to schema metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```text
skip_metadata=True:
  useful for mixed-writer Parquet datasets
  avoids metadata-level schema conflict
  does not replace explicit schema governance
```

---

## 11.7.5 File sort order

```python
from datafusion import col

df = ctx.read_parquet(
    "warehouse/events_sorted/",
    file_sort_order=[
        [col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True, nulls_first=False)]
    ],
)
```

`file_sort_order` accepts a nested sequence of sort keys, and each sort key can be a column-name string, an `Expr`, or a `SortExpr`. The context API documents the conversion helper and parameter shape for sort-order metadata. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```text
file_sort_order:
  - metadata contract supplied by caller
  - only use when upstream files truly guarantee sort order
  - invalid sort metadata can produce incorrect optimizer assumptions
```

---

## 11.7.6 Parquet read/register deployment advisory

```text
Parquet defaults:
  - prefer Parquet for analytical lake/storage
  - keep parquet_pruning=True
  - use explicit schema for mixed-writer directories
  - set partition columns for directory partitioning
  - keep file_extension=".parquet" unless suffix differs
  - use skip_metadata=True for metadata-conflict-prone inputs
  - declare file_sort_order only when guaranteed
```

---

# 11.8 Parquet writing

## 11.8.1 `df.write_parquet(...)`

### Signature family

```python
df.write_parquet(
    path: str | Path,
    compression: str | Compression = Compression.ZSTD,
    compression_level: int | None = None,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_parquet(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes the result to Parquet. Supported compression names are `uncompressed`, `snappy`, `gzip`, `brotli`, `lz4`, `lz4_raw`, and `zstd`; LZO is explicitly excluded because it is not yet implemented in arrow-rs. The default compression is ZSTD, and for ZSTD the documented recommended compression-level range is 1–22 with default 4. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
df.write_parquet(
    "output/events.parquet",
    compression="zstd",
    compression_level=4,
)
```

```python
df.write_parquet(
    "output/events.snappy.parquet",
    compression="snappy",
)
```

---

## 11.8.2 `df.write_parquet_with_options(...)`

### Signature

```python
df.write_parquet_with_options(
    path: str | Path,
    options: ParquetWriterOptions,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_parquet_with_options(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes Parquet using advanced `ParquetWriterOptions`; the docs describe it as the advanced-writer-options entrypoint. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
from datafusion.dataframe import ParquetWriterOptions

options = ParquetWriterOptions(
    compression="zstd(6)",
    writer_version="2.0",
    max_row_group_size=1_000_000,
    statistics_enabled="page",
    dictionary_enabled=True,
)

df.write_parquet_with_options(
    "output/events.parquet",
    options=options,
)
```

---

## 11.8.3 `ParquetWriterOptions`

### Constructor

```python
ParquetWriterOptions(
    data_pagesize_limit: int = 1024 * 1024,
    write_batch_size: int = 1024,
    writer_version: str = "1.0",
    skip_arrow_metadata: bool = False,
    compression: str | None = "zstd(3)",
    compression_level: int | None = None,
    dictionary_enabled: bool | None = True,
    dictionary_page_size_limit: int = 1024 * 1024,
    statistics_enabled: str | None = "page",
    max_row_group_size: int = 1024 * 1024,
    created_by: str = "datafusion-python",
    column_index_truncate_length: int | None = 64,
    statistics_truncate_length: int | None = None,
    data_page_row_count_limit: int = 20000,
    encoding: str | None = None,
    bloom_filter_on_write: bool = False,
    bloom_filter_fpp: float | None = None,
    bloom_filter_ndv: int | None = None,
    allow_single_file_parallelism: bool = True,
    maximum_parallel_row_group_writers: int = 1,
    maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream: int = 2,
    column_specific_options: dict[str, ParquetColumnOptions] | None = None,
)
```

`ParquetWriterOptions` controls file-level Parquet writer behavior: data page size, batch size, writer version, Arrow metadata, compression, dictionary encoding, dictionary page size, statistics, row-group size, created-by metadata, index/statistics truncation, data-page row count, encoding, bloom filters, parallel writer behavior, buffering, and column-specific overrides. The docs note that larger row groups require more memory but can improve compression and read speed. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 11.8.4 `ParquetColumnOptions`

### Constructor

```python
ParquetColumnOptions(
    encoding: str | None = None,
    dictionary_enabled: bool | None = None,
    compression: str | None = None,
    statistics_enabled: str | None = None,
    bloom_filter_enabled: bool | None = None,
    bloom_filter_fpp: float | None = None,
    bloom_filter_ndv: int | None = None,
)
```

`ParquetColumnOptions` overrides global Parquet writer options per column. Valid encodings include `plain`, `plain_dictionary`, `rle`, `bit_packed`, `delta_binary_packed`, `delta_length_byte_array`, `delta_byte_array`, `rle_dictionary`, and `byte_stream_split`; per-column compression supports values like `uncompressed`, `snappy`, `gzip(level)`, `brotli(level)`, `lz4`, `zstd(level)`, and `lz4_raw`; statistics settings include `none`, `chunk`, and `page`. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
from datafusion.dataframe import ParquetColumnOptions, ParquetWriterOptions

options = ParquetWriterOptions(
    compression="zstd(4)",
    column_specific_options={
        "event_type": ParquetColumnOptions(
            dictionary_enabled=True,
            statistics_enabled="page",
        ),
        "payload": ParquetColumnOptions(
            compression="zstd(9)",
            dictionary_enabled=False,
        ),
    },
)

df.write_parquet_with_options("output/events.parquet", options)
```

---

## 11.8.5 `DataFrameWriteOptions`

### Constructor

```python
DataFrameWriteOptions(
    insert_operation: InsertOp | None = None,
    single_file_output: bool = False,
    partition_by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    sort_by: Expr | SortExpr | Sequence[Expr] | Sequence[SortExpr] | None = None,
)
```

`DataFrameWriteOptions` controls DataFrame writing behavior, including insert operation, single-file output, partitioning, and sorting. The docs warn there is no guarantee every table provider supports every writer option. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
from datafusion.dataframe import DataFrameWriteOptions

write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    single_file_output=False,
    partition_by=["dt", "region"],
    sort_by=[col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True)],
)

df.write_parquet(
    "output/events/",
    compression="zstd",
    compression_level=4,
    write_options=write_options,
)
```

`InsertOp` supports `APPEND`, `OVERWRITE`, and `REPLACE` modes for table writing. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## 11.8.6 Parquet write deployment advisory

```text
Parquet writer defaults:
  - use zstd for balanced compression/performance unless downstream requires another codec
  - set compression level deliberately
  - set max_row_group_size based on memory and read-pattern tradeoffs
  - keep statistics enabled for predicate pruning usefulness
  - use dictionary encoding for low-cardinality columns
  - use column_specific_options for payload/high-cardinality exceptions
  - use partition_by for lake-style output layout
  - use single_file_output only for bounded outputs or interoperability demands
  - tune parallel writer knobs only when memory budget allows
```

---

# 11.9 CSV / JSON writing

## 11.9.1 `df.write_csv(...)`

### Signature

```python
df.write_csv(
    path: str | Path,
    with_header: bool = False,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_csv(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes results to a CSV file; `with_header=True` writes the header row, and `write_options` controls DataFrame write behavior. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
df.write_csv(
    "output/events.csv",
    with_header=True,
)
```

## 11.9.2 `df.write_json(...)`

### Signature

```python
df.write_json(
    path: str | Path,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_json(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes results to a JSON file. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

```python
df.write_json("output/events.json")
```

### Agent rules

```text
CSV/JSON writes:
  - terminal execution
  - prefer Parquet for analytical pipelines
  - use CSV for human/tool interoperability
  - use JSON for line-oriented interchange
  - use DataFrameWriteOptions for partitioning/single-file/sort behavior where supported
```

---

# 11.10 IO strategy matrix

| Need                             | Recommended IO path                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory Arrow object           | `ctx.from_arrow(obj)`                                               |
| Arrow-aware downstream consumer  | `pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)` or `pa.table(df)` if bounded |
| One-off CSV scan                 | `ctx.read_csv(...)`                                                 |
| SQL-visible CSV table            | `ctx.register_csv(...)`                                             |
| One-off line-delimited JSON scan | `ctx.read_json(...)`                                                |
| SQL-visible JSON table           | `ctx.register_json(...)`                                            |
| Avro source                      | `ctx.read_avro(...)` / `ctx.register_avro(...)`                     |
| Arrow IPC file                   | `ctx.read_arrow(...)` / `ctx.register_arrow(...)`                   |
| Analytical lake file             | `ctx.read_parquet(...)` / `ctx.register_parquet(...)`               |
| Multi-file object-store table    | `ctx.register_listing_table(...)`                                   |
| Parquet output                   | `df.write_parquet(...)` or `write_parquet_with_options(...)`        |
| Large output to Arrow consumer   | `df.__arrow_c_stream__` / `RecordBatchReader`                       |
| Human-readable output            | bounded `write_csv(..., with_header=True)`                          |
| Test fixture                     | `ctx.from_arrow(...)` or `ctx.register_record_batches(...)`         |

---

# 11.11 Format-specific deployment defaults

## Arrow

```text
Import:
  ctx.from_arrow(table_or_batch_or_reader)

Export:
  Arrow C stream
  pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
  pa.table(df) only when full materialization is acceptable

Default:
  best interop boundary for Arrow-native systems
```

## CSV

```text
Read:
  explicit schema
  explicit delimiter/header
  CsvReadOptions for quote/escape/comment/null/truncated-row handling
  explicit compression and extension

Default:
  ingestion/interchange only, not preferred analytical storage
```

## JSON

```text
Read:
  line-delimited JSON
  explicit schema
  explicit compression/extension
  inference only for exploration

Default:
  source/interchange format; convert stable feeds to Parquet
```

## Avro

```text
Read:
  use when upstream emits Avro
  explicit schema where consistency matters
  partition columns for directory sources

Default:
  source-system compatibility format
```

## Parquet

```text
Read:
  parquet_pruning=True
  explicit schema for heterogeneous datasets
  table_partition_cols for directory partitioning
  skip_metadata=True when metadata conflicts appear
  file_sort_order only when guaranteed

Write:
  zstd default
  statistics enabled
  row group sizing tuned to memory/read pattern
  partition_by for lake layout
  column options for high-cardinality/payload fields
```

---

# 11.12 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: collecting before Arrow export

```python
batches = df.collect()
table = pa.Table.from_batches(batches)
```

Correct:

```python
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
```

DataFusion’s Arrow stream export produces batches incrementally and avoids full result materialization. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

## Anti-pattern: CSV schema inference in production

```python
df = ctx.read_csv("warehouse/events/")
```

Correct:

```python
df = ctx.read_csv(
    "warehouse/events/",
    schema=events_schema,
    options=CsvReadOptions()
        .with_schema(events_schema)
        .with_has_header(True)
        .with_null_regex(r"^(null|NULL|N/A)$"),
)
```

CSV schema inference is available, but the API states it samples file data and creates default column names for headerless inference. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: assuming JSON reader accepts arbitrary JSON documents

```python
df = ctx.read_json("records-array.json")
```

Correct contract:

```text
DataFusion read_json expects line-delimited JSON.
```

`read_json(...)` is documented as reading a line-delimited JSON data source. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: disabling Parquet pruning by default

```python
df = ctx.read_parquet("events.parquet", parquet_pruning=False)
```

Correct:

```python
df = ctx.read_parquet("events.parquet", parquet_pruning=True)
```

`parquet_pruning` is a first-class read/register parameter for Parquet and defaults to `True`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: declaring file sort order without guarantee

```python
df = ctx.read_parquet(
    "events/",
    file_sort_order=[[col("event_ts").sort()]],
)
```

Correct:

```text
Only declare file_sort_order if upstream files are physically sorted by that key.
```

`file_sort_order` supplies sort metadata to DataFusion; invalid metadata is an application contract error. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## Anti-pattern: huge single-file Parquet output by default

```python
df.write_parquet(
    "events.parquet",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(single_file_output=True),
)
```

Correct:

```python
df.write_parquet(
    "events/",
    compression="zstd",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(
        partition_by=["dt"],
        single_file_output=False,
    ),
)
```

`DataFrameWriteOptions` exposes `single_file_output` and `partition_by`, and the docs note provider support may vary. ([Apache DataFusion][4])

---

# 11.13 Test harness patterns

## Arrow stream export test

```python
import pyarrow as pa

def test_arrow_stream_export(ctx):
    df = ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)

    batches = list(reader)

    assert sum(b.num_rows for b in batches) == 3
```

## CSV option test

```python
from datafusion import CsvReadOptions

def test_csv_gzip_with_nulls(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.csv.gz"
    write_gzip_csv(path)

    options = (
        CsvReadOptions()
        .with_schema(events_schema)
        .with_has_header(True)
        .with_null_regex(r"^(null|NULL|N/A)$")
        .with_file_compression_type("gzip")
        .with_file_extension(".gz")
    )

    df = ctx.read_csv(path, options=options)

    assert df.schema() == events_schema
```

## JSON line-delimited test

```python
def test_json_lines(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.json"
    path.write_text('{"x": 1}\n{"x": 2}\n')

    df = ctx.read_json(path)

    assert df.to_pydict() == {"x": [1, 2]}
```

## Parquet read/write roundtrip

```python
from datafusion.dataframe import ParquetWriterOptions

def test_parquet_roundtrip(ctx, tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    df = ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})

    df.write_parquet_with_options(
        out,
        ParquetWriterOptions(
            compression="zstd(3)",
            statistics_enabled="page",
            max_row_group_size=1024,
        ),
    )

    read_back = ctx.read_parquet(out)

    assert read_back.to_pydict() == {"x": [1, 2, 3]}
```

---

# 11.14 Deployment checklist

```text
Arrow:
  [ ] Use ctx.from_arrow for Arrow-native imports.
  [ ] Use Arrow C stream for large exports.
  [ ] Avoid collect() before Arrow consumers.
  [ ] Apply computed projections before __arrow_c_stream__.

CSV:
  [ ] Explicit pyarrow.Schema in production.
  [ ] CsvReadOptions for delimiter/header/quote/escape/comment/null/truncated-row policy.
  [ ] Explicit file_extension for directory/compressed scans.
  [ ] Explicit file_compression_type for compressed text input.
  [ ] Avoid inference for multi-file production feeds.

JSON:
  [ ] Validate line-delimited JSON contract.
  [ ] Explicit schema in production.
  [ ] Explicit compression/extension when compressed.
  [ ] Convert stable high-volume feeds to Parquet.

Avro:
  [ ] Use for Avro-native upstream systems.
  [ ] Provide schema if consistency matters.
  [ ] Use partition columns consistently.

Parquet:
  [ ] Keep parquet_pruning=True.
  [ ] Explicit schema for mixed-writer directories.
  [ ] table_partition_cols for partitioned paths.
  [ ] skip_metadata=True for metadata conflict avoidance.
  [ ] file_sort_order only with guaranteed sort.
  [ ] write with zstd unless interoperability requires otherwise.
  [ ] tune row group size with memory/read-pattern tradeoffs.
  [ ] enable statistics for pruning-friendly outputs.
  [ ] use column-specific options for special columns.
```

---

## 11.15 Section compression for LLM agents

```text
Arrow:
  ctx.from_arrow(data, name=None) -> DataFrame
  accepts __arrow_c_stream__ or __arrow_c_array__; array path must return StructArray
  df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None) -> ArrowArrayStream PyCapsule
  Arrow export executes lazily/incrementally; no full materialization

Arrow IPC:
  ctx.read_arrow(path, schema=None, file_extension=".arrow", file_partition_cols=None) -> DataFrame
  ctx.register_arrow(name, path, schema=None, file_extension=".arrow", table_partition_cols=None) -> None

CSV:
  ctx.read_csv(path, schema=None, has_header=True, delimiter=",",
               schema_infer_max_records=..., file_extension=".csv",
               table_partition_cols=None, file_compression_type=None,
               options=None) -> DataFrame

  ctx.register_csv(name, path, schema=None, has_header=True, delimiter=",",
                   schema_infer_max_records=..., file_extension=".csv",
                   file_compression_type=None, options=None) -> None

  CsvReadOptions:
    has_header delimiter quote terminator escape comment
    newlines_in_values schema schema_infer_max_records
    file_extension table_partition_cols file_compression_type
    file_sort_order null_regex truncated_rows

JSON:
  ctx.read_json(path, schema=None, schema_infer_max_records=1000,
                file_extension=".json", table_partition_cols=None,
                file_compression_type=None) -> DataFrame

  ctx.register_json(name, path, schema=None, schema_infer_max_records=1000,
                    file_extension=".json", table_partition_cols=None,
                    file_compression_type=None) -> None

  JSON is line-delimited.

Avro:
  ctx.read_avro(path, schema=None, file_partition_cols=None,
                file_extension=".avro") -> DataFrame

  ctx.register_avro(name, path, schema=None, file_extension=".avro",
                    table_partition_cols=None) -> None

Parquet read:
  ctx.read_parquet(path, table_partition_cols=None, parquet_pruning=True,
                   file_extension=".parquet", skip_metadata=True,
                   schema=None, file_sort_order=None) -> DataFrame

  ctx.register_parquet(name, path, table_partition_cols=None,
                       parquet_pruning=True, file_extension=".parquet",
                       skip_metadata=True, schema=None, file_sort_order=None) -> None

Parquet write:
  df.write_parquet(path, compression="zstd", compression_level=None,
                   write_options=None) -> None

  df.write_parquet_with_options(path, ParquetWriterOptions(...),
                                write_options=None) -> None

Writer options:
  DataFrameWriteOptions(insert_operation=None, single_file_output=False,
                        partition_by=None, sort_by=None)

  ParquetWriterOptions(compression="zstd(3)", dictionary_enabled=True,
                       statistics_enabled="page", max_row_group_size=1048576,
                       column_specific_options=None, ...)

Production defaults:
  Arrow stream for large exports
  explicit schemas for CSV/JSON
  line-delimited JSON only
  Parquet pruning enabled
  partition columns consistent across formats
  ZSTD Parquet output
  writer statistics enabled
  avoid materializing before Arrow consumers
```
