# 17.16 Query-plan debugging recipes

## 17.16.1 Predicate pushdown / scan pruning

```python id="2mp5vn"
df = (
    ctx.read_parquet("events/")
    .filter(col("event_ts") >= lit("2026-01-01"))
    .select("event_id", "event_ts", "amount")
)

print(df.optimized_logical_plan().display())
print(df.execution_plan().display_indent())
```

Check:

```text id="b0qd95"
projection lists only required columns
predicate appears near scan
Parquet scan shows predicate/pruning-related details
file_groups count is reasonable
```

DataFusion 54 release notes highlight dynamic filter pushdown, statistics propagation, and more work pushed into earlier/cheaper execution stages (continuing the pushdown investment of the 53 line), reinforcing that optimized plans should be inspected when performance changes across versions. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 17.16.2 Join diagnostics

```python id="tx6w4p"
joined = left.join(right, left_on="user_id", right_on="id", how="left")

joined.explain(format=ExplainFormat.TREE)
joined.explain(analyze=True)
```

Check:

```text id="0zqnp8"
join type
hash vs sort-merge
repartitioning
row counts from analyze
build/probe side if visible
filter placement before join
```

Relevant optimizer knobs include `join_reordering`, `prefer_hash_join`, `filter_null_join_keys`, and join dynamic filter pushdown; config docs describe those optimizer settings and their tradeoffs. ([Apache DataFusion][8])

---

## 17.16.3 Window top-N diagnostics

```python id="6ofhu8"
ranked = df.select(
    "*",
    f.row_number(
        partition_by=[col("group_id")],
        order_by=[col("score").sort(ascending=False)],
    ).alias("rn"),
).filter(col("rn") <= lit(10))

ranked.explain(analyze=True)
```

The config docs describe `datafusion.optimizer.enable_window_topn`, which can replace `Filter(rn<=K) → Window(ROW_NUMBER) → Sort` patterns with `PartitionedTopKExec`, but warn that high-cardinality partition keys may regress memory/runtime. ([Apache DataFusion][8])

---

# 17.17 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: treating `logical_plan()` as execution

```python id="3u0d4j"
plan = df.logical_plan()
# No query has run.
```

Correct mental model:

```text id="fdk17g"
logical_plan() returns plan metadata.
collect()/show()/execute_stream()/explain(analyze=True) execute.
```

---

## Anti-pattern: exact physical-plan snapshot across machines

```python id="e0yosm"
snapshot.assert_match(df.execution_plan().display_indent())
```

Correct:

```python id="xm5v31"
assert datafusion.__version__ == "54.0.0"
text = df.execution_plan().display_indent()
assert "DataSourceExec" in text or "Exec" in text
```

Physical plans are hardware/config/data-sensitive. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## Anti-pattern: `explain(analyze=True)` in normal request path

```python id="kgctbi"
def handle_request(sql):
    df = ctx.sql(sql)
    df.explain(analyze=True)
    return df.limit(100).to_pylist()
```

Correct:

```python id="v5m8he"
def handle_request(sql):
    df = ctx.sql(sql)
    return df.limit(100).to_pylist()
```

Enable runtime explain only in debug/performance mode.

---

## Anti-pattern: removing optimizer rules in production hot path

```python id="mbn1lz"
ctx.remove_optimizer_rule("some_rule")
```

Correct:

```python id="o12zu3"
if debug_config.remove_optimizer_rules:
    apply_optimizer_debug(ctx, debug_config)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: sharing raw explain output externally

```text id="psg3uo"
Raw explain may expose:
  paths
  object-store buckets
  table names
  literal predicates
  user identifiers
```

Correct:

```text id="e648sg"
sanitize:
  paths -> <PATH>
  buckets -> <BUCKET>
  literals -> <VALUE>
  table names -> aliases if sensitive
```

---

# 17.18 CI / upgrade workflow

```text id="zepc8b"
On DataFusion upgrade:
  1. pin new datafusion version in a branch
  2. run semantic query-output tests
  3. run coarse plan-shape tests
  4. diff optimized logical plan snapshots
  5. diff physical plan snapshots only for representative hardware/config
  6. run explain(analyze=True) benchmark fixtures
  7. update expected plan artifacts deliberately
  8. document optimizer-related behavior changes
```

Suggested artifact set:

```text id="7hdqpj"
artifacts/
  plans/
    optimized_logical/
      query_a_datafusion_53_0_0.txt
    physical/
      query_a_datafusion_53_0_0_linux_x86_64_target8.txt
    explain/
      query_a_tree_53_0_0.txt
  metrics/
    query_a_explain_analyze_summary_53_0_0.json_or_txt
```

---

# 17.19 Deployment checklist

```text id="u2v3ql"
Plan inspection:
  [ ] Use df.logical_plan() for unoptimized logical IR.
  [ ] Use df.optimized_logical_plan() for optimizer result.
  [ ] Use df.execution_plan() for physical operator tree.
  [ ] Use df.explain(...) for human-readable output.
  [ ] Use df.explain(analyze=True) only for performance diagnostics.

Explain formats:
  [ ] INDENT for logs/tests.
  [ ] TREE for human debugging.
  [ ] GRAPHVIZ for diagrams.
  [ ] PGJSON for visualization/tooling.

Metrics:
  [ ] analyze=True executes the query.
  [ ] Do not use analyze=True in read-only validation paths.
  [ ] Configure analyze_level/analyze_categories for performance reports.

Plan objects:
  [ ] display()/display_indent() for text.
  [ ] display_graphviz() for logical DOT output.
  [ ] inputs()/children() for traversal.
  [ ] partition_count for physical parallelism inspection.
  [ ] to_proto()/from_proto() only when catalogs/providers are compatible.

Optimizer:
  [ ] Tune optimizer config via SessionConfig when needed.
  [ ] Use remove_optimizer_rule(...) only in debug/test/benchmark.
  [ ] Record version/config/hardware with plan artifacts.

Testing:
  [ ] Prefer semantic output tests first.
  [ ] Use coarse plan-shape tests second.
  [ ] Exact plan snapshots only under version/config pinning.
  [ ] Treat physical-plan snapshots as environment-sensitive.
```

---

## 17.20 Section compression for LLM agents

```text id="m3648m"
DataFrame:
  thin wrapper over LogicalPlan
  transformations build logical plans
  terminal calls execute

Inspection:
  df.logical_plan() -> LogicalPlan
  df.optimized_logical_plan() -> LogicalPlan
  df.execution_plan() -> ExecutionPlan
  df.explain(verbose=False, analyze=False, format=None) -> None

Explain:
  analyze=False -> print plan only
  analyze=True  -> run query + report metrics
  verbose=True  -> more detail
  format:
    ExplainFormat.INDENT
    ExplainFormat.TREE
    ExplainFormat.GRAPHVIZ
    ExplainFormat.PGJSON

SQL:
  EXPLAIN [ANALYZE] [VERBOSE] [FORMAT format] statement

LogicalPlan:
  display()
  display_indent()
  display_indent_schema()
  display_graphviz()
  inputs()
  to_proto()
  from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  to_variant()
  __eq__

ExecutionPlan:
  display()
  display_indent()
  children()
  to_proto()
  from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  partition_count
  metrics() -> MetricsSet | None                    (54; per-instance — see 17.21)
  collect_metrics() -> [(description, MetricsSet)]  (54; whole tree)

Plan proto caveat:
  in-memory record-batch tables currently not supported

Context execution:
  ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan) -> DataFrame
  ctx.execute(execution_plan, partitions) -> RecordBatchStream

Optimizer:
  ctx.remove_optimizer_rule(name) -> bool
  config keys control join reorder, hash join preference, dynamic filters, window top-N, explain output

Best practices:
  use optimized plans for performance reasoning
  use explain(analyze=True) for actual runtime metrics
  snapshot plans with version/config awareness
  avoid exact physical snapshots across hardware
  sanitize explain output before sharing
  never remove optimizer rules in production without explicit debug policy
```

## 17.21 Programmatic operator metrics: `ExecutionPlan.metrics()` / `collect_metrics()` (new in 54)

DataFusion 54 exposes operator metrics to Python — previously reachable only by parsing `explain(analyze=True)` text. All behavior below was live-verified against the installed `datafusion==54.0.0` wheel (see [`datafusion_python_54vs53.md`](datafusion_python_54vs53.md) §2.5).

```python id="met54a"
plan = df.execution_plan()

plan.metrics()          # -> MetricsSet | None            (this plan node only)
plan.collect_metrics()  # -> list[tuple[str, MetricsSet]] (description, metrics) over the tree
```

`MetricsSet` (importable from `datafusion` or `datafusion.plan`, alongside `Metric`) exposes first-class properties plus generic access:

```text id="met54b"
MetricsSet:
  output_rows        elapsed_compute        (per-node aggregates; None if not recorded)
  spill_count        spilled_bytes          spilled_rows
  sum_by_name(name)  -> sum a NAMED metric across partitions
  metrics()          -> list[Metric]

Metric:
  name  value  value_as_datetime  labels  partition
  observed names include: start_timestamp, end_timestamp, elapsed_compute,
  output_rows, output_bytes, output_batches, peak_mem_used, spill_count,
  spilled_bytes, spilled_rows, and operator-specific timings
  (e.g. time_calculating_group_ids, aggregation_time, emitting_time)
```

**The plan-instance gotcha (live-verified).** Metrics belong to a specific `ExecutionPlan` *instance*. `df.collect()` builds and executes **its own** plan, so a previously captured `df.execution_plan()` object stays empty:

```python id="met54c"
captured = df.execution_plan()
df.collect()                      # executes a DIFFERENT plan instance
captured.metrics().output_rows    # -> None  (never ran)
```

To read real numbers, execute the captured instance itself:

```python id="met54d"
plan = df.execution_plan()
for p in range(plan.partition_count):
    for batch in ctx.execute(plan, p):     # drive the captured instance
        ...
plan.metrics().output_rows                 # -> real row count
for description, ms in plan.collect_metrics():
    print(description, ms.output_rows, ms.elapsed_compute, ms.spill_count)
```

Note that some operators eagerly initialize a `MetricsSet` before running, so a non-`None` return does not prove the node executed — check the values.

**`sum_by_name` quirk (live-verified):** despite its docstring naming `"output_rows"` as an example, `sum_by_name("output_rows")` and `sum_by_name("elapsed_compute")` return `None` on the installed wheel — the first-class metrics are not reachable by name. Use the properties for the standard metrics; reserve `sum_by_name` for operator-specific named metrics (`sum_by_name("peak_mem_used")` works).

Deployment guidance:

```text id="met54e"
Use collect_metrics() in performance harnesses that own plan execution (ctx.execute path).
Keep explain(analyze=True) for ad-hoc/debug sessions; metrics() for programmatic gates
  (e.g. assert spill_count == 0, track output_rows per operator across versions).
Do not snapshot metric descriptions — operator names/details are version-sensitive (17.17).
```

[1]: https://datafusion.apache.org/blog/output/2026/06/12/datafusion-54.0.0/ "Apache DataFusion 54.0.0 Released"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/using-the-dataframe-api.html "Using the DataFrame API — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/explain-usage.html "Reading Explain Plans — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[4]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html "datafusion.dataframe — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[5]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/explain.html "EXPLAIN — Apache DataFusion  documentation"
[6]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html "datafusion.plan — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[7]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html "datafusion.context — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[8]: https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/configs.html "Configuration Settings — Apache DataFusion  documentation"

# DataFusion Advanced — 18) Configuration and runtime tuning

This section follows the dense, agent-facing technical-reference style of the Cyclopts source material. 

## 18.0 Core configuration invariant

`SessionContext` accepts two orthogonal configuration objects:

```text
SessionContext(
  config:  SessionConfig | None = None,        # planning / execution / catalog config
  runtime: RuntimeEnvBuilder | None = None,    # runtime memory / spill / temp-file config
)
```

DataFusion’s Python configuration guide states that `SessionContext` can be constructed with `SessionConfig` and `RuntimeEnvBuilder`, and shows these objects controlling default catalog/schema, target partitions, information schema, repartitioning, Parquet pruning, and arbitrary config keys through `.set(...)`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```python
from datafusion import RuntimeEnvBuilder, SessionConfig, SessionContext

runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_os()
    .with_fair_spill_pool(1_000_000_000)
)

config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(True)
    .with_default_catalog_and_schema("datafusion", "public")
    .with_information_schema(True)
    .with_target_partitions(16)
    .with_repartition_file_scans(True)
    .with_repartition_joins(True)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(True)
    .with_repartition_windows(True)
    .with_parquet_pruning(True)
    .set("datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters", "true")
)

ctx = SessionContext(config=config, runtime=runtime)
```

---

## 18.1 Configuration surface map

| Layer               | Object                  | Controls                                                                                                            | Typical owner                              |
| ------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| session config      | `SessionConfig`         | batch size, catalog/schema, information schema, target partitions, repartitioning, Parquet pruning, raw config keys | application config / deployment manifest   |
| runtime env         | `RuntimeEnvBuilder`     | disk manager, temp paths, spill pool, memory pool                                                                   | infrastructure / container / worker config |
| context             | `SessionContext`        | binds session config + runtime env to query planning/execution                                                      | bootstrap factory                          |
| query plan          | `DataFrame` / SQL       | logical operations to execute under the context’s config                                                            | query builders                             |
| runtime diagnostics | `explain(analyze=True)` | execution metrics under current config                                                                              | performance workflow                       |

Agent rule:

```text
Do not scatter SessionConfig / RuntimeEnvBuilder construction across query code.
Create a context factory.
Inject configured SessionContext into query builders.
Treat config as deployment state, not transformation logic.
```

---

# 18.2 `RuntimeEnvBuilder`: runtime controls

## 18.2.1 Disk manager controls

```python
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_disk_manager_os()
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_disk_manager_specified("/mnt/df-spill-0", "/mnt/df-spill-1")
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_disk_manager_disabled()
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_temp_file_path("/tmp/datafusion")
```

`RuntimeEnvBuilder.with_disk_manager_os()` uses the operating system temporary directory; `with_disk_manager_specified(*paths)` uses specified paths for temporary files; `with_disk_manager_disabled()` makes attempts to create temporary files error; and `with_temp_file_path(path)` sets the path for needed temporary files. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/datafusion-spill/ssd0", "/datafusion-spill/ssd1")
    .with_temp_file_path("/datafusion-tmp")
)
```

### Disk-manager selection rules

```text
with_disk_manager_os():
  local dev
  notebooks
  simple batch jobs
  container has safe /tmp capacity

with_disk_manager_specified(...):
  production workers
  dedicated spill volumes
  high-throughput local SSD
  predictable storage capacity
  multiple temp disks

with_disk_manager_disabled():
  strict no-spill mode
  fail-fast memory policy
  tests that must catch accidental spilling
  environments where temp-file creation is forbidden
```

### Deployment advisory

```text
Spill/temp path requirements:
  writable by process user
  enough free space
  low-latency local disk preferred
  not a tiny container overlay filesystem
  monitored for capacity
  cleaned by job/container lifecycle
```

---

## 18.2.2 Spill and memory-pool controls

```python
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_fair_spill_pool(size_bytes)
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_greedy_memory_pool(size_bytes)
RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_unbounded_memory_pool()
```

`with_fair_spill_pool(size)` creates a fair spill pool and is documented as best when a query has multiple spillable operators likely to spill; `with_greedy_memory_pool(size)` works well for queries that do not need spilling or have a single spillable operator; `with_unbounded_memory_pool()` disables bounded memory-pool enforcement. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
# Multiple spillable operators: joins + aggregations + sorts.
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/mnt/spill")
    .with_fair_spill_pool(8 * 1024**3)
)

# One dominant operator or simple query profile.
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/mnt/spill")
    .with_greedy_memory_pool(8 * 1024**3)
)
```

### Memory-pool decision table

| Workload                            | Recommended pool                              |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| many concurrent spillable operators | `with_fair_spill_pool(...)`                   |
| one dominant spillable operator     | `with_greedy_memory_pool(...)`                |
| controlled dev notebook             | default or unbounded                          |
| correctness test for no spill       | `with_disk_manager_disabled()` + bounded pool |
| production service with memory SLO  | bounded fair/greedy pool                      |
| exploratory single-user environment | default first, tune after metrics             |

### Agent rules

```text
Fair pool:
  use when multiple operators must share spillable memory.
  can spill earlier because memory is reserved fairly.

Greedy pool:
  use when one spillable operator dominates.
  can improve simple-query throughput.

Unbounded:
  only when process/container memory limit is the real guardrail.
  unsafe for multi-tenant services.
```

---

# 18.3 `SessionConfig`: session and execution controls

## 18.3.1 Constructor and raw key setting

```python
SessionConfig(config_options: dict[str, str] | None = None)
SessionConfig().set(key: str, value: str)
```

`SessionConfig` accepts an optional dict of config options, and `.set(key, value)` sets arbitrary configuration options, returning a new `SessionConfig`. The official configuration reference also documents that DataFusion settings can be supplied programmatically, via environment variables, or through SQL `SET`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
config = SessionConfig({
    "datafusion.execution.target_partitions": "16",
    "datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters": "true",
})

config = config.set("datafusion.optimizer.join_reordering", "true")
```

Agent rules:

```text
Use typed builder methods where available.
Use .set(...) for advanced or newly exposed DataFusion config keys.
Values passed to .set(...) are strings.
Keep raw config keys centralized and documented.
```

---

## 18.3.2 Batch size

```python
SessionConfig().with_batch_size(batch_size: int)
```

`with_batch_size(...)` customizes batch size. The broader config reference lists the default execution batch size as `8192` and describes it as the default batch size for creating new batches, especially useful for buffer-in-memory batches where tiny batches create excessive metadata memory consumption. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_batch_size(16_384)
```

Selection rules:

```text
Increase batch size:
  fewer batches
  lower per-batch overhead
  potentially better vectorized throughput
  higher memory per batch

Decrease batch size:
  lower per-batch memory footprint
  finer-grained streaming/backpressure
  potentially more scheduling/metadata overhead
```

---

## 18.3.3 Default catalog/schema

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(True)
    .with_default_catalog_and_schema("analytics", "prod")
)
```

`with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(...)` controls whether the default catalog/schema are automatically created, and `with_default_catalog_and_schema(catalog, schema)` selects names for the default catalog and schema. The global config reference lists `datafusion` as the default catalog and `public` as the default schema. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Namespace policy

```text
Single-tenant/simple app:
  default catalog/schema acceptable.

Multi-domain app:
  set explicit catalog/schema names.

Generated SQL:
  prefer fully qualified catalog.schema.table when more than one namespace exists.

Tests:
  use explicit default names or fully qualified table references.
```

---

## 18.3.4 Information schema

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_information_schema(True)
```

`with_information_schema(enabled=True)` enables inclusion of `information_schema` virtual tables. The config reference lists `datafusion.catalog.information_schema` as the setting controlling access to information-schema virtual tables. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Use when:

```text
schema discovery
SQL introspection
debugging registered tables
notebook exploration
metadata-driven query generation
```

Avoid or gate when:

```text
multi-tenant services
untrusted SQL
metadata disclosure is a risk
catalog/table names are sensitive
```

---

## 18.3.5 Parquet pruning

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_parquet_pruning(True)
```

`with_parquet_pruning(...)` enables or disables pruning predicates for Parquet readers; pruning predicates let the reader skip row groups. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
ctx = SessionContext(
    config=SessionConfig().with_parquet_pruning(True)
)
```

Selection rules:

```text
Enable:
  production Parquet scans
  predicate-heavy analytics
  partitioned/object-store data
  large row-group datasets

Disable:
  debugging pruning behavior
  comparing scan behavior
  reproducing optimizer/pruning bugs
```

---

# 18.4 Parallelism and CPU utilization

## 18.4.1 Target partitions

```python
SessionConfig().with_target_partitions(target_partitions: int)
```

`with_target_partitions(...)` customizes target partitions for query execution; increasing partitions can increase concurrency. The Python configuration guide states that DataFusion uses partitions to parallelize work, that the default number of CPU cores is often enough for small queries, and that tuning partition count and automatic repartitioning can improve hardware utilization. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_target_partitions(16)
ctx = SessionContext(config=config)
```

### Partition-count policy

```text
Default:
  usually enough for small queries
  typically based on CPU-core count

Increase target_partitions when:
  scans have enough files/row groups/splits
  joins/aggregates/windows can parallelize
  CPU underutilization observed
  pipeline is batch/analytical
  operator metrics show large single partitions

Decrease target_partitions when:
  overhead dominates
  result is small
  many tiny files create scheduling overhead
  memory pressure increases with too many concurrent partitions
  service has many concurrent queries
```

### Heuristic starting points

```text
local dev:
  target_partitions = cpu_count or default

single batch worker:
  target_partitions = cpu_count to 2 * cpu_count

large object-store scan:
  target_partitions = cpu_count to 4 * cpu_count, benchmark required

memory-limited worker:
  target_partitions = cpu_count or lower; tune with spill metrics

multi-tenant service:
  target_partitions = per-query CPU budget, not host CPU count
```

---

## 18.4.2 Repartitioning controls

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_target_partitions(16)
    .with_repartition_file_scans(True)
    .with_repartition_joins(True)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(True)
    .with_repartition_sorts(True)
    .with_repartition_windows(True)
)
```

`with_repartition_file_scans(...)` enables/disables repartitioning for file scans; `with_repartition_joins(...)` enables repartitioning for joins to improve parallelism; `with_repartition_aggregations(...)` enables repartitioning for aggregations and improves parallelism; `with_repartition_windows(...)` enables repartitioning for window functions and may improve parallelism. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

### Control meanings

| Method                                | Target operator | Value case                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `with_repartition_file_scans(True)`   | file scans      | more parallel scan tasks           |
| `with_repartition_joins(True)`        | joins           | distribute join work               |
| `with_repartition_aggregations(True)` | aggregates      | parallel partial/final aggregation |
| `with_repartition_sorts(True)`        | sorts           | parallel sort-related work         |
| `with_repartition_windows(True)`      | windows         | partitioned window processing      |

### Selection rules

```text
Enable repartitioning when:
  large input
  enough CPU available
  joins/aggregates/windows dominate runtime
  plan shows insufficient partition count
  explain/analyze shows hot single operators

Disable repartitioning when:
  tiny data
  overhead dominates
  strict ordering/control needed for debugging
  memory pressure increases due to parallel operators
  reproducing bugs or comparing baseline behavior
```

---

## 18.4.3 File scan repartition size

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_repartition_file_min_size(size: int)
```

`with_repartition_file_min_size(size)` sets the minimum file range size for repartitioning scans. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_repartition_file_scans(True)
    .with_repartition_file_min_size(64 * 1024 * 1024)
)
```

Policy:

```text
Increase min size:
  fewer scan partitions
  lower scheduling overhead
  better for many small files

Decrease min size:
  more scan partitions
  more parallelism
  useful for large files and underutilized CPU
```

---

# 18.5 Manual DataFrame repartitioning

The Python configuration guide documents manual repartitioning on DataFrames through `df.repartition(num)` and `df.repartition_by_hash(col("a"), num=...)`. Use this only when automatic repartitioning is insufficient or a query requires explicit control. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```python
from datafusion import col

df = ctx.read_parquet("data.parquet")

# Evenly divide into 16 partitions.
df = df.repartition(16)

# Hash partition by one or more expressions.
df = df.repartition_by_hash(col("customer_id"), num=16)

result = df.collect()
```

Manual repartitioning rules:

```text
Use:
  targeted benchmark tuning
  known skew mitigation experiment
  preparing data for expensive group/join keys
  deterministic partition-count tests

Avoid:
  routine query construction
  small data
  before every operation by default
  without explain/analyze evidence
```

---

# 18.6 Config setting channels

DataFusion configuration settings can be supplied programmatically, via environment variables, or via SQL `SET`; the config reference gives examples for `datafusion.execution.target_partitions` in each form. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

```python
config = SessionConfig().set("datafusion.execution.target_partitions", "16")
ctx = SessionContext(config=config)
```

```bash
DATAFUSION_EXECUTION_TARGET_PARTITIONS=16 python app.py
```

```sql
SET datafusion.execution.target_partitions = '16';
```

Agent policy:

```text
Programmatic SessionConfig:
  best for application-owned config
  easiest to test/version-control

Environment variables:
  useful for infrastructure-level overrides
  document in deployment manifests

SQL SET:
  useful for SQL console/admin workflows
  dangerous for untrusted SQL unless statements are disabled
```

---

# 18.7 Production context factory

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from datafusion import RuntimeEnvBuilder, SessionConfig, SessionContext


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DataFusionRuntimeSettings:
    temp_dir: str | Path = "/tmp/datafusion"
    spill_paths: tuple[str | Path, ...] = ()
    memory_pool: str = "fair"          # fair | greedy | unbounded
    memory_limit_bytes: int = 8 * 1024**3


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DataFusionSessionSettings:
    catalog: str = "datafusion"
    schema: str = "public"
    batch_size: int = 8192
    target_partitions: int = 16
    information_schema: bool = False
    parquet_pruning: bool = True
    repartition_file_scans: bool = True
    repartition_joins: bool = True
    repartition_aggregations: bool = True
    repartition_sorts: bool = True
    repartition_windows: bool = True
    raw_options: dict[str, str] = None


def build_runtime(settings: DataFusionRuntimeSettings) -> RuntimeEnvBuilder:
    runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder()

    if settings.spill_paths:
        runtime = runtime.with_disk_manager_specified(*settings.spill_paths)
    else:
        runtime = runtime.with_disk_manager_os()

    runtime = runtime.with_temp_file_path(settings.temp_dir)

    if settings.memory_pool == "fair":
        runtime = runtime.with_fair_spill_pool(settings.memory_limit_bytes)
    elif settings.memory_pool == "greedy":
        runtime = runtime.with_greedy_memory_pool(settings.memory_limit_bytes)
    elif settings.memory_pool == "unbounded":
        runtime = runtime.with_unbounded_memory_pool()
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported memory_pool: {settings.memory_pool}")

    return runtime


def build_session_config(settings: DataFusionSessionSettings) -> SessionConfig:
    config = (
        SessionConfig()
        .with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(True)
        .with_default_catalog_and_schema(settings.catalog, settings.schema)
        .with_information_schema(settings.information_schema)
        .with_batch_size(settings.batch_size)
        .with_target_partitions(settings.target_partitions)
        .with_parquet_pruning(settings.parquet_pruning)
        .with_repartition_file_scans(settings.repartition_file_scans)
        .with_repartition_joins(settings.repartition_joins)
        .with_repartition_aggregations(settings.repartition_aggregations)
        .with_repartition_sorts(settings.repartition_sorts)
        .with_repartition_windows(settings.repartition_windows)
    )

    for key, value in (settings.raw_options or {}).items():
        config = config.set(key, value)

    return config


def make_context(
    runtime_settings: DataFusionRuntimeSettings,
    session_settings: DataFusionSessionSettings,
) -> SessionContext:
    return SessionContext(
        config=build_session_config(session_settings),
        runtime=build_runtime(runtime_settings),
    )
```

# 18.8 Workload-specific profiles

## 18.8.1 Default/local profile

```python
ctx = SessionContext()
```

Use when:

```text
small data
notebook exploration
local examples
unit tests
no special memory/spill constraints
```

The official guide says the default configuration is often sufficient for small queries. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 18.8.2 Batch analytics profile

```python
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/mnt/ssd/datafusion-spill")
    .with_temp_file_path("/mnt/ssd/datafusion-tmp")
    .with_fair_spill_pool(32 * 1024**3)
)

config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_target_partitions(64)
    .with_repartition_file_scans(True)
    .with_repartition_joins(True)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(True)
    .with_repartition_windows(True)
    .with_parquet_pruning(True)
)
```

Use when:

```text
long-running batch jobs
large Parquet scans
joins/aggregates/windows
dedicated worker resources
local spill volume available
```

---

## 18.8.3 Memory-limited service profile

```python
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/var/lib/app/datafusion-spill")
    .with_greedy_memory_pool(2 * 1024**3)
)

config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_target_partitions(4)
    .with_repartition_joins(True)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(True)
    .with_repartition_windows(False)
    .with_parquet_pruning(True)
)
```

Use when:

```text
many concurrent queries
fixed container memory
latency-sensitive service
strict resource isolation
bounded per-query CPU budget
```

---

## 18.8.4 No-spill strict profile

```python
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_disabled()
    .with_greedy_memory_pool(512 * 1024**2)
)

config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_target_partitions(2)
    .with_parquet_pruning(True)
)
```

Use when:

```text
tests must fail on spill
ephemeral environment disallows temp files
small bounded workloads
memory-only correctness runs
```

# 18.9 CPU utilization tuning workflow

```text
1. Start with default SessionContext.
2. Run representative query.
3. Capture df.explain(analyze=True).
4. Inspect CPU utilization, partition count, row counts, hot operators.
5. Increase target_partitions if CPU is underutilized and data can split.
6. Enable targeted repartitioning for hot joins/aggregates/windows.
7. Tune memory pool and spill directory if spilling or OOM occurs.
8. Re-run explain/analyze.
9. Record config and results in benchmark artifact.
```

DataFusion’s configuration guide states that partitions parallelize work and that higher target partition counts plus automatic repartitioning for joins, aggregations, and windows can improve CPU utilization. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```python
def diagnose(df):
    print("OPTIMIZED LOGICAL")
    print(df.optimized_logical_plan().display_indent())

    print("PHYSICAL")
    print(df.execution_plan().display_indent())

    print("RUNTIME")
    df.explain(analyze=True)
```

```yaml
datafusion:

    memory_pool: fair

  session:

```

Agent rule:

```text
Every production config value should have:
  value
  default assumption
  owner
  reason
  workload target
  benchmark link or issue link
  rollback value
```

# 18.11 Tuning target partitions

## 18.11.1 Symptoms and responses

| Symptom                                     | Likely cause                               | Candidate action                                              |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CPU mostly idle during large scan           | too few partitions / source not splittable | increase `target_partitions`, enable file scan repartitioning |
| CPU idle during joins                       | join not repartitioned / skew              | enable repartition joins, inspect join plan                   |
| CPU idle during group-by                    | aggregate bottleneck                       | enable aggregation repartitioning                             |
| CPU idle during windows                     | window partitions not parallelized         | enable window repartitioning, inspect partition keys          |
| high overhead on tiny queries               | too many partitions                        | reduce `target_partitions`                                    |
| memory pressure after increasing partitions | more concurrent operator state             | reduce partitions or increase memory/spill budget             |
| spill storms                                | too low memory pool / too much concurrency | fair pool, more memory, lower partitions                      |

---

## 18.11.2 Agent heuristic

```python
import os

def default_target_partitions(
    *,
    workload: str,
    query_concurrency: int = 1,
) -> int:
    cpu = os.cpu_count() or 1

    if workload == "local":
        return cpu

    if workload == "batch":
        return max(cpu, cpu * 2)

    if workload == "service":
        return max(1, cpu // max(query_concurrency, 1))

    if workload == "memory_limited":
        return max(1, cpu // 2)

    raise ValueError(f"unknown workload: {workload}")
```

Use as starting point only; validate with `explain(analyze=True)` and real hardware.

---

# 18.12 Repartitioning policy

```text
Repartitioning is not “always faster.”
It trades shuffle/exchange overhead and memory pressure for parallelism.
```

## Enable deliberately

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_repartition_file_scans(True)
    .with_repartition_joins(True)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(True)
    .with_repartition_windows(True)
)
```

Use when:

```text
large inputs
large joins
large group-bys
large windows
available CPU > observed parallelism
metrics show skewed/hot operators
```

## Disable deliberately

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_repartition_joins(False)
    .with_repartition_aggregations(False)
    .with_repartition_windows(False)
)
```

Use when:

```text
small data
debugging exact plan shape
too many partitions/overhead
memory pressure from parallelism
reproducing single-thread-ish behavior
service query concurrency is high
```

---

# 18.13 Parquet pruning and pushdown policy

```python
config = (
    SessionConfig()
    .with_parquet_pruning(True)
    .set("datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters", "true")
)
```

`with_parquet_pruning(True)` enables pruning predicates that allow Parquet readers to skip row groups. The Python configuration guide also shows raw `.set("datafusion.execution.parquet.pushdown_filters", "true")` in an explicit config example. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Use when:

```text
Parquet files contain row-group statistics
queries filter on columns with useful statistics
large file scans dominate cost
object-store I/O is expensive
```

Debug when:

```text
predicate not near scan in optimized plan
row groups not skipped
schemas lack statistics
filters wrap columns in non-pushdown-friendly expressions
```

---

# 18.14 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: config inside query builder

```python
def build_report():
    ctx = SessionContext(
        SessionConfig().with_target_partitions(64)
    )
    return ctx.sql("SELECT ...")
```

Correct:

```python
def build_report(ctx: SessionContext):
    return ctx.sql("SELECT ...")
```

---

## Anti-pattern: unbounded memory pool in multi-tenant service

```python
runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_unbounded_memory_pool()
```

Correct:

```python
runtime = (
    RuntimeEnvBuilder()
    .with_disk_manager_specified("/var/lib/app/spill")
    .with_greedy_memory_pool(2 * 1024**3)
)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: disabling disk manager accidentally

```python
runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_disk_manager_disabled()
```

Correct only when:

```text
spill must fail
tests are intentionally no-spill
queries are known bounded
```

Otherwise:

```python
runtime = RuntimeEnvBuilder().with_disk_manager_os()
```

---

## Anti-pattern: increasing partitions without memory budget

```python
config = SessionConfig().with_target_partitions(512)
```

Correct:

```text
Increase partitions only with:
  enough CPU
  enough memory
  enough spill capacity
  benchmark evidence
```

---

## Anti-pattern: environment-only config with no manifest

```bash
DATAFUSION_EXECUTION_TARGET_PARTITIONS=64 python app.py
```

Correct:

```text
Environment overrides allowed, but deployment manifest must document:
  key
  value
  reason
  owner
  workload
  rollback
```

# 18.15 Testing and benchmarking patterns

## 18.15.1 Config construction test

```python
def test_config_factory():
    ctx = make_context(
        DataFusionRuntimeSettings(
            temp_dir="/tmp/datafusion-test",
            memory_pool="greedy",
            memory_limit_bytes=512 * 1024**2,
        ),
        DataFusionSessionSettings(
            target_partitions=4,
            parquet_pruning=True,
            repartition_joins=True,
        ),
    )

    assert isinstance(ctx, SessionContext)
```

## 18.15.2 Plan-shape test under config

```python
def test_join_repartition_config_shape(ctx):
    df = build_join_query(ctx)
    plan = df.execution_plan().display_indent()

    assert "Join" in plan or "join" in plan.lower()
```

## 18.15.3 Benchmark loop

```python
def run_config_benchmark(make_df, configs):
    results = []

    for name, config, runtime in configs:
        ctx = SessionContext(config=config, runtime=runtime)
        df = make_df(ctx)

        # terminal performance path
        df.explain(analyze=True)

        results.append({
            "name": name,
            "partitions": config,
            "plan": df.execution_plan().display_indent(),
        })

    return results
```

Benchmark dimensions:

```text
target_partitions:
  default, cpu, 2*cpu, 4*cpu

repartition:
  joins on/off
  aggregations on/off
  windows on/off
  file scans on/off

memory:
  fair vs greedy
  1GB / 4GB / 16GB
  one spill path vs multiple spill paths
```

# 18.16 Deployment checklist

```text
Configuration ownership:
  [ ] Config built in context factory.
  [ ] Query builders receive SessionContext.
  [ ] No config mutation in transformation functions.
  [ ] Config values documented in deployment manifest.

Runtime:
  [ ] Disk manager configured deliberately.
  [ ] Spill/temp directories writable and monitored.
  [ ] Memory pool selected: fair / greedy / unbounded.
  [ ] Memory limit fits container/job limits.
  [ ] No unbounded pool in multi-tenant services unless externally constrained.

Session:
  [ ] Default catalog/schema selected intentionally.
  [ ] information_schema enabled only when metadata exposure is acceptable.
  [ ] batch_size tuned only with benchmark evidence.
  [ ] raw .set(...) keys documented.

Parallelism:
  [ ] target_partitions tuned to hardware/workload.
  [ ] repartition_file_scans intentional.
  [ ] repartition_joins intentional.
  [ ] repartition_aggregations intentional.
  [ ] repartition_windows intentional.
  [ ] explain/analyze evidence captured.

Parquet:
  [ ] parquet_pruning=True for production Parquet scans.
  [ ] pushdown-related raw options documented.
  [ ] filter shapes verified in optimized plans.

Validation:
  [ ] Run representative benchmark after config changes.
  [ ] Snapshot config alongside plan/metric artifacts.
  [ ] Keep version/config/hardware metadata with performance numbers.
```

## 18.17 Section compression for LLM agents

```text
Construction:
  from datafusion import RuntimeEnvBuilder, SessionConfig, SessionContext

  ctx = SessionContext(config=SessionConfig(...), runtime=RuntimeEnvBuilder(...))

RuntimeEnvBuilder:
  with_disk_manager_os()
  with_disk_manager_specified(*paths)
  with_disk_manager_disabled()
  with_temp_file_path(path)
  with_fair_spill_pool(size_bytes)
  with_greedy_memory_pool(size_bytes)
  with_unbounded_memory_pool()

SessionConfig:
  SessionConfig(config_options: dict[str, str] | None = None)
  set(key: str, value: str)
  with_batch_size(batch_size)
  with_create_default_catalog_and_schema(enabled=True)
  with_default_catalog_and_schema(catalog, schema)
  with_information_schema(enabled=True)
  with_parquet_pruning(enabled=True)
  with_repartition_file_scans(enabled=True)
  with_repartition_file_min_size(size)
  with_repartition_joins(enabled=True)
  with_repartition_aggregations(enabled=True)
  with_repartition_sorts(enabled=True)
  with_repartition_windows(enabled=True)
  with_target_partitions(target_partitions)

Runtime policy:
  OS disk manager -> simple/default
  specified disk manager -> production spill volumes
  disabled disk manager -> no-spill fail-fast tests
  fair spill pool -> multiple spillable operators
  greedy pool -> one dominant spillable operator
  unbounded pool -> dev or externally constrained process only

CPU policy:
  target_partitions controls desired execution parallelism
  default is often enough for small queries
  increase for large parallelizable workloads
  decrease for tiny queries or high service concurrency

Repartition policy:
  enable joins/aggregations/windows/file scans when CPU underutilized
  disable when overhead or memory pressure dominates
  benchmark every change

Parquet:
  with_parquet_pruning(True) enables row-group skipping
  use .set(...) for advanced keys such as parquet pushdown filters

Best practices:
  centralize context construction
  document every config value
  tune target_partitions against real hardware
  keep spill paths writable and monitored
  avoid unbounded memory in services
  use explain(analyze=True) for performance work
  store config + version + hardware with benchmark artifacts
```

[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html "datafusion.context — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"

# DataFusion Advanced — 19) Writing data and materialization

This section follows the dense, agent-facing technical-reference style of the Cyclopts source material. 

## 19.0 Core write/materialization invariant

`DataFrame.write_*` APIs are **terminal execution boundaries**. They execute the DataFusion plan and write output to a sink. They are not lazy transformations.

```text id="2w99lm"
DataFrame logical plan
  -> optimization
  -> physical execution
  -> RecordBatch stream
  -> writer sink
  -> filesystem/object-store/table side effect
```

`write_csv`, `write_json`, `write_parquet`, `write_parquet_with_options`, and `write_table` are documented as executing the `DataFrame` and writing results to CSV, JSON, Parquet, Parquet with advanced options, or a registered table. `write_table` requires the target table to be registered, and not all table providers support writing. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="x2uuv6"
from datafusion import SessionContext, col, lit

ctx = SessionContext()

df = (
    ctx.read_parquet("input/events/")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .select("event_id", "user_id", "amount", "event_ts")
)

# Terminal side effect:
df.write_parquet("output/events.parquet")
```

---

## 19.1 API surface map

| API                               | Sink                      | Terminal? | Main option object                              |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------: | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `write_parquet(...)`              | Parquet file/path         |       yes | `Compression`, `DataFrameWriteOptions`          |
| `write_parquet_with_options(...)` | Parquet file/path         |       yes | `ParquetWriterOptions`, `DataFrameWriteOptions` |
| `write_csv(...)`                  | CSV file/path             |       yes | `DataFrameWriteOptions`                         |
| `write_json(...)`                 | JSON file/path            |       yes | `DataFrameWriteOptions`                         |
| `write_table(...)`                | registered table provider |       yes | `DataFrameWriteOptions`                         |

The DataFrame API documents `write_csv`, `write_json`, `write_parquet`, `write_parquet_with_options`, and `write_table`; `write_table` notes that table provider support varies. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

# 19.2 `write_parquet(...)`

## 19.2.1 Signatures

```python id="7ja088"
df.write_parquet(
    path: str | Path,
    compression: str,
    compression_level: int | None = None,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

```python id="5hor16"
df.write_parquet(
    path: str | Path,
    compression: Compression = Compression.ZSTD,
    compression_level: int | None = None,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

```python id="z8dpqj"
df.write_parquet(
    path: str | Path,
    compression: ParquetWriterOptions,
    compression_level: None = None,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_parquet(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes a Parquet file. The DataFrame API lists accepted compression codecs: `uncompressed`, `snappy`, `gzip`, `brotli`, `lz4`, `lz4_raw`, and `zstd`; LZO is excluded because it is not implemented in arrow-rs. The default compression is ZSTD, and for ZSTD the recommended level range is 1–22 with default 4; higher levels improve compression but reduce speed. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="hmt4q0"
from datafusion.dataframe import Compression

df.write_parquet(
    "output/events.parquet",
    compression=Compression.ZSTD,
    compression_level=4,
)
```

String codec:

```python id="jj8g60"
df.write_parquet(
    "output/events.parquet",
    compression="zstd",
    compression_level=4,
)
```

Uncompressed:

```python id="9b0zry"
df.write_parquet(
    "output/events-uncompressed.parquet",
    compression="uncompressed",
)
```

---

## 19.2.2 Compression enum

```python id="zlv4y0"
from datafusion.dataframe import Compression

Compression.UNCOMPRESSED
Compression.SNAPPY
Compression.GZIP
Compression.BROTLI
Compression.LZ4
Compression.LZ4_RAW
Compression.ZSTD

Compression.from_str("zstd")
Compression.ZSTD.get_default_level()
```

`Compression` is an enum for Parquet compression types and exposes `from_str(...)` and `get_default_level()`; the documented enum values are `BROTLI`, `GZIP`, `LZ4`, `LZ4_RAW`, `SNAPPY`, `UNCOMPRESSED`, and `ZSTD`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

# 19.3 Compression strategy

## 19.3.1 Codec semantics

```text id="35zsap"
uncompressed:
  no compression
  fastest write/decode in some cases
  largest files
  useful for debugging or legacy consumers

snappy:
  fast compression/decompression
  widely supported in Parquet ecosystems
  moderate compression ratio
  good interoperability fallback

gzip:
  strong compatibility
  better ratio than snappy
  slower compression/decompression
  useful when downstream mandates gzip

brotli:
  high compression ratio
  potentially slower
  useful for archival or bandwidth-constrained output where supported

lz4:
  very fast
  lower compression ratio than zstd/gzip/brotli
  useful for speed-prioritized intermediate data

lz4_raw:
  raw LZ4 variant
  validate downstream support before using

zstd:
  balanced speed/compression
  modern default choice
  tunable level range
```

DataFusion Python changed Parquet saving to use ZSTD by default in 46.0.0; the release note says ZSTD balances speed and compression ratio, and users can still write uncompressed Parquet by passing the compression argument. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/blog/output/2025/03/30/datafusion-python-46.0.0/))

---

## 19.3.2 Compression level policy

```text id="98rnp6"
ZSTD:
  range: 1..22
  default from write_parquet docs: 4
  lower level -> faster, larger files
  higher level -> slower, smaller files

GZIP/BROTLI in ParquetWriterOptions:
  expressed as gzip(level), brotli(level)

SNAPPY/LZ4/LZ4_RAW:
  no level in common Parquet option syntax

UNCOMPRESSED:
  no level
```

For `write_parquet`, ZSTD’s recommended range and speed/ratio tradeoff are documented directly in the Python DataFrame API. For advanced writer options, `ParquetWriterOptions` supports compression strings such as `gzip(n)`, `brotli(n)`, and `zstd(n)`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

## 19.3.3 Codec decision table

| Need                                           | Recommended codec                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| balanced production default                    | `zstd`, level 3–6                            |
| maximum compatibility with old Parquet readers | `snappy`                                     |
| fast intermediate writes                       | `lz4` or `snappy`                            |
| smallest archival output                       | `zstd` higher level or `brotli` if supported |
| debug raw output                               | `uncompressed`                               |
| downstream requires gzip                       | `gzip(level)`                                |
| uncertain consumer support                     | test `zstd`, fallback to `snappy`            |

Agent rule:

```text id="rtt4v4"
Choose ZSTD by default unless:
  downstream reader does not support it
  low-latency write speed dominates
  legacy ecosystem requires snappy/gzip
  debugging requires uncompressed output
```

---

# 19.4 `write_parquet_with_options(...)`

## 19.4.1 Signature

```python id="g0prkm"
df.write_parquet_with_options(
    path: str | Path,
    options: ParquetWriterOptions,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_parquet_with_options(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes Parquet while allowing advanced writer options through `ParquetWriterOptions`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="k9a71n"
from datafusion.dataframe import ParquetWriterOptions

options = ParquetWriterOptions(
    compression="zstd(6)",
    max_row_group_size=1_000_000,
    statistics_enabled="page",
    dictionary_enabled=True,
)

df.write_parquet_with_options(
    "output/events.parquet",
    options=options,
)
```

---

# 19.5 `ParquetWriterOptions`

## 19.5.1 Constructor

```python id="b05k2f"
ParquetWriterOptions(
    data_pagesize_limit: int = 1024 * 1024,
    write_batch_size: int = 1024,
    writer_version: str = "1.0",
    skip_arrow_metadata: bool = False,
    compression: str | None = "zstd(3)",
    compression_level: int | None = None,
    dictionary_enabled: bool | None = True,
    dictionary_page_size_limit: int = 1024 * 1024,
    statistics_enabled: str | None = "page",
    max_row_group_size: int = 1024 * 1024,
    created_by: str = "datafusion-python",
    column_index_truncate_length: int | None = 64,
    statistics_truncate_length: int | None = None,
    data_page_row_count_limit: int = 20000,
    encoding: str | None = None,
    bloom_filter_on_write: bool = False,
    bloom_filter_fpp: float | None = None,
    bloom_filter_ndv: int | None = None,
    allow_single_file_parallelism: bool = True,
    maximum_parallel_row_group_writers: int = 1,
    maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream: int = 2,
    column_specific_options: dict[str, ParquetColumnOptions] | None = None,
)
```

`ParquetWriterOptions` is documented as the advanced Parquet writer option object. It applies to the entire file, with some options overridable per column through `column_specific_options`. Options include page size, batch size, writer version, Arrow metadata, compression, dictionary encoding, statistics, row group size, encoding, bloom filters, and parallel writer controls. Larger row groups require more memory but can improve compression and scan efficiency. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

## 19.5.2 Writer option policy table

| Option                                       | Role                               | Typical policy                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compression`                                | global codec/level                 | `zstd(3)` to `zstd(6)` default production                                  |
| `max_row_group_size`                         | rows per row group                 | raise for large scans/read efficiency; lower for memory-constrained writes |
| `statistics_enabled`                         | min/max/null stats                 | keep `page` or `chunk` for pruning-friendly files                          |
| `dictionary_enabled`                         | dictionary encoding                | true for low-cardinality string/category columns                           |
| `encoding`                                   | page encoding                      | leave `None` unless downstream/per-column need                             |
| `skip_arrow_metadata`                        | omit Arrow schema metadata         | false unless consumer compatibility requires                               |
| `writer_version`                             | Parquet writer format              | `1.0` for conservative compatibility; `2.0` after consumer validation      |
| `bloom_filter_on_write`                      | write bloom filters globally       | enable only for selective equality filters and validated readers           |
| `column_specific_options`                    | override per column                | use for payload/high-cardinality/special columns                           |
| `allow_single_file_parallelism`              | parallelism for single-file output | keep true if memory budget allows                                          |
| `maximum_parallel_row_group_writers`         | row-group writer concurrency       | increase only with memory budget                                           |
| `maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream` | buffering                          | tune for throughput vs memory                                              |

The SQL format-options page documents that Parquet compression, encoding, dictionary, and statistics can be column-specific; unsupported options error, while column-specific options for nonexistent columns are ignored. It also lists default Parquet compression as `zstd(3)`, `max_row_group_size` as `1048576`, row-group size memory/read-efficiency tradeoffs, page index/pruning defaults, and writer-related keys such as write batch size, writer version, Arrow metadata, and created-by metadata. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html))

---

# 19.6 Column-level Parquet options

## 19.6.1 Constructor

```python id="0eg9pa"
ParquetColumnOptions(
    encoding: str | None = None,
    dictionary_enabled: bool | None = None,
    compression: str | None = None,
    statistics_enabled: str | None = None,
    bloom_filter_enabled: bool | None = None,
    bloom_filter_fpp: float | None = None,
    bloom_filter_ndv: int | None = None,
)
```

`ParquetColumnOptions` contains options applied to individual Parquet columns, replacing global `ParquetWriterOptions` settings. Valid encodings include `plain`, `plain_dictionary`, `rle`, `bit_packed`, `delta_binary_packed`, `delta_length_byte_array`, `delta_byte_array`, `rle_dictionary`, and `byte_stream_split`; compression supports codec strings such as `uncompressed`, `snappy`, `gzip(level)`, `brotli(level)`, `lz4`, `zstd(level)`, and `lz4_raw`; statistics settings include `none`, `chunk`, and `page`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="fje3px"
from datafusion.dataframe import ParquetColumnOptions, ParquetWriterOptions

options = ParquetWriterOptions(
    compression="zstd(4)",
    dictionary_enabled=True,
    statistics_enabled="page",
    column_specific_options={
        "event_type": ParquetColumnOptions(
            dictionary_enabled=True,
            compression="zstd(3)",
            statistics_enabled="page",
        ),
        "raw_payload": ParquetColumnOptions(
            dictionary_enabled=False,
            compression="zstd(9)",
            statistics_enabled="none",
        ),
        "amount": ParquetColumnOptions(
            encoding="byte_stream_split",
            compression="zstd(4)",
            statistics_enabled="page",
        ),
    },
)

df.write_parquet_with_options("output/events.parquet", options)
```

---

## 19.6.2 Column-option use cases

```text id="bcz9xc"
Low-cardinality categorical:
  dictionary_enabled=True
  compression=zstd(3)
  statistics_enabled=page

High-cardinality free text / JSON payload:
  dictionary_enabled=False
  compression=zstd(6..9)
  statistics_enabled=none or chunk depending on filter usage

Numeric analytics column:
  encoding=byte_stream_split if reader ecosystem supports it
  compression=zstd(3..6)
  statistics_enabled=page

Join/filter key:
  dictionary_enabled=True when cardinality permits
  statistics_enabled=page
  optional bloom_filter_enabled=True after consumer validation

Sensitive string:
  statistics_enabled=none
  consider statistics_truncate_length / column_index_truncate_length
```

Agent rule:

```text id="ih7c4h"
Column-specific options are a schema contract.
Validate downstream readers before using specialized encoding, bloom filters, or uncommon codecs.
```

---

# 19.7 `DataFrameWriteOptions`

## 19.7.1 Constructor

```python id="0x3p43"
DataFrameWriteOptions(
    insert_operation: InsertOp | None = None,
    single_file_output: bool = False,
    partition_by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    sort_by: Expr | SortExpr | Sequence[Expr] | Sequence[SortExpr] | None = None,
)
```

`DataFrameWriteOptions` controls DataFrame writing behavior. The docs warn that there is no guarantee a given table provider supports every writer option, so support must be validated per sink/provider. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="ak2gbc"
from datafusion import col
from datafusion.dataframe import DataFrameWriteOptions

write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    single_file_output=False,
    partition_by=["dt", "region"],
    sort_by=[
        col("dt").sort(ascending=True),
        col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True),
    ],
)
```

---

## 19.7.2 `InsertOp`

```python id="0jagpd"
from datafusion.dataframe import InsertOp

InsertOp.APPEND
InsertOp.OVERWRITE
InsertOp.REPLACE
```

`InsertOp.APPEND` appends rows without modifying existing rows; `InsertOp.OVERWRITE` overwrites all existing rows; `InsertOp.REPLACE` replaces rows that collide, typically by unique key or primary key. These modes are used by table-writing features. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="66rn6w"
write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    insert_operation=InsertOp.OVERWRITE,
    partition_by=["dt"],
)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="e5e1bd"
Every write path should declare overwrite/append/replace semantics explicitly.
If the sink/provider ignores a mode, fail deployment validation.
```

---

## 19.7.3 Partitioned output

```python id="3j71qs"
write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    partition_by=["dt", "region"],
)

df.write_parquet(
    "output/events/",
    compression="zstd",
    compression_level=4,
    write_options=write_options,
)
```

SQL `COPY ... PARTITIONED BY (...)` examples show partitioned output; the format-options docs state that one Parquet file is written in parallel per query partition for a folder output and demonstrate `PARTITIONED BY (column3, column4)`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html))

Partition policy:

```text id="5c80w3"
Use partition_by when:
  downstream queries filter by partition columns
  output is a dataset directory, not one file
  partition cardinality is bounded and useful
  lakehouse layout convention requires it

Avoid partition_by when:
  high-cardinality partition keys create many tiny files
  downstream expects single file
  partition column values are sparse/unbounded
  consumer cannot read partitioned layouts
```

---

## 19.7.4 Single-file output

```python id="m1842q"
write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    single_file_output=True,
)

df.write_parquet(
    "output/events.parquet",
    compression="zstd",
    write_options=write_options,
)
```

Use when:

```text id="c6e9rk"
bounded output
human/download artifact
interoperability system expects one file
test fixture / golden file
```

Avoid when:

```text id="ullidq"
large result
parallel output desired
object-store output at scale
memory pressure from single sink
downstream can read dataset directory
```

---

## 19.7.5 Sort-before-write

```python id="af5uff"
write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    sort_by=[
        col("dt").sort(ascending=True, nulls_first=False),
        col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True, nulls_first=False),
    ],
)

df.write_parquet(
    "output/events/",
    compression="zstd",
    write_options=write_options,
)
```

Sort policy:

```text id="piq83v"
Use sort_by when:
  downstream read patterns benefit from ordering
  row-group statistics/pruning improve
  deterministic file contents needed
  range scans over sort key are common

Cost:
  sort may be expensive
  sort may require spill
  sort before write is a deliberate physical layout decision
```

---

# 19.8 `write_table(...)`

## 19.8.1 Signature

```python id="scbg67"
df.write_table(
    table_name: str,
    write_options: DataFrameWriteOptions | None = None,
) -> None
```

`write_table(...)` executes the DataFrame and writes results to a registered table. The table must be registered with the session, and not all providers support writing operations. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="f3cm6a"
df.write_table(
    "target_table",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(
        insert_operation=InsertOp.APPEND,
    ),
)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="6q2qwy"
Use write_table only after validating target provider write support.
Do not assume all registered tables are writable.
Test append/overwrite/replace semantics per provider.
```

---

# 19.9 SQL `COPY` option equivalence

SQL `COPY` supports format options and partitioned output. Example syntax:

```sql id="7n6722"
COPY source_table
TO 'test/table_with_options'
PARTITIONED BY (column3, column4)
OPTIONS (
  format parquet,
  compression snappy,
  'compression::column1' 'zstd(5)'
);
```

The SQL format-options guide explains that this writes a folder of Parquet files, one file in parallel per query partition, sets global Snappy compression, and overrides `column1` to use ZSTD level 5. It also states column-specific Parquet option keys use `OPTION::COLUMN.NESTED.PATH` syntax. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html))

Python equivalent:

```python id="u5xr07"
options = ParquetWriterOptions(
    compression="snappy",
    column_specific_options={
        "column1": ParquetColumnOptions(compression="zstd(5)")
    },
)

write_options = DataFrameWriteOptions(
    partition_by=["column3", "column4"],
)

df.write_parquet_with_options(
    "test/table_with_options",
    options=options,
    write_options=write_options,
)
```

---

# 19.10 Output materialization strategy

## 19.10.1 File write vs Python materialization

```text id="c0ayob"
write_parquet:
  query executes and streams into file writer
  avoids Python-side pandas/list/dict materialization
  preferred for large durable analytical output

to_pandas / to_pylist / collect:
  materializes in Python memory
  use only for bounded outputs or tests
```

The DataFrame API states `__arrow_c_stream__` exposes streaming record batches without materializing the full result, while write APIs execute and write to files. Use writer APIs for large durable outputs rather than collecting then writing with Python libraries. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

## 19.10.2 Recommended pipeline

```python id="49o3ww"
prepared = (
    ctx.table("events")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .select("dt", "region", "event_id", "user_id", "amount", "event_ts")
)

prepared.write_parquet_with_options(
    "s3://bucket/curated/events/",
    options=ParquetWriterOptions(
        compression="zstd(4)",
        statistics_enabled="page",
        max_row_group_size=1_000_000,
        created_by="my-pipeline/1.2.3 datafusion-python",
    ),
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(
        partition_by=["dt", "region"],
        sort_by=[col("event_ts").sort(ascending=True)],
    ),
)
```

---

# 19.11 Writer config object pattern

```python id="w4vbik"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

from datafusion.dataframe import DataFrameWriteOptions, ParquetColumnOptions, ParquetWriterOptions


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParquetOutputPolicy:
    compression: str = "zstd(4)"
    max_row_group_size: int = 1_000_000
    statistics_enabled: Literal["none", "chunk", "page"] = "page"
    dictionary_enabled: bool = True
    single_file_output: bool = False
    partition_by: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    created_by: str = "datafusion-python"
    sort_by: tuple = ()


def build_parquet_writer_options(policy: ParquetOutputPolicy) -> ParquetWriterOptions:
    return ParquetWriterOptions(
        compression=policy.compression,
        max_row_group_size=policy.max_row_group_size,
        statistics_enabled=policy.statistics_enabled,
        dictionary_enabled=policy.dictionary_enabled,
        created_by=policy.created_by,
    )


def build_write_options(policy: ParquetOutputPolicy) -> DataFrameWriteOptions:
    return DataFrameWriteOptions(
        single_file_output=policy.single_file_output,
        partition_by=list(policy.partition_by) if policy.partition_by else None,
        sort_by=list(policy.sort_by) if policy.sort_by else None,
    )


def write_curated_parquet(df, path: str, policy: ParquetOutputPolicy) -> None:
    df.write_parquet_with_options(
        path,
        options=build_parquet_writer_options(policy),
        write_options=build_write_options(policy),
    )
```

Agent rule:

```text id="y695ik"
Encode writer defaults as policy objects.
Do not scatter compression/partitioning/overwrite behavior across call sites.
```

---

# 19.12 Overwrite / append / replace semantics

## 19.12.1 File-path writes

`write_parquet(...)` writes to a path. File/directory overwrite behavior can depend on target filesystem/object-store and DataFusion writer behavior. Treat path existence semantics as part of deployment validation, not as an assumption.

```text id="8qg4vo"
For file/directory writes:
  explicitly decide if output path must be empty
  delete/stage output directory before write if overwrite semantics required
  use atomic staging/rename where filesystem/object store supports it
  object-store rename may be copy+delete, not atomic
```

## 19.12.2 Table writes

For `write_table(...)`, `DataFrameWriteOptions.insert_operation` expresses intended write mode: append, overwrite, or replace. Provider support is not guaranteed. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="8f94mo"
df.write_table(
    "target",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(
        insert_operation=InsertOp.APPEND,
    ),
)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="ds7pgh"
Expose write mode in public APIs:
  append
  overwrite
  replace
  fail-if-exists
  staging-then-commit

Validate actual provider behavior in integration tests.
```

---

# 19.13 Downstream compatibility validation

## 19.13.1 Compatibility dimensions

```text id="ot83x2"
Validate downstream support for:
  compression codec
  compression level syntax/effect
  writer_version 1.0 vs 2.0
  dictionary encoding
  byte_stream_split encoding
  page statistics
  page index / column index
  bloom filters
  Arrow schema metadata
  partitioned directory layout
  single-file vs multi-file output
  nested column paths for column-specific options
```

The Parquet format-options page lists compression, encoding, dictionary, statistics, bloom filters, page/index, row-group, write-batch, writer-version, Arrow metadata, created-by, and truncation options; many are column-specific, and unsupported options raise errors while nonexistent column-specific options are ignored. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html))

---

## 19.13.2 Consumer validation helper

```python id="xvd4s4"
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

def validate_parquet_readable_by_pyarrow(path: str) -> None:
    dataset = pq.ParquetDataset(path)
    schema = dataset.schema
    table = dataset.read()
    assert table.num_columns == len(schema.names)
```

Optional cross-engine validation matrix:

```text id="73mgpn"
Readers:
  pyarrow
  duckdb
  spark
  polars
  downstream warehouse/lakehouse engine
  production application reader
```

Agent rule:

```text id="yu8oep"
Do not introduce writer_version=2.0, byte_stream_split, bloom filters, uncommon codecs, or metadata-stripping without downstream validation.
```

# 19.14 Testing patterns

## 19.14.1 Basic Parquet roundtrip

```python id="55qmy8"
def test_write_parquet_roundtrip(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    df = ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    df.write_parquet(path, compression="zstd", compression_level=4)

    actual = ctx.read_parquet(path).to_pydict()

    assert actual == {"x": [1, 2, 3]}
```

---

## 19.14.2 Advanced options roundtrip

```python id="i10as1"
def test_write_parquet_options_roundtrip(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    df = ctx.from_pydict({
        "event_type": ["click", "view"],
        "amount": [10.0, 20.0],
    })

    options = ParquetWriterOptions(
        compression="zstd(5)",
        statistics_enabled="page",
        dictionary_enabled=True,
        max_row_group_size=1024,
        column_specific_options={
            "event_type": ParquetColumnOptions(dictionary_enabled=True),
            "amount": ParquetColumnOptions(compression="zstd(3)"),
        },
    )

    df.write_parquet_with_options(path, options)

    actual = ctx.read_parquet(path).sort("event_type").to_pydict()

    assert actual["event_type"] == ["click", "view"]
```

---

## 19.14.3 Partitioned output smoke test

```python id="7w609v"
def test_partitioned_parquet_write(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events_out"

    df = ctx.from_pydict({
        "dt": ["2026-01-01", "2026-01-01", "2026-01-02"],
        "region": ["us", "ca", "us"],
        "amount": [1, 2, 3],
    })

    df.write_parquet(
        path,
        compression="zstd",
        write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(
            partition_by=["dt", "region"],
        ),
    )

    read_back = ctx.read_parquet(
        path,
        table_partition_cols=[("dt", "utf8"), ("region", "utf8")],
    )

    assert read_back.count() == 3
```

---

## 19.14.4 Single-file output test

```python id="k099l3"
def test_single_file_output(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "single.parquet"

    ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]}).write_parquet(
        path,
        write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(single_file_output=True),
```
