# 19.15 Performance tuning workflow

```text id="vs71ub"
1. Pick output policy:
     codec
     row group size
     partition layout
     sort layout
     dictionary/statistics policy

2. Write representative data:
     small sample
     production-scale sample

3. Measure:
     write time
     output bytes
     downstream read time
     predicate-pruned query time
     memory/spill behavior

4. Vary:
     zstd level
     max_row_group_size
     partition_by keys
     sort_by keys
     dictionary_enabled
     statistics_enabled

5. Validate:
     downstream reader compatibility
     schema preservation
     null behavior
     partition discovery
```

---

# 19.16 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: materialize to Pandas before writing Parquet

```python id="nmdjg0"
pdf = df.to_pandas()
pdf.to_parquet("events.parquet")
```

Correct:

```python id="i4vu9f"
df.write_parquet("events.parquet", compression="zstd")
```

---

## Anti-pattern: unpartitioned massive lake output

```python id="tfly61"
df.write_parquet("s3://bucket/events/", compression="zstd")
```

Correct when partition filters are common:

```python id="6jqf12"
df.write_parquet(
    "s3://bucket/events/",
    compression="zstd",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(partition_by=["dt", "region"]),
)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: high-cardinality partitioning

```python id="o2zt8b"
df.write_parquet(
    "output/",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(partition_by=["user_id"]),
)
```

Correct:

```text id="frrscj"
Partition by low/moderate-cardinality query predicates:
  dt
  region
  tenant_id if bounded
  product_category

Do not partition by:
  user_id
  event_id
  uuid
  timestamp at high precision
```

---

## Anti-pattern: compression without consumer validation

```python id="rsrlq7"
df.write_parquet_with_options(
    "output.parquet",
    ParquetWriterOptions(
        compression="brotli(11)",
        encoding="byte_stream_split",
        writer_version="2.0",
    ),
)
```

Correct:

```text id="fqlh6w"
Validate every downstream reader before deploying non-default compression/encoding/writer_version features.
```

---

## Anti-pattern: leaving overwrite semantics implicit

```python id="wg7rvc"
df.write_parquet("output/events/")
```

Correct:

```text id="jjim4v"
Declare:
  fail if output exists
  delete then write
  staging path then commit
  append mode
  table overwrite mode
```

For table writes:

```python id="c64lst"
df.write_table(
    "target",
    write_options=DataFrameWriteOptions(insert_operation=InsertOp.OVERWRITE),
)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: disabling statistics globally

```python id="jxd3r0"
options = ParquetWriterOptions(statistics_enabled="none")
```

Correct unless sensitive data or consumer constraint requires otherwise:

```python id="2k5ko0"
options = ParquetWriterOptions(statistics_enabled="page")
```

Statistics are important for pruning and read efficiency; DataFusion’s Parquet options document statistics as a configurable global or column-specific setting and list row-group/page pruning-related options. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/format_options.html))

---

# 19.17 Deployment checklist

```text id="vlq7ux"
Write API:
  [ ] Use df.write_parquet for common Parquet output.
  [ ] Use df.write_parquet_with_options for advanced Parquet layout.
  [ ] Avoid Python materialization before durable writes.
  [ ] Treat writes as terminal side effects.

Compression:
  [ ] Default to ZSTD unless compatibility dictates otherwise.
  [ ] Set compression level deliberately.
  [ ] Use Snappy for conservative interoperability.
  [ ] Use Uncompressed only for debugging/legacy cases.
  [ ] Validate Brotli/LZ4/LZ4_RAW support downstream.

ParquetWriterOptions:
  [ ] max_row_group_size chosen with memory/read tradeoff.
  [ ] statistics_enabled not disabled accidentally.
  [ ] dictionary_enabled policy documented.
  [ ] writer_version validated downstream.
  [ ] skip_arrow_metadata only if needed.
  [ ] column_specific_options used for special columns only.
  [ ] bloom filters enabled only after reader validation.

DataFrameWriteOptions:
  [ ] partition_by declared or explicitly omitted.
  [ ] single_file_output declared or explicitly omitted.
  [ ] sort_by declared when physical order matters.
  [ ] insert_operation declared for table writes.
  [ ] provider support validated.

Partitioning:
  [ ] Partition by query predicates.
  [ ] Avoid high-cardinality keys.
  [ ] Test readback with table_partition_cols.
  [ ] Document directory layout.

Overwrite/append:
  [ ] Public write APIs expose write mode.
  [ ] File path existence behavior tested.
  [ ] Table provider insert semantics tested.

Compatibility:
  [ ] PyArrow readback test.
  [ ] DuckDB/Polars/Spark/warehouse readback when relevant.
  [ ] Schema and null behavior verified.
  [ ] Compression/encoding support verified.
```

---

## 19.18 Section compression for LLM agents

```text id="yjs2lo"
Terminal write APIs:
  df.write_parquet(path, compression=Compression.ZSTD, compression_level=None, write_options=None)
  df.write_parquet_with_options(path, options=ParquetWriterOptions(...), write_options=None)
  df.write_table(table_name, write_options=None)
  df.write_csv(path, with_header=False, write_options=None)
  df.write_json(path, write_options=None)

Parquet compression:
  uncompressed
  snappy
  gzip
  brotli
  lz4
  lz4_raw
  zstd
  LZO excluded in write_parquet docs

Defaults:
  write_parquet default compression = ZSTD
  ZSTD recommended level range = 1..22; default write_parquet level = 4
  ParquetWriterOptions default compression = zstd(3)

DataFrameWriteOptions:
  insert_operation: InsertOp | None
  single_file_output: bool = False
  partition_by: str | Sequence[str] | None
  sort_by: Expr | SortExpr | Sequence[...] | None

InsertOp:
  APPEND
  OVERWRITE
  REPLACE

ParquetWriterOptions:
  data_pagesize_limit
  write_batch_size
  writer_version
  skip_arrow_metadata
  compression
  compression_level
  dictionary_enabled
  dictionary_page_size_limit
  statistics_enabled
  max_row_group_size
  created_by
  column_index_truncate_length
  statistics_truncate_length
  data_page_row_count_limit
  encoding
  bloom_filter_on_write
  bloom_filter_fpp
  bloom_filter_ndv
  allow_single_file_parallelism
  maximum_parallel_row_group_writers
  maximum_buffered_record_batches_per_stream
  column_specific_options

ParquetColumnOptions:
  encoding
  dictionary_enabled
  compression
  statistics_enabled
  bloom_filter_enabled
  bloom_filter_fpp
  bloom_filter_ndv

Best practices:
  choose ZSTD for balanced production output
  use Snappy for maximum legacy compatibility
  expose partition_by and write mode in public APIs
  avoid high-cardinality output partitioning
  validate downstream support for codec/encoding/writer_version/bloom filters
  keep statistics enabled unless privacy/compatibility requires otherwise
  do not materialize to Pandas before writing
  test write-read roundtrips and consumer compatibility
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 20) Arrow interoperability and zero-copy exchange

This section follows the dense, agent-facing technical-reference style of the Cyclopts source material. 

## 20.0 Core interoperability invariant

DataFusion Python uses Apache Arrow as the memory/interchange boundary between Python and the Rust DataFusion engine.

```text id="lr02w6"
Python object / Arrow-compatible producer
  -> Arrow C Data / C Stream / PyCapsule interface
  -> DataFusion Python binding
  -> Rust DataFusion execution engine
  -> Arrow RecordBatch stream
  -> Python Arrow-compatible consumer
```

The Arrow C data interface defines a small, stable set of C definitions for Arrow-format columnar data interchange across runtimes, and Arrow’s PyCapsule interface specifies how Python libraries expose those C interface structs through dunder methods such as `__arrow_c_stream__` without forcing every producer/consumer to depend on PyArrow-specific private import/export methods. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface.html)) ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html))

---

## 20.1 DataFusion-specific Arrow contract

DataFusion Python supports Arrow import through `SessionContext.from_arrow(...)` and Arrow export through `DataFrame.__arrow_c_stream__(...)`. The official DataFusion Arrow IO guide states that `from_arrow` accepts objects implementing `__arrow_c_stream__` or `__arrow_c_array__`, and that DataFusion DataFrames implement `__arrow_c_stream__` so Arrow-compatible Python libraries can import them directly. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/io/arrow.html))

```python id="f1siwp"
from datafusion import SessionContext, col, lit
import pyarrow as pa

ctx = SessionContext()

source = pa.table({
    "a": [1, 2, 3],
    "b": [4, 5, 6],
})

df = ctx.from_arrow(source)

out = df.select(
    (col("a") * lit(1.5)).alias("c"),
    lit("df").alias("d"),
)

# Export through Arrow C stream into PyArrow.
table = pa.table(out)
```

The DataFusion guide notes that `pa.table(df)` works because the DataFrame implements the Arrow C stream interface, but it materializes the entire table; for streaming, use `pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html))

---

## 20.2 Import pathways: Arrow → DataFusion

## 20.2.1 `ctx.from_arrow(...)`

### Signature

```python id="vvlh6m"
ctx.from_arrow(
    data: ArrowStreamExportable | ArrowArrayExportable,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> DataFrame
```

`SessionContext.from_arrow(...)` creates a DataFrame from any object implementing `__arrow_c_stream__` or `__arrow_c_array__`; for `__arrow_c_array__`, the object must return a struct array. DataFusion docs list PyArrow, Polars, Pandas, and other Arrow-compatible sources as possible inputs. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

```python id="5do64l"
df = ctx.from_arrow(pa.table({"x": [1, 2, 3]}))
```

### Accepted categories

```text id="vhf6dc"
PyArrow:
  pa.Table
  pa.RecordBatch
  pa.RecordBatchReader
  StructArray-compatible Arrow array

Other Arrow-compatible:
  object with __arrow_c_stream__()
  object with __arrow_c_array__() returning StructArray
  Polars/Pandas objects where supported through Arrow export
```

The Arrow IO guide explicitly lists PyArrow Array, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, and Table as common imports, with the Array caveat that it must return a struct array. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/io/arrow.html))

---

## 20.2.2 Import `pyarrow.Table`

```python id="od1aws"
import pyarrow as pa

table = pa.table({
    "user_id": [1, 2, 3],
    "amount": [10.0, 20.5, 30.0],
})

df = ctx.from_arrow(table)
```

Use when:

```text id="sv1ftb"
schema already Arrow-native
input has multiple columns
source came from PyArrow dataset/read path
DataFusion should plan/query over existing Arrow memory
```

---

## 20.2.3 Import `pyarrow.RecordBatch`

```python id="js4qtj"
batch = pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({
    "user_id": [1, 2],
    "amount": [10.0, 20.5],
})

df = ctx.from_arrow(batch)
```

Use when:

```text id="6pfrte"
single batch fixture
stream chunk already available
low-overhead unit test
adapter receives batches from another Arrow producer
```

---

## 20.2.4 Import `pyarrow.RecordBatchReader`

```python id="gd6zls"
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_batches(
    pa.schema([
        ("user_id", pa.int64()),
        ("amount", pa.float64()),
    ]),
    [
        pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"user_id": [1], "amount": [10.0]}),
        pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"user_id": [2], "amount": [20.0]}),
    ],
)

df = ctx.from_arrow(reader)
```

Use when:

```text id="d347uk"
producer is streaming batches
avoid assembling full Table before import
data source already exposes RecordBatchReader
pipeline should remain batch-oriented
```

---

## 20.2.5 Import Arrow stream-exporting object

```python id="5608wz"
class ArrowStreamSource:
    def __arrow_c_stream__(self):
        return some_arrow_array_stream_capsule

df = ctx.from_arrow(ArrowStreamSource())
```

Use when:

```text id="z5wbpw"
custom library exposes Arrow PyCapsule protocol
producer is not PyArrow-specific
producer avoids pandas/numpy materialization
Rust/C/C++/Polars/cuDF-like source can export Arrow stream
```

DataFusion’s contributor FFI guide says DataFusion Python reuses Arrow C Stream Interface definitions for importing/exporting tables and that any Python package supporting Arrow C Stream reading can work with DataFusion Python. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/contributor-guide/ffi.html))

---

## 20.2.6 Import from Pandas / Polars via context helpers

```python id="we15uc"
df_from_pandas = ctx.from_pandas(pandas_df)
df_from_polars = ctx.from_polars(polars_df)
```

`SessionContext.from_pandas(...)` and `SessionContext.from_polars(...)` create DataFusion DataFrames from Pandas and Polars DataFrames respectively. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

Agent rule:

```text id="6s2cne"
Use from_arrow(...) when you can control Arrow interchange explicitly.
Use from_pandas/from_polars for ergonomic boundary handoff from existing code.
Avoid repeated Pandas/Polars/DataFusion round trips.
```

---

# 20.3 Export pathways: DataFusion → Arrow

## 20.3.1 `df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None)`

### Signature

```python id="3avlfg"
df.__arrow_c_stream__(
    requested_schema: object | None = None,
) -> object
```

`DataFrame.__arrow_c_stream__()` exports a DataFrame as an Arrow C Stream PyCapsule. DataFusion executes the DataFrame using streaming APIs and exposes record batches incrementally, so the full result set is not materialized in memory. If `requested_schema` is supplied, DataFusion supports simple projection/reordering of existing columns, but not renaming, computed expressions, or type coercion through that interface. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="wqahzt"
capsule = df.__arrow_c_stream__()
```

Agent rules:

```text id="029hm7"
__arrow_c_stream__:
  terminal execution boundary
  streaming, not collect()
  returns PyCapsule wrapping ArrowArrayStream
  use requested_schema only for projection/reordering
  do computed expressions before export with df.select(...)
```

---

## 20.3.2 PyArrow streaming consumer

```python id="x0pj07"
import pyarrow as pa

reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)

for batch in reader:
    # batch is pyarrow.RecordBatch
    process(batch)
```

DataFusion’s DataFrame guide recommends `pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)` to create a PyArrow reader without materializing all batches; it also states that batches are produced on demand through the streaming protocol. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html))

Use when:

```text id="5s5nj0"
large result
Arrow-native sink
file/network streaming writer
backpressure-aware pipeline
avoid Python list[RecordBatch] collection
```

---

## 20.3.3 Full PyArrow materialization

```python id="sc71ti"
table = pa.table(df)
```

`pa.table(df)` collects the entire DataFusion DataFrame eagerly into a PyArrow Table; DataFusion docs explicitly contrast this with `RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)` for streaming. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html))

Use only when:

```text id="d5ggd7"
result is bounded
consumer requires pyarrow.Table
schema-level postprocessing needs Table
unit test / notebook inspection
```

Avoid when:

```text id="mzg6ug"
result cardinality unknown
service endpoint
large scan/join/aggregate result
memory budget is constrained
```

---

## 20.3.4 DataFusion-native batch iteration

```python id="uq075f"
for rb in df:
    # rb is datafusion.RecordBatch
    pa_batch = rb.to_pyarrow()
    process(pa_batch)
```

DataFrame objects are iterable and yield `datafusion.RecordBatch` instances lazily; each batch exposes `to_pyarrow()`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html))

Async:

```python id="f137sn"
async for rb in df:
    await process_async(rb.to_pyarrow())
```

The DataFrame API defines both `__iter__()` and `__aiter__()` returning lazy record-batch iterators. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

## 20.3.5 Direct stream API

```python id="mfgsd1"
stream = df.execute_stream()

for rb in stream:
    process(rb.to_pyarrow())
```

`execute_stream()` executes the DataFrame and returns a `RecordBatchStream`; `execute_stream_partitioned()` returns one stream per partition. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

```python id="cpkac9"
streams = df.execute_stream_partitioned()

for partition_id, stream in enumerate(streams):
    for rb in stream:
        sink(partition_id, rb.to_pyarrow())
```

---

# 20.4 Arrow C Data Interface and PyCapsule mechanics

## 20.4.1 Interface concepts

```text id="bwq45a"
Arrow C Data Interface:
  ArrowArray
  ArrowSchema

Arrow C Stream Interface:
  ArrowArrayStream

Arrow PyCapsule Interface:
  __arrow_c_array__()
  __arrow_c_stream__()
  __arrow_c_device_array__()
```

The Arrow C data interface defines standard C structs for Arrow columnar data interchange, and the PyCapsule interface describes how Python libraries expose those structs without requiring PyArrow as a hard interchange dependency. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface.html)) ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html))

## 20.4.2 DataFusion mapping

```text id="g78vjw"
DataFusion import:
  ctx.from_arrow(obj)
    obj.__arrow_c_stream__() -> ArrowArrayStream PyCapsule
    or obj.__arrow_c_array__() -> ArrowArray/ArrowSchema PyCapsule pair

DataFusion export:
  df.__arrow_c_stream__() -> ArrowArrayStream PyCapsule

PyArrow consumption:
  pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
  pa.table(df)
```

---

# 20.5 Zero-copy model

## 20.5.1 What “zero-copy where possible” means

```text id="yajpws"
Zero-copy possible when:
  producer and consumer both understand Arrow memory
  schema/layout is compatible
  no type coercion required
  no computed projection required at the interchange boundary
  consumer accepts streaming batches directly
  buffers can be referenced without reshaping into another memory model

Copy likely/required when:
  converting to pandas/native Python objects
  requested schema requires type coercion
  computed columns are created at export boundary
  multiple chunks must become contiguous arrays
  consumer requires a different physical layout
  Python lists/dicts are produced
```

PyArrow’s Pandas integration docs state that zero-copy Pandas/NumPy conversion is only possible under specific conditions, including compatible integer/float/timestamp types, no nulls, and single-chunk arrays; multiple chunks require a copy because Pandas requires contiguous memory. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/pandas.html))

---

## 20.5.2 DataFusion-specific zero-copy boundaries

```text id="uj4omd"
Likely low/zero-copy:
  ctx.from_arrow(pa.Table / RecordBatch / RecordBatchReader)
  ctx.from_arrow(object with Arrow C stream)
  pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
  Arrow-compatible consumer reading df.__arrow_c_stream__()

Materializing / copy-heavy:
  df.to_pandas()
  df.to_pydict()
  df.to_pylist()
  pa.table(df) for full table assembly
  Python UDF with as_py() loops
```

The DataFusion DataFrame guide explicitly labels `__arrow_c_stream__` support as zero-copy, lazy streaming into Arrow-based libraries, and notes that `pa.table(df)` collects the whole DataFrame eagerly. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html))

---

# 20.6 Interop with PyArrow

## 20.6.1 DataFusion → PyArrow streaming

```python id="n1rrbc"
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)

for batch in reader:
    assert isinstance(batch, pa.RecordBatch)
    # Write, transform, or pass downstream.
```

## 20.6.2 DataFusion → PyArrow Table

```python id="eztwds"
table = pa.table(df)
```

## 20.6.3 PyArrow → DataFusion

```python id="8y2g1z"
table = pa.table({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
df = ctx.from_arrow(table)
```

## 20.6.4 PyArrow record-batch reader roundtrip

```python id="b5j5ab"
schema = pa.schema([("x", pa.int64())])
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_batches(
    schema,
    [
        pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2]}),
        pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"x": [3, 4]}),
    ],
)

df = ctx.from_arrow(reader)

out_reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
for batch in out_reader:
    ...
```

---

# 20.7 Interop with Pandas

## 20.7.1 Pandas → DataFusion

```python id="qvw275"
df = ctx.from_pandas(pandas_df)
```

## 20.7.2 DataFusion → Pandas

```python id="u2sf7d"
pdf = df.limit(10_000).to_pandas()
```

`to_pandas()` executes the DataFrame and converts it into a Pandas DataFrame. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

Agent rules:

```text id="lalz1m"
Use Pandas interop for:
  notebook display
  legacy Pandas code boundary
  plotting
  small bounded results

Avoid Pandas interop for:
  large/unknown-cardinality results
  streaming services
  durable storage writes
  inner pipeline transformations
```

Pandas conversion is not generally zero-copy; Arrow’s Pandas docs list strict conditions for zero-copy conversion and state that multiple chunks always require a copy because Pandas requires contiguous memory. ([arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/pandas.html))

---

# 20.8 Interop with Polars

## 20.8.1 Polars → DataFusion

```python id="tm96fx"
df = ctx.from_polars(polars_df)
```

`from_polars(...)` creates a DataFusion DataFrame from a Polars DataFrame. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

## 20.8.2 DataFusion → Polars

```python id="vk8ozi"
pldf = df.limit(1_000_000).to_polars()
```

`to_polars()` executes a DataFrame and converts it into a Polars DataFrame. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

Agent rules:

```text id="c7wsan"
Use Polars interop for:
  downstream Polars-only operations
  bounded handoff
  integration with existing Polars pipelines

Prefer Arrow streaming when:
  result is large
  consumer accepts Arrow batches
  avoiding full materialization matters
```

---

# 20.9 Other Arrow-aware libraries

Any Python library that understands Arrow C Stream / PyCapsule input can consume a DataFusion DataFrame through `__arrow_c_stream__`. DataFusion’s contributor FFI guide says any Python package that supports reading the Arrow C Stream interface can work with DataFusion Python out of the box. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/contributor-guide/ffi.html))

```python id="6lfzut"
# Generic pseudo-pattern.
consumer.consume_arrow_stream(df)  # consumer internally calls __arrow_c_stream__()
```

Examples of library classes that often support Arrow interop patterns:

```text id="rbd1fi"
PyArrow
Polars
Pandas with Arrow-backed interop paths
cuDF / GPU Arrow consumers where supported
Rust/PyO3 extensions
C/C++ extensions
DataFrame protocol / Narwhals-style adapters
custom storage writers accepting Arrow streams
```

Agent rule:

```text id="k3am5d"
Prefer Arrow stream handoff over library-specific materialization when the consumer can accept Arrow C Stream.
```

---

# 20.10 Memory model: streaming vs full materialization

## 20.10.1 Streaming

```python id="miz9na"
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
for batch in reader:
    sink.write(batch)
```

```python id="zv911i"
for rb in df.execute_stream():
    sink.write(rb.to_pyarrow())
```

Characteristics:

```text id="uiztsm"
incremental
batch-oriented
bounded peak memory relative to batch size/operator state
consumer pulls batches
good for service/file/network sinks
no Python list of all batches
```

## 20.10.2 Full materialization

```python id="rnxvbj"
batches = df.collect()
table = df.to_arrow_table()
pdf = df.to_pandas()
rows = df.to_pylist()
```

Characteristics:

```text id="ymkm5f"
entire result in memory
Python object overhead for pydict/pylist/pandas
simpler API
good for tests/small outputs
dangerous for unknown cardinality
```

`collect()` executes and collects results into memory as a list of `pyarrow.RecordBatch`; conversion APIs such as `to_arrow_table`, `to_pandas`, `to_polars`, `to_pydict`, and `to_pylist` execute and materialize results in their target representation. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

# 20.11 Requested schema on Arrow stream export

```python id="0si94b"
requested = pa.schema([
    ("amount", pa.float64()),
    ("user_id", pa.int64()),
])

capsule = df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=requested)
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(capsule)
```

`requested_schema` may be a `pyarrow.Schema` or Arrow C Schema PyCapsule, and DataFusion attempts to align output fields/order with that schema. Only simple projections and reordering of existing columns are supported; renaming, computed expressions, and type coercion are not supported through this interface. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

Correct for computed exports:

```python id="548r8b"
prepared = df.select(
    (col("amount") * lit(100)).alias("amount_cents"),
    col("user_id"),
)

reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(prepared)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="6pt7tk"
Use requested_schema for selecting/reordering existing columns only.
Use DataFrame.select/cast/alias before export for all computed/renamed/coerced outputs.
```

---

# 20.12 GIL and Python UDF considerations

Scalar Python UDFs receive one or more PyArrow arrays and return one PyArrow array; they operate on entire record batches at a time. DataFusion’s UDF guide recommends using PyArrow compute functions where possible and warns that converting to Python objects and reconstructing arrays is one of the slowest approaches. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/common-operations/udf-and-udfa.html))

```python id="4h5ct8"
# Fast-ish: vectorized Arrow compute.
def add_one(x: pa.Array) -> pa.Array:
    return pc.add(x, 1)

# Slow: per-element Python object conversion.
def add_one_slow(x: pa.Array) -> pa.Array:
    return pa.array([
        v.as_py() + 1 if v.as_py() is not None else None
        for v in x
    ])
```

Historical DataFusion Python package docs describe the engine as achieving zero-copy between Python and the execution engine, with UDF/UDAF/result collection costs apart from locking the GIL when running Python operations. Treat Python UDFs as Python execution boundaries that can contend on the GIL and reduce effective parallelism. ([pypi.org](https://pypi.org/project/datafusion/0.4.0/))

Agent rules:

```text id="12zwxb"
Built-ins first:
  datafusion.functions
  Expr methods
  SQL built-ins

Then Arrow compute:
  pyarrow.compute in scalar UDF
  batch/vectorized operations

Avoid:
  per-row Python loops
  v.as_py() in hot paths
  Python object lists for large arrays
  network calls inside UDF
  hidden global mutable state

Use Rust-backed UDFs when:
  hot path
  complex algorithm
  Python GIL limits throughput
  per-row logic unavoidable
```

---

# 20.13 Import/export decision table

| Need                                           | Recommended path                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| query an existing PyArrow Table                | `ctx.from_arrow(table)`                             |
| query existing PyArrow RecordBatch stream      | `ctx.from_arrow(reader)`                            |
| query Pandas input once                        | `ctx.from_pandas(pdf)`                              |
| query Polars input once                        | `ctx.from_polars(pldf)`                             |
| stream DataFusion output to PyArrow            | `pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)`              |
| materialize DataFusion output as PyArrow Table | `pa.table(df)` or `df.to_arrow_table()`             |
| materialize small output as Pandas             | `df.limit(n).to_pandas()`                           |
| materialize small output as Polars             | `df.limit(n).to_polars()`                           |
| hand off large output to Arrow-aware sink      | `df.__arrow_c_stream__()` / `execute_stream()`      |
| test exact tiny output                         | `df.to_pydict()`                                    |
| write durable Parquet                          | `df.write_parquet(...)`, not Pandas materialization |

---

# 20.14 Stable interoperability adapter patterns

## 20.14.1 Arrow stream sink adapter

```python id="h7vt6w"
import pyarrow as pa

def stream_to_arrow_sink(df, sink) -> None:
    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
    for batch in reader:
        sink.write_batch(batch)
```

## 20.14.2 DataFusion-native stream adapter

```python id="5hc7tw"
def stream_to_pyarrow_batches(df):
    for rb in df.execute_stream():
        yield rb.to_pyarrow()
```

## 20.14.3 Bounded Pandas adapter

```python id="1c9iyo"
def to_pandas_bounded(df, *, max_rows: int):
    return df.limit(max_rows).to_pandas()
```

## 20.14.4 Import adapter

```python id="x7pxg4"
def dataframe_from_any_arrow(ctx: SessionContext, obj):
    if hasattr(obj, "__arrow_c_stream__") or hasattr(obj, "__arrow_c_array__"):
        return ctx.from_arrow(obj)
    raise TypeError("Object does not expose Arrow C stream/array protocol")
```

---

# 20.15 Arrow stream output to Parquet without Python table materialization

```python id="flszsf"
# Preferred: DataFusion writer.
df.write_parquet("output/events/", compression="zstd")
```

When a custom writer requires PyArrow batches:

```python id="87bi2b"
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
writer = None

try:
    for batch in reader:
        if writer is None:
            writer = pq.ParquetWriter("output/events.parquet", batch.schema)
        writer.write_batch(batch)
finally:
    if writer is not None:
        writer.close()
```

Agent rule:

```text id="2jtrbv"
Prefer DataFusion write_parquet when possible.
Use PyArrow streaming writer only when custom sink logic requires it.
Avoid pa.table(df) for large writes.
```

---

# 20.16 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: collect before Arrow consumer

```python id="3atqs4"
batches = df.collect()
table = pa.Table.from_batches(batches)
consumer.consume(table)
```

Correct:

```python id="jgipqh"
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
consumer.consume_stream(reader)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: Pandas conversion for large Arrow handoff

```python id="5qfe4l"
pdf = df.to_pandas()
```

Correct:

```python id="6k4ett"
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: compute in `requested_schema`

```python id="yk9bda"
requested = pa.schema([("amount_cents", pa.int64())])
df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=requested)
```

Correct:

```python id="897ggu"
prepared = df.select((col("amount") * lit(100)).cast(pa.int64()).alias("amount_cents"))
reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(prepared)
```

`requested_schema` supports only projection/reordering, not computed expressions, renaming, or type coercion. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

## Anti-pattern: row-wise Python UDF for vectorizable logic

```python id="6ko9r6"
def normalize_email_slow(arr: pa.Array) -> pa.Array:
    return pa.array([x.as_py().strip().lower() for x in arr])
```

Correct:

```python id="ib6rcu"
def normalize_email_fast(arr: pa.Array) -> pa.Array:
    return pc.utf8_lower(pc.utf8_trim_whitespace(arr))
```

---

## Anti-pattern: repeated library round trips

```python id="fx4f65"
pdf = df.to_pandas()
df2 = ctx.from_pandas(pdf)
pldf = df2.to_polars()
df3 = ctx.from_polars(pldf)
```

Correct:

```text id="spzzha"
Choose one execution engine for the main pipeline.
Use one clear handoff boundary.
Use Arrow stream/table as interchange, not repeated materialization.
```

---

# 20.17 Testing patterns

## 20.17.1 PyArrow table import

```python id="j08a12"
def test_from_arrow_table(ctx):
    table = pa.table({"x": [1, 2, 3]})

    df = ctx.from_arrow(table)

    assert df.to_pydict() == {"x": [1, 2, 3]}
```

## 20.17.2 RecordBatchReader import

```python id="4zhkm0"
def test_from_record_batch_reader(ctx):
    schema = pa.schema([("x", pa.int64())])
    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_batches(
        schema,
        [
            pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2]}),
            pa.RecordBatch.from_pydict({"x": [3]}),
        ],
    )

    df = ctx.from_arrow(reader)

    assert df.to_pydict() == {"x": [1, 2, 3]}
```

## 20.17.3 Arrow C stream export

```python id="1sdh0v"
def test_arrow_stream_export(ctx):
    df = ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})

    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
    batches = list(reader)

    assert sum(batch.num_rows for batch in batches) == 3
```

## 20.17.4 Requested schema projection/reordering

```python id="mxahox"
def test_arrow_stream_requested_schema(ctx):
    df = ctx.from_pydict({
        "a": [1, 2],
        "b": [3, 4],
    })

    requested = pa.schema([
        ("b", pa.int64()),
    ])

    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(
        df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=requested)
    )
    table = reader.read_all()

    assert table.schema.names == ["b"]
```

## 20.17.5 Bounded Pandas handoff

```python id="rnxuve"
def test_bounded_pandas(ctx):
    df = ctx.from_pydict({"x": list(range(100))})

    pdf = df.limit(10).to_pandas()

    assert len(pdf) == 10
```

# 20.18 Deployment checklist

```text id="wqfv38"
Import:
  [ ] Use ctx.from_arrow for Arrow-native inputs.
  [ ] Accept __arrow_c_stream__ or __arrow_c_array__ only where intended.
  [ ] Validate __arrow_c_array__ sources return StructArray-compatible data.
  [ ] Use from_pandas/from_polars only at explicit boundaries.

Export:
  [ ] Use pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df) for large Arrow outputs.
  [ ] Use pa.table(df) only for bounded full materialization.
  [ ] Use df.execute_stream() for DataFusion-native streaming.
  [ ] Use async iteration in async services.
  [ ] Use requested_schema only for projection/reordering.

Memory:
  [ ] Avoid collect()/to_pandas()/to_pylist() for unknown-cardinality data.
  [ ] Process RecordBatches incrementally.
  [ ] Release batch references promptly in long-running services.
  [ ] Prefer write_parquet over collect-then-write.

Zero-copy:
  [ ] Do not promise zero-copy for Pandas conversion.
  [ ] Validate consumer memory behavior.
  [ ] Avoid type coercion/renaming/computed expressions at stream-boundary.
  [ ] Keep data Arrow-native across library handoffs.

UDF/GIL:
  [ ] Prefer built-ins.
  [ ] Prefer pyarrow.compute in Python UDFs.
  [ ] Avoid as_py loops.
  [ ] Use Rust-backed UDFs for hot paths.
  [ ] Document UDF batch semantics and GIL risk.

Testing:
  [ ] Test Arrow table import.
  [ ] Test RecordBatchReader import.
  [ ] Test Arrow stream export.
  [ ] Test requested_schema behavior.
  [ ] Test bounded Pandas/Polars handoffs only with row caps.
```

---

## 20.19 Section compression for LLM agents

```text id="7yw205"
Core:
  Arrow C Data Interface = cross-runtime columnar memory ABI.
  Arrow PyCapsule Interface = Python dunder protocol exposing Arrow C structs.
  DataFusion uses Arrow C Stream for Python/Rust data exchange.

Import:
  ctx.from_arrow(data, name=None) -> DataFrame
  data must implement:
    __arrow_c_stream__()
    or __arrow_c_array__() returning StructArray-compatible data

Common imports:
  pyarrow.Table
  pyarrow.RecordBatch
  pyarrow.RecordBatchReader
  Arrow-compatible Polars/Pandas/other objects

Export:
  df.__arrow_c_stream__(requested_schema=None) -> PyCapsule[ArrowArrayStream]
  pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df) -> streaming PyArrow reader
  pa.table(df) -> eager full PyArrow Table materialization
  for rb in df -> lazy datafusion.RecordBatch
  async for rb in df -> async lazy batches
  df.execute_stream() -> RecordBatchStream
  df.execute_stream_partitioned() -> per-partition streams

requested_schema:
  supports selecting/reordering existing columns
  does not support renaming
  does not support computed expressions
  does not support type coercion

Interop:
  PyArrow:
    ctx.from_arrow(pa.Table/Batch/Reader)
    pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(df)
    pa.table(df) only when bounded

  Pandas:
    ctx.from_pandas(pdf)
    df.limit(n).to_pandas()
    not generally zero-copy; copies often required

  Polars:
    ctx.from_polars(pldf)
    df.limit(n).to_polars()

Memory:
  streaming = bounded batch flow
  collect/to_pandas/to_pylist = full materialization
  zero-copy possible only when layouts are compatible
  Pandas conversion has strict zero-copy limits

UDF/GIL:
  Python UDFs receive PyArrow arrays and return PyArrow arrays
  batch-oriented, but Python execution can lock/contend on GIL
  use datafusion.functions and pyarrow.compute first
  avoid as_py loops
  use Rust-backed functions for hot paths

Best practices:
  keep pipelines Arrow-native
  use streaming Arrow consumers for large outputs
  materialize only at explicit bounded boundaries
  avoid repeated Pandas/Polars/DataFusion round trips
  prefer DataFusion write_parquet for durable large writes
```
# DataFusion Advanced — 21) Substrait interoperability

This section follows the dense, agent-facing technical-reference style of the Cyclopts source material. 

## 21.0 Core interoperability invariant

Substrait is a cross-language format for describing compute operations on structured data; its goal is interoperability across languages and execution systems. The Substrait project describes the spec as a consistent declaration of common operations, custom operations, and serialized representations, with use cases including communicating a compute plan between a SQL parser and an execution engine, serializing views for reuse across systems, submitting a plan to different engines, and building plan-visualization tooling. ([substrait.io][1])

```text id="y4z0c8"
DataFusion SQL / DataFrame API
  -> DataFusion LogicalPlan
  -> Substrait Plan
  -> bytes / JSON / file
  -> another process / engine / test artifact
  -> Substrait Plan
  -> DataFusion LogicalPlan
  -> DataFrame execution
```

DataFusion Python exposes Substrait support through `datafusion.substrait`, with `Producer`, `Consumer`, `Plan`, and `Serde` classes. The module documentation states that it provides support for using Substrait with DataFusion. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

---

## 21.1 Object model map

| Object     | Role                                     |           Primary direction | Core APIs                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Producer` | DataFusion logical plan → Substrait plan |                      export | `to_substrait_plan(...)`                                                                                         |
| `Consumer` | Substrait plan → DataFusion logical plan |                      import | `from_substrait_plan(...)`                                                                                       |
| `Plan`     | Encodable Substrait plan wrapper         |              representation | `encode()`, `to_json()`, `from_json(...)`                                                                        |
| `Serde`    | SQL-to-Substrait serialization helpers   | file/bytes/plan convenience | `serialize(...)`, `serialize_bytes(...)`, `serialize_to_plan(...)`, `deserialize(...)`, `deserialize_bytes(...)` |

The official DataFusion Python API documents exactly these classes: `Consumer` generates logical plans from Substrait plans, `Producer` generates Substrait plans from logical plans, `Plan` is an encodable Substrait plan wrapper, and `Serde` provides Substrait serialization/deserialization helpers. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="gvb260"
from datafusion import SessionContext
from datafusion.substrait import Consumer, Plan, Producer, Serde
```

---

## 21.2 Why Substrait matters

```text id="wx079v"
Value case:
  portable relational plan representation
  SQL parser / planner decoupling from execution engine
  query-plan persistence
  cross-engine plan exchange
  logical-plan compatibility testing
  generated-query artifact storage
  plan visualization / inspection
  stable-ish interchange layer beyond string SQL
```

Substrait’s own docs list benefits such as avoiding pairwise integration protocols between every system, enabling engines to be swapped into an ecosystem, enabling heterogeneous execution environments, and allowing text-form plans to be inspected without a visualizer. ([substrait.io][1])

Agent framing:

```text id="hc7o9i"
SQL string:
  human-readable query source
  dialect-sensitive
  requires parsing every time
  may lose planner-specific semantics

DataFusion LogicalPlan:
  DataFusion-native logical IR
  Python object
  version/context/catalog sensitive

Substrait Plan:
  portable structured plan artifact
  binary and JSON encodable
  designed for cross-system exchange
  still subject to feature/type/function compatibility
```

---

# 21.3 `Producer`: DataFusion `LogicalPlan` → Substrait `Plan`

## 21.3.1 Signature

```python id="fteol9"
Producer.to_substrait_plan(
    logical_plan: datafusion.plan.LogicalPlan,
    ctx: datafusion.context.SessionContext,
) -> Plan
```

`Producer.to_substrait_plan(...)` converts a DataFusion `LogicalPlan` to a Substrait `Plan`; it requires both the logical plan and the `SessionContext`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="o26q4c"
from datafusion import SessionContext, col, lit, functions as f
from datafusion.substrait import Producer

ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

df = (
    ctx.table("events")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .aggregate(
        [col("country")],
        [f.count_star().alias("n_rows"), f.sum(col("amount")).alias("gross_amount")],
    )
)

logical_plan = df.logical_plan()
substrait_plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(logical_plan, ctx)
```

## 21.3.2 Export flow

```text id="daafdx"
DataFrame builder:
  df = ctx.table(...).filter(...).aggregate(...)

Extract plan:
  logical_plan = df.logical_plan()

Produce Substrait:
  substrait_plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(logical_plan, ctx)

Encode:
  bytes_payload = substrait_plan.encode()
  json_payload = substrait_plan.to_json()
```

Agent rule:

```text id="3509ux"
Use Producer when the query already exists as a DataFrame/LogicalPlan.
Use Serde.serialize_* when the source artifact is SQL text.
```

---

# 21.4 `Plan`: encoded/JSON Substrait representation

## 21.4.1 Constructor rule

```python id="2j4ylf"
Plan(plan_internal)
```

The `Plan` constructor is documented but not intended for direct end-user use; users should create `Plan` objects via `Serde` or `Producer`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Agent rule:

```text id="fgx8sn"
Do not instantiate Plan directly.
Create Plan via:
  Producer.to_substrait_plan(...)
  Serde.serialize_to_plan(...)
  Plan.from_json(...)
  Serde.deserialize(...)
  Serde.deserialize_bytes(...)
```

---

## 21.4.2 `Plan.encode()`

```python id="1i1kdv"
payload: bytes = substrait_plan.encode()
```

`Plan.encode()` encodes the Substrait plan to bytes. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Use for:

```text id="baf0xo"
database/blob storage
message queues
artifact files
cache keys / content hashes
binary plan interchange
```

Hashing example:

```python id="ryic6h"
import hashlib

plan_bytes = substrait_plan.encode()
plan_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(plan_bytes).hexdigest()
```

---

## 21.4.3 `Plan.to_json()`

```python id="npueiu"
json_text: str = substrait_plan.to_json()
```

`Plan.to_json()` returns a JSON representation of the Substrait plan. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Use for:

```text id="i7k46o"
human-readable debugging
code review artifacts
golden snapshots
plan diffing
documentation
visualization pipeline inputs
```

---

## 21.4.4 `Plan.from_json(json)`

```python id="lj2r5g"
plan = Plan.from_json(json_text)
```

`Plan.from_json(json)` parses a JSON string representation into a `Plan` object. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

Use for:

```text id="l1a1l6"
loading text plan artifacts
replaying reviewed plans
JSON snapshot tests
cross-language plan interchange through text form
```

---

# 21.5 `Consumer`: Substrait `Plan` → DataFusion `LogicalPlan`

## 21.5.1 Signature

```python id="3zrirf"
Consumer.from_substrait_plan(
    ctx: datafusion.context.SessionContext,
    plan: Plan,
) -> datafusion.plan.LogicalPlan
```

`Consumer.from_substrait_plan(...)` converts a Substrait `Plan` to a DataFusion `LogicalPlan`, using a `SessionContext`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="m74m2n"
from datafusion.substrait import Consumer

logical_plan = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, substrait_plan)
df_reconstructed = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan)

df_reconstructed.show()
```

`SessionContext.execute_logical_plan(plan)` executes a `LogicalPlan` and returns a `DataFrame`; this provides the bridge from consumed Substrait plan back to DataFusion execution. DataFusion’s plan API defines `LogicalPlan` as a relational-operator tree that can be created by SQL planning, the DataFrame API, or programmatically. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

---

## 21.5.2 Context dependency

```text id="tief3b"
Consumer requires SessionContext because:
  table resolution
  function registry
  catalog/schema state
  config/runtime assumptions
  extension/function mapping
```

Agent rule:

```text id="vp3fmd"
Substrait plan replay is not context-free.
Before Consumer.from_substrait_plan(...):
  register required tables
  register required UDFs if supported/needed
  configure catalogs/schemas
  configure object stores
  pin DataFusion version
```

---

# 21.6 `Serde`: SQL ⇄ Substrait convenience APIs

`Serde` provides serialization/deserialization helpers for SQL-to-Substrait workflows. The API documents file serialization, byte serialization, plan serialization, file deserialization, and byte deserialization. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

## 21.6.1 `Serde.serialize(sql, ctx, path)`

```python id="lqkace"
Serde.serialize(
    sql: str,
    ctx: SessionContext,
    path: str | pathlib.Path,
) -> None
```

Serializes a SQL query to a Substrait plan and writes it to a file. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="sx479d"
from pathlib import Path
from datafusion.substrait import Serde

Serde.serialize(
    """
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    GROUP BY country
    """,
    ctx,
    Path("plans/events_by_country.substrait"),
)
```

---

## 21.6.2 `Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx)`

```python id="0rvukg"
payload: bytes = Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx)
```

Serializes a SQL query to Substrait plan bytes. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="4tf5wr"
payload = Serde.serialize_bytes(
    "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events",
    ctx,
)
```

Use for:

```text id="jw9494"
database storage
message transport
cache payload
network API response
content-addressed plan artifacts
```

---

## 21.6.3 `Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx)`

```python id="k50wgj"
plan: Plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx)
```

Serializes SQL to a `Plan` object. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="ijjqu2"
plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(
    "SELECT country, sum(amount) AS gross FROM events GROUP BY country",
    ctx,
)

print(plan.to_json())
```

---

## 21.6.4 `Serde.deserialize(path)`

```python id="bfw52v"
plan: Plan = Serde.deserialize(path)
```

Deserializes a Substrait plan from a file path. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="1toyxu"
plan = Serde.deserialize("plans/events_by_country.substrait")
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

## 21.6.5 `Serde.deserialize_bytes(proto_bytes)`

```python id="pt5928"
plan: Plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(proto_bytes)
```

Deserializes Substrait plan bytes into a `Plan`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

```python id="pshcdg"
plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

# 21.7 API selection matrix

| Source artifact          | Target artifact          | Use                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| DataFrame / LogicalPlan  | Substrait `Plan`         | `Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)` |
| SQL string               | Substrait file           | `Serde.serialize(sql, ctx, path)`                    |
| SQL string               | Substrait bytes          | `Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx)`                    |
| SQL string               | Substrait `Plan`         | `Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx)`                  |
| Substrait JSON string    | Substrait `Plan`         | `Plan.from_json(json)`                               |
| Substrait file           | Substrait `Plan`         | `Serde.deserialize(path)`                            |
| Substrait bytes          | Substrait `Plan`         | `Serde.deserialize_bytes(bytes)`                     |
| Substrait `Plan`         | DataFusion `LogicalPlan` | `Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)`            |
| DataFusion `LogicalPlan` | DataFrame execution      | `ctx.execute_logical_plan(plan)`                     |

---

# 21.8 End-to-end workflows

## 21.8.1 DataFrame → Substrait bytes → DataFusion replay

```python id="ne6lmu"
from datafusion import SessionContext, col, lit, functions as f
from datafusion.substrait import Producer, Serde, Consumer

ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

df = (
    ctx.table("events")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .aggregate(
        [col("country")],
        [f.sum(col("amount")).alias("gross_amount")],
    )
)

plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)
payload = plan.encode()

# Later / elsewhere, with equivalent catalog context:
ctx2 = SessionContext()
ctx2.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

plan2 = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
logical2 = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx2, plan2)
df2 = ctx2.execute_logical_plan(logical2)

df2.show()
```

---

## 21.8.2 SQL → Substrait file → DataFusion replay

```python id="4c88zy"
from pathlib import Path
from datafusion.substrait import Serde, Consumer

sql = """
SELECT country, count(*) AS n
FROM events
WHERE amount > 0
GROUP BY country
"""

Serde.serialize(sql, ctx, Path("plans/country_counts.substrait"))

plan = Serde.deserialize("plans/country_counts.substrait")
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

## 21.8.3 SQL → Substrait JSON snapshot

```python id="l44rkj"
plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(
    """
    SELECT country, sum(amount) AS gross
    FROM events
    GROUP BY country
    """,
    ctx,
)

json_text = plan.to_json()

Path("plans/country_gross.substrait.json").write_text(json_text)
```

Replay:

```python id="va8qsb"
json_text = Path("plans/country_gross.substrait.json").read_text()
plan = Plan.from_json(json_text)

logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

## 21.8.4 Plan content-addressing

```python id="o12i9u"
import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SubstraitArtifact:
    bytes_payload: bytes
    sha256: str
    json_text: str


def make_substrait_artifact(df, ctx) -> SubstraitArtifact:
    plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)
    payload = plan.encode()
    return SubstraitArtifact(
        bytes_payload=payload,
        sha256=hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
        json_text=plan.to_json(),
    )
```

Use for:

```text id="n7a5zc"
query cache identity
plan-registry keys
artifact integrity checks
golden-plan snapshots
audit records
```

---

# 21.9 Substrait vs DataFusion protobuf plan serialization

DataFusion Python also exposes `LogicalPlan.to_proto()` / `from_proto(...)` and `ExecutionPlan.to_proto()` / `from_proto(...)`, but those are DataFusion plan protobufs, not Substrait. `LogicalPlan` is DataFusion’s relational-operator tree; its protobuf methods serialize DataFusion-native plans and currently do not support tables created in memory from record batches. ([Apache DataFusion][3])

| Serialization path                | Scope                           | Portability goal                      |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `LogicalPlan.to_proto()`          | DataFusion-native logical plan  | DataFusion plan roundtrip             |
| `ExecutionPlan.to_proto()`        | DataFusion-native physical plan | DataFusion physical plan roundtrip    |
| `Producer.to_substrait_plan(...)` | Substrait logical plan          | cross-system relational plan exchange |
| `Serde.serialize_*`               | SQL → Substrait                 | SQL-to-portable-plan artifact         |

Agent rule:

```text id="pfiudv"
Use DataFusion protobuf for DataFusion-internal plan replay.
Use Substrait for cross-system or portable-plan workflows.
```

---

# 21.10 Compatibility and context constraints

```text id="zhlk42"
Substrait plan compatibility depends on:
  table/catalog names
  schema names and data types
  function/operator support
  extension-function mapping
  SQL dialect/query features used at production time
  DataFusion version
  Substrait spec/version support
  custom UDF/table-provider availability
```

Substrait’s own docs emphasize a semantic specification, common and custom operations, and serialized representations, but cross-engine consistency requires each engine to support the operations used by the plan. ([substrait.io][1])

Agent rules:

```text id="xxmx3b"
Before replay:
  register same logical table names
  ensure equivalent schemas
  ensure function support
  avoid opaque Python UDFs for portable plans
  pin engine versions for regression tests
  keep plan + schema metadata together
```

---

# 21.11 Plan artifact envelope

```python id="il6qpr"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
import datafusion
import hashlib
import json


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SubstraitPlanEnvelope:
    datafusion_version: str
    plan_sha256: str
    table_contracts: dict[str, str]       # table name -> schema JSON/string/hash
    sql_source: str | None
    substrait_json: str


def export_sql_envelope(
    sql: str,
    ctx: SessionContext,
    table_contracts: dict[str, str],
) -> SubstraitPlanEnvelope:
    plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx)
    payload = plan.encode()
    return SubstraitPlanEnvelope(
        datafusion_version=datafusion.__version__,
        plan_sha256=hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
        table_contracts=table_contracts,
        sql_source=sql,
        substrait_json=plan.to_json(),
    )


def write_envelope(path: str | Path, envelope: SubstraitPlanEnvelope) -> None:
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(asdict(envelope), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
```

Agent rule:

```text id="o1gc45"
Do not store a plan artifact without:
  DataFusion version
  table/schema contract
  source SQL or source plan identity
  plan hash
  Substrait JSON or bytes
  producer application version
```

---

# 21.12 Logical-plan compatibility test pattern

```python id="gl7gde"
def assert_substrait_roundtrip(ctx: SessionContext, df):
    original_plan = df.logical_plan()

    substrait_plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(original_plan, ctx)
    logical_roundtrip = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, substrait_plan)

    assert logical_roundtrip is not None

    df_roundtrip = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_roundtrip)

    # Semantic output comparison should use deterministic sort and bounded fixture.
    expected = df.sort("country").to_pydict()
    actual = df_roundtrip.sort("country").to_pydict()

    assert actual == expected
```

Use with small deterministic fixtures:

```python id="pj1evk"
ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[make_events_batch()]])

df = ctx.sql("""
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    GROUP BY country
""")

assert_substrait_roundtrip(ctx, df)
```

# 21.13 Cross-context replay test

```python id="ynm16v"
def make_context_with_sources(path: str) -> SessionContext:
    ctx = SessionContext()
    ctx.register_parquet("events", path)
    return ctx


ctx_a = make_context_with_sources("events.parquet")
plan_bytes = Serde.serialize_bytes(
    """
    SELECT country, sum(amount) AS gross
    FROM events
    GROUP BY country
    """,
    ctx_a,
)

ctx_b = make_context_with_sources("events.parquet")
plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(plan_bytes)
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx_b, plan)
df = ctx_b.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

Agent rule:

```text id="15hb0b"
Cross-context replay validates:
  table name consistency
  schema consistency
  catalog/bootstrap contract
  function availability
  plan consumer compatibility
```

---

# 21.14 Plan exchange between systems

```text id="a9qida"
Producer system:
  builds SQL/DataFrame query
  produces Substrait bytes/JSON
  attaches schema/catalog metadata
  ships artifact

Consumer system:
  validates metadata
  registers tables/functions/providers
  deserializes Plan
  consumes into LogicalPlan
  executes or validates
```

Substrait is designed specifically to let systems support producing and ingesting a shared compute-plan representation rather than maintaining pairwise communication methods between all systems. ([substrait.io][1])

Agent protocol sketch:

```python id="il8q7z"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlanMessage:
    substrait_bytes: bytes
    plan_sha256: str
    datafusion_version: str
    required_tables: dict[str, str]  # table -> schema hash
    producer: str
```

Consumer guard:

```python id="lgyyuo"
def consume_plan_message(ctx: SessionContext, msg: PlanMessage):
    actual_hash = hashlib.sha256(msg.substrait_bytes).hexdigest()
    if actual_hash != msg.plan_sha256:
        raise ValueError("Substrait plan hash mismatch")

    plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(msg.substrait_bytes)
    logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
    return ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

# 21.15 Use cases

## 21.15.1 Plan exchange between systems

```text id="im7qcg"
Use:
  SQL parser service -> DataFusion executor service
  agent planner -> query execution worker
  UI query builder -> backend execution engine
  DataFusion producer -> compatible external engine consumer

Value:
  structured plan artifact
  avoids shipping raw SQL only
  can decouple query-generation and execution processes
```

## 21.15.2 Query-plan persistence

```text id="1agmkf"
Use:
  materialized view definition
  scheduled query artifact
  reviewed/approved plan registry
  reproducible benchmark plan
  audit log for generated queries

Value:
  store bytes for exact machine artifact
  store JSON for review/debug
  attach schema/version metadata
```

## 21.15.3 Logical plan compatibility testing

```text id="9oiyue"
Use:
  roundtrip DataFusion LogicalPlan -> Substrait -> LogicalPlan
  SQL -> Substrait -> LogicalPlan -> execution
  compare deterministic outputs on fixture data
  detect unsupported expressions/functions/types
  validate generated SQL feature subset
```

## 21.15.4 Plan visualization

```text id="cxh8pm"
Use:
  Plan.to_json()
  Substrait visualizer/tooling
  compare plan structure across generators
  debugging generated query pipelines
```

Substrait notes that text-form plans can help users see how a plan functions and that plan-visualization tools are a supported example use case. ([substrait.io][1])

---

# 21.16 Security and governance

```text id="avw5yz"
Substrait plans are executable query artifacts.
Treat them like code or compiled query plans.

Risks:
  reads from registered tables
  expensive execution
  unsupported functions causing errors
  sensitive table names / literals in JSON
  stale schema assumptions
  cross-tenant catalog leakage if context is shared
```

Governance rules:

```text id="9pnz8u"
For untrusted Substrait:
  do not execute directly
  validate plan metadata
  restrict registered tables
  use tenant-scoped SessionContext
  enforce output limits/timeouts at execution layer
  avoid registering sensitive catalogs/functions
  log plan hash, not full plan if sensitive
```

---

# 21.17 Anti-pattern catalog

## Anti-pattern: executing Substrait in a context with too many tables

```python id="17apnz"
ctx = global_shared_context_with_all_tables()
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

Correct:

```python id="ziuv3v"
ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_parquet("events", "approved/events.parquet")
logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

---

## Anti-pattern: plan artifact without schema contract

```python id="bttw34"
Path("plan.substrait").write_bytes(plan.encode())
```

Correct:

```text id="gu04zw"
Store:
  plan bytes
  plan JSON
  plan hash
  DataFusion version
  table names
  table schema hashes
  source SQL/logical-plan identity
```

---

## Anti-pattern: using Substrait as a universal guarantee of portability

```text id="y2ns7g"
Wrong:
  Substrait plan works everywhere automatically.

Correct:
  Substrait is a portable representation,
  but engines must support the used relations, types, functions, extensions, and semantics.
```

---

## Anti-pattern: relying on Python UDFs for portable Substrait plans

```text id="nsj7z3"
Python UDFs may not map to portable Substrait semantics.
Built-in functions and standard relational operations are more portable.
```

Correct:

```text id="i6ibow"
Use built-ins when portability matters.
Define extension-function contracts if custom functions are required.
Test consumer support explicitly.
```

---

## Anti-pattern: direct `Plan(...)` construction

```python id="0t1fud"
plan = Plan(raw_internal_object)
```

Correct:

```python id="jnyz3l"
plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)
plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx)
plan = Plan.from_json(json_text)
plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
```

The `Plan` constructor documentation says users should not call it directly and should create plans via `Serde` or `Producer`. ([Apache DataFusion][2])

# 21.18 Testing patterns

## 21.18.1 SQL bytes roundtrip

```python id="oo3r4f"
def test_sql_substrait_bytes_roundtrip(ctx):
    ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[make_events_batch()]])

    sql = """
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    GROUP BY country
    """

    payload = Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx)
    plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
    logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)

    df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)

    assert df.sort("country").to_pydict() == ctx.sql(sql).sort("country").to_pydict()
```

## 21.18.2 Plan JSON roundtrip

```python id="6ns024"
def test_substrait_json_roundtrip(ctx):
    ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[make_events_batch()]])

    plan = Serde.serialize_to_plan(
        "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events",
        ctx,
    )

    json_text = plan.to_json()
    plan2 = Plan.from_json(json_text)

    logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan2)
    df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)

    assert df.to_pydict()["n"][0] > 0
```

# 21.19 Deployment checklist

```text id="mmwf62"
Creation:
  [ ] Use Producer for LogicalPlan/DataFrame-origin plans.
  [ ] Use Serde for SQL-origin plans.
  [ ] Do not call Plan constructor directly.

Serialization:
  [ ] Use Plan.encode() for binary artifact.
  [ ] Use Plan.to_json() for human-readable artifact.
  [ ] Use Plan.from_json() for JSON replay.
  [ ] Use Serde.serialize(path) for SQL-to-file.
  [ ] Use Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx) for SQL-to-bytes.
  [ ] Use Serde.deserialize(path) / deserialize_bytes(bytes) for replay.

Replay:
  [ ] Build equivalent SessionContext.
  [ ] Register required catalogs/tables/object stores.
  [ ] Register required functions/extensions.
  [ ] Consume with Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan).
  [ ] Execute with ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan).

Portability:
  [ ] Avoid Python-only UDFs when portability matters.
  [ ] Prefer built-in functions and standard relational operators.
  [ ] Test consumer support for functions/types/extensions.
  [ ] Attach schema/table contracts to plan artifacts.

Testing:
  [ ] Roundtrip SQL -> Substrait -> LogicalPlan -> output.
  [ ] Roundtrip DataFrame logical plan -> Substrait -> LogicalPlan -> output.
  [ ] Snapshot JSON under version pin.
  [ ] Store DataFusion version with artifacts.
  [ ] Compare deterministic outputs, not just plan bytes.

Security:
  [ ] Treat Substrait plans as executable artifacts.
  [ ] Use scoped contexts for untrusted plans.
  [ ] Restrict registered tables/functions.
  [ ] Sanitize plan JSON before external sharing.
```

## 21.20 Section compression for LLM agents

```text id="gssfls"
Why:
  Substrait = portable structured query-plan representation.
  Use for plan exchange, persistence, compatibility testing, visualization.

Imports:
  from datafusion.substrait import Producer, Consumer, Plan, Serde

Producer:
  Producer.to_substrait_plan(logical_plan, ctx) -> Plan
  use when source is DataFrame/LogicalPlan

Consumer:
  Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan) -> LogicalPlan
  then ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan) -> DataFrame

Plan:
  do not construct directly
  plan.encode() -> bytes
  plan.to_json() -> str
  Plan.from_json(json: str) -> Plan

Serde:
  Serde.serialize(sql, ctx, path) -> None
  Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx) -> bytes
  Serde.serialize_to_plan(sql, ctx) -> Plan
  Serde.deserialize(path) -> Plan
  Serde.deserialize_bytes(bytes) -> Plan

Workflows:
  DataFrame:
    plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)
    payload = plan.encode()

  SQL:
    payload = Serde.serialize_bytes(sql, ctx)

  Replay:
    plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
    logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
    df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)

Rules:
  create equivalent SessionContext before replay
  register required tables/catalogs/object stores/functions
  store plan bytes + JSON + hash + schema contracts + DataFusion version
  prefer built-ins for portable plans
  test deterministic output after roundtrip
  treat plan artifacts as executable/sensitive
```

[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/substrait/index.html "datafusion.substrait — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html "datafusion.plan — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"

# DataFusion Advanced — 22) SQL unparsing and dialect conversion

This section follows the same dense, agent-facing technical-reference style as the Cyclopts source material. 

## 22.0 Core unparser invariant

`datafusion.unparser` converts a **DataFusion logical plan** back into a SQL string. It is a reverse-codegen layer: `LogicalPlan → SQL`, not `SQL → LogicalPlan`. The Python API documents `Dialect` and `Unparser`, states that the module supports unparsing DataFusion plans to SQL, and exposes dialect factories plus `Unparser.plan_to_sql(...)` and `Unparser.with_pretty(...)`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```text id="z2d7sf"
SQL text
  -> DataFusion SQL parser/planner
  -> LogicalPlan
  -> optimizer / DataFrame transformations
  -> LogicalPlan
  -> Unparser
  -> SQL string

DataFrame API
  -> LogicalPlan
  -> Unparser
  -> SQL string
```

Rust-side DataFusion describes `plan_to_sql` as the opposite of `SqlToRel::sql_statement_to_plan`: it converts a `LogicalPlan` to a SQL AST statement, then display formatting can turn that statement into SQL text. It may error when the plan cannot be converted to SQL. ([Docs.rs][2])

---

## 22.1 API surface map

```python id="c8y2ax"
from datafusion.unparser import Dialect, Unparser
```

| Object                       | Role                                | Factory / method                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Dialect`                    | SQL output dialect configuration    | `Dialect.default()`, `Dialect.duckdb()`, `Dialect.mysql()`, `Dialect.postgres()`, `Dialect.sqlite()` |
| `Unparser`                   | logical-plan-to-SQL converter       | `Unparser(dialect)`                                                                                  |
| `Unparser.plan_to_sql(plan)` | convert `LogicalPlan` to SQL string | `str`                                                                                                |
| `Unparser.with_pretty(True)` | enable pretty formatting            | returns `Unparser`                                                                                   |

The Python unparser API lists `Dialect.default()`, `duckdb()`, `mysql()`, `postgres()`, and `sqlite()` as static factories, and `Unparser.plan_to_sql(plan) -> str` plus `Unparser.with_pretty(pretty) -> Unparser`. The constructors exist but are “not typically called by the end user” for `Dialect`, while `Unparser` is constructed with a dialect. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

# 22.2 Dialects

## 22.2.1 `Dialect.default()`

```python id="qmd7lw"
dialect = Dialect.default()
unparser = Unparser(dialect)
```

Use when:

```text id="avtm21"
target is DataFusion SQL
no external SQL engine target
round-tripping inside DataFusion
baseline lineage SQL
```

`Dialect.default()` creates a new default dialect. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 22.2.2 `Dialect.duckdb()`

```python id="abec00"
dialect = Dialect.duckdb()
unparser = Unparser(dialect)
```

Use when:

```text id="go3bb1"
target engine is DuckDB
SQL handoff to DuckDB runtime
compatibility smoke testing against DuckDB
```

`Dialect.duckdb()` creates a new DuckDB dialect. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 22.2.3 `Dialect.mysql()`

```python id="z0fo14"
dialect = Dialect.mysql()
unparser = Unparser(dialect)
```

Use when:

```text id="o1eulw"
target engine is MySQL-compatible
identifier quoting/function rendering should follow MySQL style
```

`Dialect.mysql()` creates a new MySQL dialect. Note that DataFusion’s Python SQL parameter docs state that `$name` named replacement does not work for the SQL parser’s `hive` and `mysql` dialects because those dialects do not support named placeholders; this matters when comparing unparsed SQL with parameterized SQL-generation flows. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 22.2.4 `Dialect.postgres()`

```python id="p2zbd5"
dialect = Dialect.postgres()
unparser = Unparser(dialect)
```

Use when:

```text id="0i76l8"
target engine is PostgreSQL-compatible
identifier/alias conventions should follow PostgreSQL style
```

`Dialect.postgres()` creates a new PostgreSQL dialect. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

---

## 22.2.5 `Dialect.sqlite()`

```python id="of38jz"
dialect = Dialect.sqlite()
unparser = Unparser(dialect)
```

Use when:

```text id="b0n9ni"
target engine is SQLite-compatible
generated SQL should be checked against SQLite dialect limitations
```

`Dialect.sqlite()` creates a new SQLite dialect. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

# 22.3 `Unparser.plan_to_sql(plan)`

## 22.3.1 Signature

```python id="ti9bmm"
Unparser.plan_to_sql(
    plan: datafusion.plan.LogicalPlan,
) -> str
```

`plan_to_sql(plan)` converts a DataFusion `LogicalPlan` to a SQL string. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```python id="ysaxn4"
from datafusion import SessionContext, col, lit, functions as f
from datafusion.unparser import Dialect, Unparser

ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

df = (
    ctx.table("events")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .aggregate(
        [col("country")],
        [f.sum(col("amount")).alias("gross_amount")],
    )
)

plan = df.logical_plan()

sql = Unparser(Dialect.default()).plan_to_sql(plan)
print(sql)
```

---

## 22.3.2 Unparse optimized vs unoptimized plan

```python id="eo4037"
unparser = Unparser(Dialect.default())

sql_unoptimized = unparser.plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
sql_optimized = unparser.plan_to_sql(df.optimized_logical_plan())
```

Policy:

```text id="1ylp6i"
Unoptimized logical plan:
  closer to author intent / DataFrame construction sequence
  better for lineage and query reconstruction

Optimized logical plan:
  closer to optimizer-chosen logical shape
  may contain rewrites not ideal for readable SQL
  better for debug/codegen of optimizer output
  more version-sensitive
```

Rust `plan_to_sql` can return an error if the plan cannot be converted to SQL, so generated systems should wrap unparse calls and preserve fallback diagnostics such as logical-plan display. ([Docs.rs][2])

```python id="mr4onj"
def safe_plan_to_sql(plan, dialect=None, *, pretty: bool = False) -> str:
    dialect = dialect or Dialect.default()
    unparser = Unparser(dialect).with_pretty(pretty)
    try:
        return unparser.plan_to_sql(plan)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not unparse DataFusion logical plan to SQL: {exc}") from exc
```

---

# 22.4 `Unparser.with_pretty(True)`

## 22.4.1 Signature

```python id="aapvvi"
Unparser.with_pretty(pretty: bool) -> Unparser
```

`with_pretty(pretty)` sets the pretty flag and returns an `Unparser`. ([Apache DataFusion][1])

```python id="w36m0x"
unparser = Unparser(Dialect.default()).with_pretty(True)
sql = unparser.plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
```

Use pretty SQL for:

```text id="itxfw4"
human review
lineage logs
docs
golden snapshots
code review artifacts
debugging generated plans
```

Use compact SQL for:

```text id="whv2qb"
machine comparison
query registry keys
cache fingerprints
short logs
transport payloads
```

# 22.5 Core workflow patterns

## 22.5.1 DataFrame pipeline → SQL lineage

```python id="tp9ewl"
from datafusion import col, lit, functions as f
from datafusion.unparser import Dialect, Unparser

def build_report(ctx):
    return (
        ctx.table("events")
        .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
        .aggregate(
            [col("country")],
            [
                f.count_star().alias("n_rows"),
                f.sum(col("amount")).alias("gross_amount"),
            ],
        )
        .sort(col("gross_amount").sort(ascending=False))
    )

df = build_report(ctx)

lineage_sql = (
    Unparser(Dialect.default())
    .with_pretty(True)
    .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
)
```

Value case:

```text id="sje9y6"
DataFrame API code is composable.
SQL lineage string is inspectable.
Unparser bridges generated DataFrame pipelines back into human-readable SQL.
```

## 22.5.4 Cross-dialect compatibility matrix

```python id="h88vwh"
def unparse_all_dialects(plan, *, pretty: bool = True) -> dict[str, str]:
    dialects = {
        "default": Dialect.default(),
        "duckdb": Dialect.duckdb(),
        "mysql": Dialect.mysql(),
        "postgres": Dialect.postgres(),
        "sqlite": Dialect.sqlite(),
    }

    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name, dialect in dialects.items():
        try:
            out[name] = Unparser(dialect).with_pretty(pretty).plan_to_sql(plan)
        except Exception as exc:
            out[name] = f"-- UNPARSE_FAILED[{name}]: {exc}"
    return out
```

Use in tests:

```python id="o1a7nd"
sql_by_dialect = unparse_all_dialects(df.logical_plan())

assert "SELECT" in sql_by_dialect["default"]
assert not sql_by_dialect["postgres"].startswith("-- UNPARSE_FAILED")
```

# 22.6 Query lineage use cases

## 22.6.1 Log a SQL lineage artifact for DataFrame pipeline

```python id="1sah79"
def lineage_sql_for_df(df, *, dialect=Dialect.default()) -> str:
    return (
        Unparser(dialect)
        .with_pretty(True)
        .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())

```

Lineage envelope:

```python id="76016c"
from dataclasses import dataclass
import datafusion
import hashlib


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QueryLineage:
    datafusion_version: str
    dialect: str
    sql: str
    sql_sha256: str


def make_lineage(df, dialect_name: str, dialect) -> QueryLineage:
    sql = Unparser(dialect).with_pretty(True).plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
    return QueryLineage(
        datafusion_version=datafusion.__version__,
        dialect=dialect_name,
        sql=sql,
        sql_sha256=hashlib.sha256(sql.encode()).hexdigest(),
    )
```

# 22.7 SQL generation from DataFrame pipelines

## 22.7.1 Generated DataFrame → SQL pushdown

```python id="onabk1"
def generated_pipeline(ctx, metric: str):
    allowed = {"amount", "latency_ms"}
    if metric not in allowed:
        raise ValueError(metric)

    return (
        ctx.table("events")
        .filter(col(metric).is_not_null())
        .aggregate(
            [col("country")],
            [
                f.avg(col(metric)).alias(f"avg_{metric}"),
                f.count_star().alias("n_rows"),
            ],
        )
    )


df = generated_pipeline(ctx, "amount")

pushdown_sql = (
    Unparser(Dialect.duckdb())
    .with_pretty(True)
    .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
)
```

Use cases:

```text id="wihzzb"
remote SQL pushdown
SQL-only downstream systems
preview generated logic to users
migration from DataFrame builders to SQL templates
```

Agent rule:

```text id="0uqdsz"
Unparsed SQL is generated SQL, not guaranteed original SQL.
Validate it against target dialect/engine before pushdown.
```

## 22.7.2 Safe pushdown wrapper

```python id="fjghwj"
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PushdownSQL:
    dialect: str
    sql: str
    validated: bool = False


def build_pushdown_sql(df, dialect_name: str) -> PushdownSQL:
    dialects = {
        "duckdb": Dialect.duckdb(),
        "postgres": Dialect.postgres(),
        "mysql": Dialect.mysql(),
        "sqlite": Dialect.sqlite(),
        "default": Dialect.default(),
    }

    if dialect_name not in dialects:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dialect: {dialect_name}")

    sql = (
        Unparser(dialects[dialect_name])
        .with_pretty(True)
        .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
    )

    return PushdownSQL(dialect=dialect_name, sql=sql)
```

Validation step:

```text id="x1aihf"
Target-engine validation:
  parse generated SQL in target engine
  run against fixture tables
  compare result with DataFusion fixture result
  store compatibility result per query/dialect/version
```
