# DataFusion Advanced — 29) Schema engineering III: schema evolution, compatibility, and drift management

## 29.0 Core governance invariant

Production DataFusion pipelines need a **schema lifecycle**, not only explicit schemas. The lifecycle contract is:

```text
canonical schema registry
  -> source registration schema
  -> runtime df.schema() validation
  -> transformation output schema validation
  -> write/output schema validation
  -> compatibility gate for future schema versions
  -> CI drift detection
  -> migration playbooks
```

A PyArrow `Schema` defines column names, types, and metadata for tables/record batches; schema metadata is also used for round-tripping systems such as Pandas. PyArrow schemas support metadata-sensitive equality, structural edits that return new schema objects, serialization, and human-readable rendering, making them suitable as registry artifacts and CI contracts. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

# 29.1 Schema versioning model

## 29.1.1 Version identity

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
import pyarrow as pa


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SchemaVersion:
    name: str
    version: str
    schema: pa.Schema
    compatibility: str  # "backward" | "forward" | "full" | "breaking"
```

Recommended schema-level metadata:

```python
EVENTS_SCHEMA_V1 = pa.schema(
    [
        pa.field("event_id", pa.string(), nullable=False),
        pa.field("user_id", pa.int64(), nullable=False),
        pa.field("amount", pa.decimal128(18, 2), nullable=True),
        pa.field("event_ts", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=False),
        pa.field("dt", pa.string(), nullable=False),
    ],
    metadata={
        "schema_name": "events",
        "schema_version": "1.0.0",
        "compatibility": "backward",
        "owner": "data-platform",
    },
)
```

## 29.1.2 Versioning rules

```text
patch:
  metadata-only addition
  documentation-only change
  non-semantic description update

minor:
  add nullable field
  add optional nested child field
  add metadata that consumers may ignore
  widen type safely

major:
  remove field
  rename field
  change field meaning
  tighten nullability
  narrow type
  change decimal scale
  change timestamp unit/timezone
  change partition column type/name
```

Agent rule:

```text
Schema version must change when:
  field set changes
  type changes
  nullability changes
  metadata contract changes
  nested field path changes
  partition contract changes
```

---

# 29.2 Schema hash / fingerprint

## 29.2.1 Canonical fingerprint

```python
import hashlib
import json
import pyarrow as pa


def decode_metadata(md: dict[bytes, bytes] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    if not md:
        return {}
    return {k.decode("utf-8"): v.decode("utf-8") for k, v in sorted(md.items())}


def field_to_contract(field: pa.Field) -> dict:
    return {
        "name": field.name,
        "type": str(field.type),
        "nullable": field.nullable,
        "metadata": decode_metadata(field.metadata),
    }


def schema_to_contract(schema: pa.Schema, *, include_metadata: bool = True) -> dict:
    return {
        "fields": [field_to_contract(field) for field in schema],
        "metadata": decode_metadata(schema.metadata) if include_metadata else {},
    }


def schema_fingerprint(schema: pa.Schema, *, include_metadata: bool = True) -> str:
    payload = json.dumps(
        schema_to_contract(schema, include_metadata=include_metadata),
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
```

## 29.2.2 Binary IPC fingerprint

```python
def schema_ipc_fingerprint(schema: pa.Schema) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(schema.serialize().to_pybytes()).hexdigest()
```

`Schema.serialize()` emits an encapsulated IPC representation, while `Schema.to_string(...)` and `Schema.equals(..., check_metadata=True)` support human and metadata-sensitive contract workflows. ([Apache Arrow][1])

## 29.2.3 Policy

```text
Use JSON/text fingerprint:
  stable registry diffing
  human-readable artifact review
  explicit metadata normalization

Use IPC fingerprint:
  Arrow-native binary identity
  transport/storage artifact
  low-level compatibility tests

Store both when possible.
```

---

# 29.3 Schema diff algorithms

## 29.3.1 Top-level schema diff

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field as dc_field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FieldChange:
    name: str
    old: pa.Field | None
    new: pa.Field | None
    change_type: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SchemaDiff:
    added: list[pa.Field] = dc_field(default_factory=list)
    removed: list[pa.Field] = dc_field(default_factory=list)
    changed: list[FieldChange] = dc_field(default_factory=list)
    reordered: bool = False
    metadata_changed: bool = False


def diff_schema(old: pa.Schema, new: pa.Schema, *, check_metadata: bool = True) -> SchemaDiff:
    old_by_name = {f.name: f for f in old}
    new_by_name = {f.name: f for f in new}

    added = [new_by_name[name] for name in sorted(set(new_by_name) - set(old_by_name))]
    removed = [old_by_name[name] for name in sorted(set(old_by_name) - set(new_by_name))]

    changed = []
    for name in sorted(set(old_by_name) & set(new_by_name)):
        old_f = old_by_name[name]
        new_f = new_by_name[name]

        if old_f.type != new_f.type:
            changed.append(FieldChange(name, old_f, new_f, "type"))
        elif old_f.nullable != new_f.nullable:
            changed.append(FieldChange(name, old_f, new_f, "nullability"))
        elif check_metadata and old_f.metadata != new_f.metadata:
            changed.append(FieldChange(name, old_f, new_f, "metadata"))

    reordered = [f.name for f in old] != [f.name for f in new if f.name in old_by_name]
    metadata_changed = check_metadata and old.metadata != new.metadata

    return SchemaDiff(
        added=added,
        removed=removed,
        changed=changed,
        reordered=reordered,
        metadata_changed=metadata_changed,
    )
```

## 29.3.2 Nested schema diff

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NestedField:
    path: str
    field: pa.Field


def walk_field(field: pa.Field, prefix: str = ""):
    path = f"{prefix}.{field.name}" if prefix else field.name
    yield NestedField(path, field)

    typ = field.type

    if pa.types.is_struct(typ):
        for i in range(typ.num_fields):
            yield from walk_field(typ.field(i), path)

    elif pa.types.is_list(typ) or pa.types.is_large_list(typ) or pa.types.is_fixed_size_list(typ):
        yield from walk_field(typ.value_field, f"{path}.item")

    elif pa.types.is_map(typ):
        yield from walk_field(typ.key_field, f"{path}.key")
        yield from walk_field(typ.item_field, f"{path}.value")


def flatten_schema_paths(schema: pa.Schema) -> dict[str, pa.Field]:
    out = {}
    for field in schema:
        for nested in walk_field(field):
            out[nested.path] = nested.field
    return out


def diff_nested_schema(old: pa.Schema, new: pa.Schema, *, check_metadata: bool = True) -> dict:
    old_paths = flatten_schema_paths(old)
    new_paths = flatten_schema_paths(new)

    added = sorted(set(new_paths) - set(old_paths))
    removed = sorted(set(old_paths) - set(new_paths))

    changed = []
    for path in sorted(set(old_paths) & set(new_paths)):
        old_f = old_paths[path]
        new_f = new_paths[path]
        if not old_f.equals(new_f, check_metadata=check_metadata):
            changed.append(path)

    return {
        "added": added,
        "removed": removed,
        "changed": changed,
    }
```

---

# 29.4 Compatibility classification

## 29.4.1 Compatibility enum

```python
from enum import Enum


class Compatibility(str, Enum):
    COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
    BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE = "backward_compatible"
    FORWARD_COMPATIBLE = "forward_compatible"
    BREAKING = "breaking"
    REVIEW_REQUIRED = "review_required"
```

## 29.4.2 Field-change policy table

| Change                                   | Classification                  | Notes                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| add nullable field                       | backward-compatible             | old consumers can ignore it               |
| add non-nullable field without default   | breaking                        | old producers cannot supply it            |
| remove field                             | breaking                        | existing consumers may fail               |
| rename field                             | breaking                        | treat as remove + add                     |
| widen integer signedness/width carefully | review required                 | depends on value domain                   |
| int → float                              | review required                 | possible precision loss                   |
| float → decimal                          | review required                 | requires scale policy                     |
| decimal precision increase, same scale   | usually compatible              | consumer support required                 |
| decimal scale change                     | breaking                        | semantic value change                     |
| timestamp same unit, add metadata        | compatible/review               | if metadata-only                          |
| timestamp unit change                    | review/breaking                 | rounding/truncation risk                  |
| timezone change                          | breaking                        | semantic time meaning changes             |
| nullable False → True                    | backward-compatible for readers | producers loosen contract                 |
| nullable True → False                    | breaking                        | existing data may contain nulls           |
| field metadata added                     | compatible/review               | depends on governance                     |
| field metadata changed                   | review/breaking                 | PII/unit/semantic changes can be breaking |
| field reorder                            | usually compatible by name      | breaking for position-based consumers     |

## 29.4.3 Compatibility classifier

```python
def classify_nullability(old: pa.Field, new: pa.Field) -> Compatibility:
    if old.nullable == new.nullable:
        return Compatibility.COMPATIBLE

    if old.nullable is False and new.nullable is True:
        return Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE

    if old.nullable is True and new.nullable is False:
        return Compatibility.BREAKING

    return Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

---

# 29.5 Nullable compatibility

## 29.5.1 Rules

```text
nullable False -> True:
  safe for new data readers.
  downstream code must handle new NULLs.
  classify as backward-compatible but behavior-changing.

nullable True -> False:
  unsafe unless historical data is proven null-free.
  requires data backfill or validation.
  classify as breaking.

nullable unchanged:
  compatible if type and metadata contract unchanged.
```

## 29.5.2 Validation before tightening nullability

```python
def assert_column_has_no_nulls(df, column: str) -> None:
    n = (
        df.filter(df.col(column).is_null())
          .count()
    )
    if n != 0:
        raise AssertionError(f"Cannot tighten nullability for {column}; found {n} null rows")
```

`count()` is terminal and executes a plan, so use this only as an explicit validation job, not a cheap metadata operation. DataFusion documents `count()` as running a plan and potentially being slow for large or complex DataFrames. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

---

# 29.6 Type widening and narrowing

## 29.6.1 Safe-ish widening rules

```text
Integers:
  int8 -> int16 -> int32 -> int64
  uint8 -> uint16 -> uint32 -> uint64
  signed/unsigned crossing requires value-domain review

Floats:
  float32 -> float64

Decimal:
  decimal128(p, s) -> decimal128(p+n, s)
  decimal128 -> decimal256 with same scale, consumer validation required

String:
  string -> large_string only if consumer supports LargeString
  binary -> large_binary only if consumer supports LargeBinary

List:
  list -> large_list only if consumer supports LargeList

Timestamp:
  lower precision -> higher precision may be compatible if no semantic precision added
```

## 29.6.2 Unsafe narrowing rules

```text
int64 -> int32
uint64 -> int64
float64 -> float32
float -> integer
decimal precision decrease
decimal scale change
timestamp ns -> us/ms/s without rounding policy
large_string -> string without size proof
large_list -> list without offset-size proof
dictionary value type change
struct field type change
map key/value type change
fixed-size list size change
```

## 29.6.3 Type classifier

```python
def is_safe_numeric_widen(old: pa.DataType, new: pa.DataType) -> bool:
    signed_rank = {
        pa.int8(): 1,
        pa.int16(): 2,
        pa.int32(): 3,
        pa.int64(): 4,
    }
    unsigned_rank = {
        pa.uint8(): 1,
        pa.uint16(): 2,
        pa.uint32(): 3,
        pa.uint64(): 4,
    }

    if old in signed_rank and new in signed_rank:
        return signed_rank[new] >= signed_rank[old]

    if old in unsigned_rank and new in unsigned_rank:
        return unsigned_rank[new] >= unsigned_rank[old]

    if old == pa.float32() and new == pa.float64():
        return True

    return False
```

## 29.6.4 Decimal compatibility

```python
def decimal_compatibility(old: pa.DataType, new: pa.DataType) -> Compatibility:
    if not (pa.types.is_decimal(old) and pa.types.is_decimal(new)):
        return Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED

    if old.scale != new.scale:
        return Compatibility.BREAKING

    if new.precision >= old.precision:
        return Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE

    return Compatibility.BREAKING
```

---

# 29.7 Field addition/removal policies

## 29.7.1 Add field

```text
Allowed without major version:
  add nullable field
  add field with documented default/fill policy
  add optional nested field inside struct
  add optional map key by convention

Requires major or migration:
  add non-nullable field without default
  add required partition column
  add field whose absence changes semantics
```

## 29.7.2 Remove field

```text
Safe only after:
  deprecation period
  consumer usage scan
  compatibility window
  dual-write / alias field if rename
  major version bump
```

## 29.7.3 Rename field

```text
Rename = add new field + deprecate old field + remove old field later.

Never treat rename as metadata-only.
```

## 29.7.4 Deprecation metadata

```python
deprecated_field = pa.field(
    "old_user_id",
    pa.int64(),
    nullable=True,
    metadata={
        "deprecated": "true",
        "replacement": "user_id",
        "remove_after": "2026-12-31",
    },
)
```

---

# 29.8 Metadata-preserving changes

## 29.8.1 Metadata-sensitive diff

```python
def metadata_diff(old: pa.Schema, new: pa.Schema) -> dict:
    changes = {
        "schema_metadata_changed": old.metadata != new.metadata,
        "field_metadata_changed": [],
    }

    old_fields = {f.name: f for f in old}
    new_fields = {f.name: f for f in new}

    for name in sorted(set(old_fields) & set(new_fields)):
        if old_fields[name].metadata != new_fields[name].metadata:
            changes["field_metadata_changed"].append(name)

    return changes
```

## 29.8.2 Metadata compatibility policy

```text
Usually compatible:
  add description
  add owner
  add lineage
  add non-enforcing tags

Review required:
  change semantic_type
  change unit
  change classification
  change pii flag
  change timezone policy metadata
  change default value metadata

Breaking:
  pii false -> true without redaction policy update
  unit USD -> cents without data transformation
  semantic_type user_id -> account_id
```

## 29.8.3 Preserve metadata through schema edits

```python
def replace_field_preserve_metadata(schema: pa.Schema, name: str, new_type: pa.DataType) -> pa.Schema:
    idx = schema.get_field_index(name)
    if idx < 0:
        raise KeyError(name)

    old = schema.field(idx)
    new = old.with_type(new_type).with_metadata(old.metadata)
    return schema.set(idx, new)
```

PyArrow schema/field edit methods return new objects; metadata-preserving utilities should explicitly carry metadata when changing field type/name/nullability. ([Apache Arrow][1])

---

# 29.9 Parquet mixed-writer reconciliation

## 29.9.1 Failure modes

```text
mixed writers:
  schema metadata differs
  field metadata differs
  timestamp units differ
  decimal precision/scale differs
  column nullability differs
  dictionary encoding differs
  partition columns absent from file schema
  old files missing newly added fields
```

DataFusion Parquet read/register APIs expose `schema` and `skip_metadata`; `skip_metadata=True` can help avoid schema conflicts caused by metadata in the file schema, and `schema=None` causes inference from file data. ([datafusion.apache.org][2])

## 29.9.2 Reconciliation pattern

```python
CANONICAL_EVENTS = get_schema("events", "2.0.0")

ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "s3://bucket/events/",
    schema=CANONICAL_EVENTS,
    table_partition_cols=[("dt", pa.string()), ("region", pa.string())],
    parquet_pruning=True,
    file_extension=".parquet",
    skip_metadata=True,
)
```

## 29.9.3 Parquet compatibility scanner

```python
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from pathlib import Path


def scan_parquet_file_schemas(paths: list[str | Path]) -> dict[str, pa.Schema]:
    out = {}
    for path in paths:
        meta = pq.read_metadata(path)
        out[str(path)] = meta.schema.to_arrow_schema()
    return out


def summarize_parquet_schema_drift(paths: list[str | Path], canonical: pa.Schema) -> dict:
    file_schemas = scan_parquet_file_schemas(paths)
    return {
        path: diff_schema(canonical, schema, check_metadata=True)
        for path, schema in file_schemas.items()
        if not schema.equals(canonical, check_metadata=True)
    }
```

## 29.9.4 Policy

```text
Use skip_metadata=True when:
  file metadata differs but structural schema is compatible.
  metadata is not runtime-enforced.

Do not rely on skip_metadata when:
  field types differ.
  decimal scale differs.
  timestamp unit/timezone differs.
  nested field paths differ.

Use explicit schema for:
  mixed-writer directories.
  old/new schema transition windows.
  partitioned data with virtual partition columns.
```

---

# 29.10 CSV/JSON inference-to-explicit migration

## 29.10.1 Discovery phase

```python
candidate = ctx.read_csv(
    "events.csv",
    has_header=True,
    schema_infer_max_records=10_000,
)

print(candidate.schema())
candidate.limit(20).show()
```

CSV read/register APIs infer schema when no schema is provided, using `schema_infer_max_records`; JSON has a similar inference row-limit parameter. ([datafusion.apache.org][2])

## 29.10.2 Registry promotion

```python
DISCOVERED_SCHEMA = candidate.schema()

PROMOTED_SCHEMA = pa.schema(
    [
        pa.field("event_id", pa.string(), nullable=False),
        pa.field("user_id", pa.int64(), nullable=False),
        pa.field("amount", pa.decimal128(18, 2), nullable=True),
        pa.field("event_ts", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC"), nullable=False),
    ],
    metadata={
        "schema_name": "events_csv",
        "schema_version": "1.0.0",
        "source": "promoted_from_csv_inference",
    },
)
```

## 29.10.3 Production registration

```python
ctx.register_csv(
    "events",
    "events.csv",
    schema=PROMOTED_SCHEMA,
    has_header=True,
    file_extension=".csv",
)
```

## 29.10.4 Migration checklist

```text
CSV/JSON inference migration:
  1. infer on representative sample.
  2. inspect df.schema().
  3. correct types manually.
  4. set nullability manually.
  5. add metadata.
  6. create registry artifact.
  7. use explicit schema in read/register.
  8. add CI schema test.
  9. reject future inference drift unless approved.
```

---

# 29.11 Partition-column compatibility

## 29.11.1 Partition contract

```python
PARTITION_SCHEMA = [
    ("dt", pa.string()),
    ("region", pa.string()),
]

ctx.register_parquet(
    "events",
    "events/",
    schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA,
    table_partition_cols=PARTITION_SCHEMA,
)
```

DataFusion file source APIs accept partition columns; Parquet read/register and listing-table registration expose partition-column parameters, and file extension controls which files are selected. ([datafusion.apache.org][2])

## 29.11.2 Compatibility rules

```text
Partition column name change:
  breaking

Partition column type change:
  breaking unless all paths and consumers are migrated

Partition column removal:
  breaking for pruning/filtering/query contracts

Partition column addition:
  usually breaking for layout readers unless backward path logic exists

Partition value format change:
  breaking if predicates depend on string/date format
```

## 29.11.3 Partition assertion

```python
def assert_partition_contract(
    actual_schema: pa.Schema,
    partition_cols: list[tuple[str, pa.DataType]],
) -> None:
    for name, typ in partition_cols:
        if name not in actual_schema.names:
            raise AssertionError(f"Partition column missing from DataFrame schema: {name}")
        if actual_schema.field(name).type != typ:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"Partition column type mismatch for {name}: "
                f"{actual_schema.field(name).type} != {typ}"
            )
```

---

# 29.12 Pandas / Polars / Arrow schema preservation

## 29.12.1 Arrow as canonical interchange

```text
DataFusion schema contract:
  canonical = pyarrow.Schema
  DataFusion df.schema() returns pyarrow.Schema
  PyArrow Table/RecordBatch preserve Arrow schema
  Pandas/Polars interop may alter metadata/types
```

PyArrow `Schema` documentation notes that schemas converted from Pandas contain metadata about original Pandas types so they can be converted back to the same types. ([Apache Arrow][1]) Polars can construct from Arrow data and says the operation is mostly zero-copy, but unsupported Arrow types may be cast to the closest supported type; its schema API accepts objects implementing the Arrow schema PyCapsule interface such as PyArrow schemas. ([docs.pola.rs][3])

## 29.12.2 Preservation test

```python
def assert_arrow_roundtrip_preserves_schema(table: pa.Table) -> None:
    reconstructed = pa.Table.from_batches(table.to_batches(), schema=table.schema)
    if not reconstructed.schema.equals(table.schema, check_metadata=True):
        raise AssertionError("Arrow roundtrip did not preserve schema metadata")
```

## 29.12.3 Polars boundary test

```python
def validate_polars_boundary(pa_table: pa.Table) -> None:
    import polars as pl

    pl_df = pl.from_arrow(pa_table)
    pa_back = pl_df.to_arrow()

    # Metadata and exact type preservation may not be guaranteed for all types.
    if not pa_back.schema.equals(pa_table.schema, check_metadata=False):
        raise AssertionError(
            f"Polars structural schema changed:\nIN={pa_table.schema}\nOUT={pa_back.schema}"
        )
```

Polars also documents Arrow producer/consumer behavior and notes that it can move data in/out of Arrow mostly zero-copy, while converting a multi-chunk Series to a contiguous Arrow array may not be zero-copy. ([docs.pola.rs][4])

## 29.12.4 Policy

```text
Use Arrow schema as source of truth.

At Pandas boundary:
  expect metadata/type changes.
  validate schema after conversion.
  keep Pandas as bounded interop, not registry source.

At Polars boundary:
  validate unsupported-type casts.
  check exact nested/decimal/dictionary behavior.
  compare structural schema at minimum.

At Arrow boundary:
  prefer pa.Table / pa.RecordBatch with explicit schema.
  use check_metadata=True when metadata is contract-critical.
```

---

# 29.13 CI schema tests

## 29.13.1 Registry test

```python
def test_events_schema_fingerprint():
    expected = "known_sha256_from_registry"
    actual = schema_fingerprint(EVENTS_SCHEMA, include_metadata=True)
    assert actual == expected
```

## 29.13.2 Source registration test

```python
def test_events_source_schema(ctx):
    ctx.register_parquet(
        "events",
        "tests/data/events/",
        schema=EVENTS_SCHEMA,
        parquet_pruning=True,
```

```python
def test_report_schema(ctx):

    EXPECTED_REPORT_SCHEMA = pa.schema([
        pa.field("dt", pa.string()),
        pa.field("region", pa.string()),

    ])

```

## 29.13.4 Drift classification test

```python
def test_events_v2_is_backward_compatible():
    result = classify_schema_change(EVENTS_SCHEMA_V1, EVENTS_SCHEMA_V2)

    assert result.compatibility in {
        Compatibility.COMPATIBLE,
        Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE,
    }
```

---

# 29.14 Compatibility classifier implementation

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompatibilityFinding:
    path: str
    classification: Compatibility
    reason: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompatibilityReport:
    compatibility: Compatibility
    findings: list[CompatibilityFinding]


def classify_field_change(path: str, old: pa.Field, new: pa.Field) -> list[CompatibilityFinding]:
    findings = []

    if old.type != new.type:
        if is_safe_numeric_widen(old.type, new.type):
            findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE, "safe numeric widening"))
        elif pa.types.is_decimal(old.type) and pa.types.is_decimal(new.type):
            findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, decimal_compatibility(old.type, new.type), "decimal change"))
        else:
            findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.BREAKING, f"type change {old.type} -> {new.type}"))

    if old.nullable != new.nullable:
        findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, classify_nullability(old, new), "nullability change"))

    if old.metadata != new.metadata:
        findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED, "metadata change"))

    return findings


def classify_schema_change(old: pa.Schema, new: pa.Schema) -> CompatibilityReport:
    old_flat = flatten_schema_paths(old)
    new_flat = flatten_schema_paths(new)

    findings = []

    for path in sorted(set(new_flat) - set(old_flat)):
        f = new_flat[path]
        if f.nullable:
            findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE, "added nullable field"))
        else:
            findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.BREAKING, "added non-nullable field"))

    for path in sorted(set(old_flat) - set(new_flat)):
        findings.append(CompatibilityFinding(path, Compatibility.BREAKING, "removed field"))

    for path in sorted(set(old_flat) & set(new_flat)):
        findings.extend(classify_field_change(path, old_flat[path], new_flat[path]))

    if old.metadata != new.metadata:
        findings.append(CompatibilityFinding("<schema>", Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED, "schema metadata change"))

    if any(f.classification == Compatibility.BREAKING for f in findings):
        overall = Compatibility.BREAKING
    elif any(f.classification == Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED for f in findings):
        overall = Compatibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED
    elif any(f.classification == Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE for f in findings):
        overall = Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE
    else:
        overall = Compatibility.COMPATIBLE

    return CompatibilityReport(overall, findings)
```

---

# 29.15 Failure modes and migration playbooks

## 29.15.1 Field added

```text
Symptom:
  downstream consumers ignore or fail on unexpected column.

Playbook:
  add nullable field only.
  publish minor schema version.
  update registry.
  add output tests.
  communicate availability.
```

## 29.15.2 Field removed

```text
Symptom:
  SQL/DataFrame expression column-not-found failure.

Playbook:
  mark deprecated with metadata.
  dual-write old and new fields.
  migrate consumers.
  remove in major version.
  add CI test preventing old field usage.
```

## 29.15.3 Field renamed

```text
Symptom:
  same as removal; lineage unclear.

Playbook:
  add new field.
  keep old field temporarily.
  metadata old field: deprecated=true, replacement=new_name.
  publish migration window.
  remove old field in major release.
```

## 29.15.4 Type widened

```text
Symptom:
  downstream strict schema equality fails.

Playbook:
  classify as compatible/review.
  validate values fit old/new range.
  update registry minor version.
  update consumers that assert exact type.
```

## 29.15.5 Type narrowed

```text
Symptom:
  overflow, precision loss, cast failure.

Playbook:
  block by default.
  run data-domain validation.
  add explicit cast with failure tracking.
  major version if approved.
```

## 29.15.6 Decimal scale changed

```text
Symptom:
  values change meaning.

Playbook:
  treat as breaking.
  add new column with new scale.
  transform explicitly.
  backfill.
  major version.
```

## 29.15.7 Timestamp timezone/unit changed

```text
Symptom:
  ordering/window/filter differences.

Playbook:
  add new timestamp column.
  convert explicitly.
  validate monotonicity/order.
  major version if replacing old field.
```

## 29.15.8 Parquet mixed writer

```text
Symptom:
  schema conflict at read time or inconsistent df.schema().

Playbook:
  scan file schemas.
  choose canonical schema.
  use explicit schema in register_parquet/read_parquet.
  use skip_metadata=True if conflict is metadata-only.
  rewrite/compact files to canonical schema when feasible.
```

## 29.15.9 CSV/JSON inference drift

```text
Symptom:
  same column inferred differently across files/runs.

Playbook:
  freeze inferred schema into registry.
  manually correct types/nullability.
  use explicit schema.
  add test on representative data.
  block future inference in production.
```

## 29.15.10 Partition-column drift

```text
Symptom:
  filters stop pruning, missing partition column, wrong partition type.

Playbook:
  stop ingestion.
  fix directory layout or registration partition cols.
  run partition inventory.
  validate `df.schema()` includes partition fields.
  update registry only if intentional breaking layout change.
```

---

# 29.16 End-to-end migration gate

```python
def migration_gate(
    *,
    old: pa.Schema,
    new: pa.Schema,
    allowed: set[Compatibility],
) -> CompatibilityReport:
    report = classify_schema_change(old, new)

    if report.compatibility not in allowed:
        details = "\n".join(
            f"{f.path}: {f.classification.value}: {f.reason}"
            for f in report.findings
        )
        raise AssertionError(
            f"Schema migration rejected: {report.compatibility.value}\n{details}"
        )

    return report
```

Usage:

```python
report = migration_gate(
    old=EVENTS_SCHEMA_V1,
    new=EVENTS_SCHEMA_V2,
    allowed={Compatibility.COMPATIBLE, Compatibility.BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE},
)
```

---

# 29.17 Deployment checklist

```text
Schema registry:
  [ ] every schema has name/version/owner metadata
  [ ] every schema has fingerprint
  [ ] schema text artifact stored
  [ ] schema IPC artifact stored if needed
  [ ] changelog stored per version

Compatibility:
  [ ] nullable changes classified
  [ ] type widening/narrowing classified
  [ ] field additions/removals classified
  [ ] metadata changes reviewed
  [ ] nested path changes diffed
  [ ] partition column changes gated

DataFusion IO:
  [ ] CSV/JSON production uses explicit schema
  [ ] Parquet mixed-writer datasets use explicit schema
  [ ] skip_metadata policy documented
  [ ] partition columns typed consistently
  [ ] source registration tests validate df.schema()

Interop:
  [ ] Pandas boundary schema checked
  [ ] Polars boundary schema checked for unsupported casts
  [ ] Arrow table/record-batch schema checked with metadata when required

CI:
  [ ] registry fingerprint tests
  [ ] source schema tests
  [ ] output schema tests
  [ ] migration compatibility tests
  [ ] drift report generated for failed checks
  [ ] major-version migrations require explicit approval
```

---

## 29.18 Section compression for LLM agents

```text
Core:
  schema governance = explicit schema + version + fingerprint + compatibility gate + CI tests.

Diff:
  compare field names
  compare field order if position-sensitive
  compare field types
  compare nullability
  compare field metadata
  compare schema metadata
  recurse through struct/list/map nested paths

Compatible:
  add nullable field
  add optional nested child
  widen numeric type with review
  increase decimal precision with same scale
  add non-enforcing metadata

Breaking:
  remove field
  rename field
  add non-nullable field without default
  tighten nullability
  narrow type
  decimal scale change
  timestamp timezone/unit change
  partition column name/type/layout change
  fixed-size list size change

DataFusion:
  register_csv/read_csv schema=...
  register_json/read_json schema=...
  register_parquet/read_parquet schema=..., skip_metadata=True for metadata-only conflicts
  table_partition_cols must be stable
  df.schema() validates runtime contract

Interop:
  Arrow schema is canonical.
  Pandas metadata may be embedded in Arrow schema.
  Polars Arrow interop is mostly zero-copy, but unsupported types may be cast.
  Validate schema after Pandas/Polars boundaries.

CI:
  schema fingerprint test
  migration compatibility classifier
  source registration schema test
  transformation output schema test
  pre-write output schema test
  partition-column compatibility test
```

[1]: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/generated/pyarrow.Schema.html "pyarrow.Schema — Apache Arrow v25.0.0"
[2]: https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html "datafusion.context — Apache Arrow DataFusion  documentation"
[3]: https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/api/polars.from_arrow.html "polars.from_arrow — Polars  documentation"
[4]: https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/misc/arrow/ "Arrow producer/consumer - Polars user guide"

# DataFusion Advanced — 30) Plan lifecycle I: plan creation pathways and execution contracts

## 30.0 Core plan lifecycle invariant

DataFusion Python is a plan-building interface over a Rust query engine. SQL and the DataFrame API both produce logical plans; logical plans are optimized into physical execution plans; physical plans execute as streams of Arrow `RecordBatch` values. DataFusion’s own custom-provider guide summarizes the lifecycle as `SQL / DataFrame API → Logical Plan → Logical Optimization → Physical Plan → Physical Optimization → Execution`, with execution producing streaming record batches. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/custom-table-providers.html))

```text
Source / Table / SQL / DataFrame / Substrait / protobuf
  -> LogicalPlan
  -> optimized LogicalPlan
  -> ExecutionPlan
  -> RecordBatchStream
  -> collect / stream / write / convert
```

Agent rule:

```text
Never collapse these artifacts into one mental model.
LogicalPlan answers “what”.
ExecutionPlan answers “how”.
RecordBatchStream answers “running output”.
DataFrame is the Python lazy handle tying them together.
```

---

# 30.1 Artifact taxonomy

| Artifact                | Created by                                                       | Contains                             |                Executable directly? |           Portable? |            Context-bound? |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------: | ------------------: | ------------------------: |
| SQL string              | user/agent/template                                              | textual query                        |                      no, must parse |   dialect-sensitive | tables/functions required |
| `DataFrame`             | SQL/DataFrame/read/from APIs                                     | lazy query handle                    |               yes via terminal APIs |                  no |                       yes |
| `LogicalPlan`           | SQL planner, DataFrame API, Substrait, protobuf, custom language | relational operator tree             | via `ctx.execute_logical_plan(...)` |             limited |                       yes |
| optimized `LogicalPlan` | optimizer                                                        | rewritten relational operator tree   |  via plan execution if materialized |   version-sensitive |                       yes |
| `ExecutionPlan`         | physical planner / physical protobuf                             | physical operator tree               |              via `ctx.execute(...)` |      highly limited |                       yes |
| `RecordBatchStream`     | physical execution                                               | streaming Arrow batches              |          already executing/iterable |                  no |             runtime-bound |
| Substrait `Plan`        | Substrait producer/serde                                         | portable logical plan representation |                   no, consume first |             yes-ish |  needs compatible context |
| DataFusion protobuf     | `to_proto()`                                                     | DataFusion-native plan bytes         |               no, deserialize first | DataFusion-internal |                       yes |
| unparsed SQL            | unparser                                                         | SQL generated from logical plan      |             parse/execute elsewhere |   dialect-sensitive | tables/functions required |

DataFusion’s Python `LogicalPlan` docs define it as a tree of relational operators such as projection or filter, transforming an input relation to an output relation, and explicitly state that logical plans can be created by the SQL planner, the DataFrame API, or programmatically. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

---

# 30.2 Plan creation path A: SQL → DataFrame → LogicalPlan

## 30.2.1 SQL creates a lazy DataFrame

```python
from datafusion import SessionContext

ctx = SessionContext()
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

df = ctx.sql("""
    SELECT country, count(*) AS n
    FROM events
    WHERE amount > 0
    GROUP BY country
""")
```

`SessionContext` is the main interface for executing queries and creating DataFrames; it maintains the state of the connection between the user and the DataFusion engine. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

## 30.2.2 Extract logical plan

```python
logical = df.logical_plan()
print(logical.display_indent())
```

`DataFrame.logical_plan()` returns a `LogicalPlan`; the plan can be displayed, traversed, serialized to protobuf, and used to create new DataFrames. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 30.2.3 SQL path lifecycle

```text
ctx.sql(sql)
  -> parse SQL
  -> resolve catalog tables/functions
  -> create DataFrame
  -> df.logical_plan()
  -> df.optimized_logical_plan()
  -> df.execution_plan()
  -> terminal execution
```

Agent rule:

```text
SQL source is not sufficient for replay.
Replay requires:
  same or compatible catalog/table registrations
  same UDF/UDAF registrations if used
  same parser/dialect assumptions
  same security policy if DDL/DML/statements matter
```

---

# 30.3 Plan creation path B: DataFrame API → LogicalPlan

## 30.3.1 DataFrame API pipeline

```python
from datafusion import col, lit, functions as f

df = (
    ctx.table("events")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .aggregate(
        [col("country")],
        [f.count_star().alias("n")]
    )
    .sort(col("n").sort(ascending=False))
)
```

DataFusion Python lets users build a plan through SQL or a DataFrame API against in-memory data and files, and then run it in a multi-threaded environment. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/))

## 30.3.2 DataFrame is a logical-plan builder

```python
logical = df.logical_plan()
optimized = df.optimized_logical_plan()
physical = df.execution_plan()
```

A logical plan is a structured representation of a query describing high-level operations such as filtering, sorting, and joining, abstracting away physical implementation details before optimized physical execution planning. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/building-logical-plans.html))

Agent rule:

```text
DataFrame API is preferred for generated query structure.
SQL is preferred for human-authored query text.
Both converge on LogicalPlan.
```

---

# 30.4 Plan creation path C: file/read/source APIs → DataFrame → LogicalPlan

## 30.4.1 Direct read

```python
df = (
    ctx.read_parquet("events.parquet")
    .filter(col("amount") > lit(0))
    .select("event_id", "amount")
)

logical = df.logical_plan()
```

## 30.4.2 Registered table

```python
ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")

df = ctx.table("events").select("event_id", "amount")
logical = df.logical_plan()
```

## 30.4.3 Context and table requirements

```text
Direct read:
  path/source encoded inside DataFrame plan.
  object-store/file access still required at execution.

Registered table:
  table name resolved through SessionContext catalog.
  replay requires same table name and compatible provider.
```

`SessionContext.create_dataframe(...)`, table registration, table lookup, catalog lookup, and read APIs are all context-owned methods; therefore source-backed plans depend on the context’s catalog, object stores, and runtime configuration. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

---

# 30.5 Plan creation path D: Substrait → LogicalPlan

## 30.5.1 Consume Substrait

```python
from datafusion.substrait import Consumer, Serde

payload = ...
plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)

logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

`datafusion.substrait` exposes `Producer`, `Consumer`, `Plan`, and `Serde`; `Consumer` generates logical plans from Substrait plans, and `Producer` generates Substrait plans from logical plans. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/substrait/index.html))

## 30.5.2 Context dependency

```text
Substrait Plan is not self-executing.
Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan) requires:
  catalog/table names resolvable in ctx
  table schemas compatible
  functions/operators supported
  object stores registered
  custom providers available
```

Agent rule:

```text
Substrait improves portability of the plan artifact.
It does not remove the need for context reconstruction.
```

---

# 30.6 Plan creation path E: DataFusion protobuf → LogicalPlan / ExecutionPlan

## 30.6.1 LogicalPlan protobuf roundtrip

```python
from datafusion.plan import LogicalPlan

logical = df.logical_plan()

payload: bytes = logical.to_proto()
logical2 = LogicalPlan.from_proto(ctx, payload)

df2 = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical2)
```

`LogicalPlan.to_proto()` converts a logical plan to protobuf bytes, and `LogicalPlan.from_proto(ctx, data)` creates a logical plan from protobuf bytes. Tables created in memory from record batches are currently not supported. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 30.6.2 ExecutionPlan protobuf roundtrip

```python
from datafusion.plan import ExecutionPlan

physical = df.execution_plan()

payload: bytes = physical.to_proto()
physical2 = ExecutionPlan.from_proto(ctx, payload)

stream = ctx.execute(physical2, partitions=physical2.partition_count)
```

`ExecutionPlan.to_proto()` converts an execution plan into protobuf bytes; `ExecutionPlan.from_proto(ctx, data)` creates one from protobuf bytes; the same in-memory record-batch table limitation is documented for execution-plan protobuf serialization. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 30.6.3 Protobuf policy

```text
Use DataFusion protobuf for:
  DataFusion-internal plan replay
  version-pinned tests
  internal execution workers
  native plan artifact storage

Do not use it as:
  cross-engine interchange format
  stable cross-version contract
  replacement for Substrait
  plan snapshot for in-memory record-batch fixtures
```

---

# 30.7 Reverse path: LogicalPlan → SQL with Unparser

## 30.7.1 Unparse logical plan

```python
from datafusion.unparser import Dialect, Unparser

sql = (
    Unparser(Dialect.default())
    .with_pretty(True)
    .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
)

print(sql)
```

`datafusion.unparser` supports converting DataFusion logical plans to SQL; `Unparser.plan_to_sql(plan)` converts a logical plan to a SQL string, and `with_pretty(pretty)` sets pretty formatting. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/unparser/index.html))

## 30.7.2 Dialect-specific SQL

```python
duckdb_sql = Unparser(Dialect.duckdb()).plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
postgres_sql = Unparser(Dialect.postgres()).plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
mysql_sql = Unparser(Dialect.mysql()).plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
sqlite_sql = Unparser(Dialect.sqlite()).plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
```

## 30.7.3 Reverse-path policy

```text
Unparser is lineage/codegen, not guaranteed exact source reconstruction.

Use:
  logical_plan() for user-facing lineage.
  optimized_logical_plan() only for optimizer-debug SQL.

Validate:
  unparsed SQL can parse.
  target dialect accepts syntax.
  fixture outputs match.
```

---

# 30.8 LogicalPlan vs optimized LogicalPlan

## 30.8.1 Unoptimized logical plan

```python
lp = df.logical_plan()
print(lp.display_indent())
```

Meaning:

```text
direct relational representation of the DataFrame/SQL construction
best for lineage and query intent
before optimizer rewrites
```

## 30.8.2 Optimized logical plan

```python
olp = df.optimized_logical_plan()
print(olp.display_indent())
```

Meaning:

```text
logical plan after optimizer rewrites
better for performance reasoning
version/config-sensitive
may differ substantially from authored query
```

The custom-provider guide describes logical optimization as semantic-preserving rewrites such as predicate pushdown, projection pruning, expression simplification, subquery decorrelation, and limit pushdown. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/custom-table-providers.html))

## 30.8.3 Decision table

| Need                                   | Use                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| lineage                                | `df.logical_plan()`                                   |
| human explanation of authored pipeline | `df.logical_plan()`                                   |
| performance triage                     | `df.optimized_logical_plan()`                         |
| pushdown/pruning verification          | `df.optimized_logical_plan()` + `df.execution_plan()` |
| optimizer regression testing           | both                                                  |
| unparse back to SQL                    | usually `df.logical_plan()`                           |

---

# 30.9 ExecutionPlan

## 30.9.1 Physical plan extraction

```python
ep = df.execution_plan()

print(ep.display())
print(ep.display_indent())
print(ep.partition_count)
```

The Python `ExecutionPlan` API exposes `display()`, `display_indent()`, protobuf serialization/deserialization, child traversal, and `partition_count`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 30.9.2 Physical plan semantics

```text
ExecutionPlan contains:
  scan operators
  repartitions
  joins
  aggregates
  windows
  sorts
  limits
  output partitioning
  physical execution choices
```

Rust-side DataFusion defines `ExecutionPlan` as nodes in the physical plan; calling `execute` produces an async `SendableRecordBatchStream` that incrementally computes one partition of output. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/physical_plan/trait.ExecutionPlan.html))

## 30.9.3 ExecutionPlan policy

```text
Use ExecutionPlan for:
  performance diagnostics
  partition-count inspection
  physical operator checks
  custom-provider validation
  physical protobuf replay tests

Do not treat ExecutionPlan as:
  stable across hardware
  stable across config
  portable across engines
  ideal user-facing lineage artifact
```

---

# 30.10 Executing a LogicalPlan: `ctx.execute_logical_plan(...)`

## 30.10.1 Signature and usage

```python
df2 = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan)
```

`SessionContext.execute_logical_plan(plan)` executes a logical plan and returns a DataFrame. The context API also exposes `create_dataframe_from_logical_plan(plan)` to create a DataFrame from an existing plan. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

```python
logical = df.logical_plan()

replayed_df = ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
replayed_df.show()
```

## 30.10.2 Execution contract

```text
Input:
  datafusion.plan.LogicalPlan

Output:
  DataFrame

Still lazy?
  yes, returned DataFrame is a plan handle.
  terminal operation still needed for execution/materialization.
```

## 30.10.3 Agent rules

```text
Use execute_logical_plan for:
  plan replay
  Substrait consumption
  protobuf logical-plan replay
  custom query-language output
  plan transformation/lint pipelines

Requirements:
  same SessionContext or equivalent context.
  required catalogs/tables/functions/providers registered.
  compatible schemas.
```

---

# 30.11 Executing an ExecutionPlan: `ctx.execute(...)`

## 30.11.1 Signature and usage

```python
stream = ctx.execute(
    plan=execution_plan,
    partitions=execution_plan.partition_count,
)
```

`SessionContext.execute(plan, partitions)` executes a physical `ExecutionPlan` and returns a `RecordBatchStream`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

```python
physical = df.execution_plan()

stream = ctx.execute(physical, partitions=physical.partition_count)

for rb in stream:
    process(rb.to_pyarrow())
```

## 30.11.2 Execution contract

```text
Input:
  ExecutionPlan
  partitions count

Output:
  RecordBatchStream

Execution:
  streaming physical execution
  result batches consumed incrementally
```

## 30.11.3 Agent rules

```text
Use ctx.execute(...) only for:
  low-level physical-plan replay
  execution-plan serialization tests
  custom physical planning experiments
  provider/execution diagnostics

Most application code should:
  execute DataFrames, not physical plans.
```

---

# 30.12 `execute_stream` vs `collect`

## 30.12.1 `collect()`

```python
batches = df.collect()
```

Contract:

```text
terminal
executes full plan
returns list[pyarrow.RecordBatch]
buffers result in memory
best for small/bounded outputs and tests
```

The DataFrame API states that `collect()` executes the DataFrame and collects results into memory. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

## 30.12.2 `execute_stream()`

```python
stream = df.execute_stream()

for rb in stream:
    process(rb.to_pyarrow())
```

Contract:

```text
terminal
executes plan
returns RecordBatchStream
incremental output
best for large or unknown-cardinality outputs
```

DataFusion’s Rust physical plan docs describe execution as producing streaming record batches incrementally; the custom-provider guide also emphasizes that streams are where rows are produced during execution. ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/physical_plan/trait.ExecutionPlan.html))

## 30.12.3 Decision table

| Need                                   | Use                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| small test assertion                   | `collect()` / `to_pydict()`    |
| bounded notebook preview               | `limit(n).show()`              |
| Arrow-native full table                | `limit(n).to_arrow_table()`    |
| large export                           | `write_parquet(...)`           |
| large service response                 | `execute_stream()`             |
| physical-plan replay                   | `ctx.execute(...)`             |
| partition-aware sink                   | `execute_stream_partitioned()` |
| avoid Python-side full materialization | streaming / writer APIs        |

---

# 30.13 Catalog/table requirements

## 30.13.1 Context state required for plans

```text
A plan may reference:
  catalog names
  schema names
  table names
  table providers
  object stores
  UDF/UDAF/UDWF/UDTF names
  session config
  runtime properties
```

`SessionContext` maintains the connection/session state with the DataFusion engine and is the main interface for executing queries and creating DataFrames. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/context/index.html))

## 30.13.2 Replay bootstrap

```python
def make_replay_context() -> SessionContext:
    ctx = SessionContext()
    ctx.register_parquet("events", "events.parquet")
    ctx.register_udf(my_udf)  # if required
    return ctx
```

## 30.13.3 Table-provider dependencies

A custom table provider participates in query planning by describing table schema/capabilities and producing an execution plan when queried; its execution plan defines partitioning, ordering, and child relationships; and the stream layer yields record batches. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/library-user-guide/custom-table-providers.html))

```text
Replay of provider-backed plan requires:
  provider package installed
  provider registered under same logical table name
  provider schema compatible
  object-store/credentials available
  function/extension codecs available if required
```

---

# 30.14 Context reconstruction

## 30.14.1 Minimal context envelope

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TableBinding:
    name: str
    kind: str
    uri: str | None = None
    schema_fingerprint: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContextEnvelope:
    datafusion_version: str
    default_catalog: str
    default_schema: str
    tables: list[TableBinding]
    required_udfs: list[str]
    object_store_schemes: list[str]
    config: dict[str, str]
```

## 30.14.2 Reconstructable artifact requirements

```text
To replay a plan:
  DataFusion version
  logical/physical plan bytes or Substrait bytes
  table names and schemas
  source URIs or provider identifiers
  object-store registrations
  UDF/function registrations
  config/runtime values if physical plan matters
```

## 30.14.3 Agent rule

```text
Never store a plan artifact alone.
Store a plan artifact with a context envelope.
```

---

# 30.15 In-memory table serialization limitations

## 30.15.1 Documented limitation

`LogicalPlan.to_proto()` and `ExecutionPlan.to_proto()` both document that tables created in memory from record batches are currently not supported. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 30.15.2 Failure-prone pattern

```python
ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[batch]])

df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events")

payload = df.logical_plan().to_proto()  # may fail / unsupported for this source class
```

## 30.15.3 Safer test pattern

```python
# Use Parquet/temp file for serialization/replay tests.
df_input = ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
df_input.write_parquet(tmp_path / "events.parquet")

ctx.register_parquet("events", tmp_path / "events.parquet")

df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events")
payload = df.logical_plan().to_proto()
```

## 30.15.4 Agent rules

```text
For plan protobuf tests:
  prefer file-backed registered tables.
  avoid register_record_batches sources.
  avoid from_pydict/from_pylist-only sources.
  if in-memory fixtures are needed, use semantic output tests, not proto roundtrip.
```

---

# 30.16 Portable vs executable vs serializable matrix

| Artifact               |              Serializable | Executable without context | Cross-engine portable | Best use                       |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------: | -------------------------: | --------------------: | ------------------------------ |
| SQL string             |                       yes |                         no |     dialect-dependent | source query, lineage          |
| DataFrame              |  no durable serialization |                         no |                    no | Python lazy handle             |
| LogicalPlan object     |          in-memory object |                         no |                    no | DataFusion planning/audit      |
| LogicalPlan protobuf   |                       yes |                         no |                    no | DataFusion-native replay       |
| ExecutionPlan object   |          in-memory object |         with `ctx.execute` |                    no | physical diagnostics           |
| ExecutionPlan protobuf |                       yes |                         no |                    no | version-pinned physical replay |
| Substrait Plan         |                       yes |                         no |               yes-ish | portable plan exchange         |
| unparsed SQL           |                       yes |                         no |     dialect-dependent | lineage/codegen                |
| RecordBatchStream      |                        no |          already executing |                    no | runtime output                 |
| list[RecordBatch]      | yes if separately written |       already materialized |      Arrow-compatible | small bounded output           |

---

# 30.17 Plan artifact envelope

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
import datafusion
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path


def sha256_bytes(payload: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()


def sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlanArtifact:
    query_name: str
    datafusion_version: str
    logical_plan_text: str
    optimized_plan_text: str
    physical_plan_text: str
    logical_plan_hash: str
    optimized_plan_hash: str
    physical_plan_hash: str
    physical_partition_count: int
    context_envelope: dict


def make_plan_artifact(df, query_name: str, context_envelope: dict) -> PlanArtifact:
    logical = df.logical_plan().display_indent()
    optimized = df.optimized_logical_plan().display_indent()
    physical_plan = df.execution_plan()
    physical = physical_plan.display_indent()

    return PlanArtifact(
        query_name=query_name,
        datafusion_version=datafusion.__version__,
        logical_plan_text=logical,
        optimized_plan_text=optimized,
        physical_plan_text=physical,
        logical_plan_hash=sha256_text(logical),
        optimized_plan_hash=sha256_text(optimized),
        physical_plan_hash=sha256_text(physical),
        physical_partition_count=physical_plan.partition_count,
        context_envelope=context_envelope,
    )


def write_plan_artifact(path: str | Path, artifact: PlanArtifact) -> None:
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(asdict(artifact), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
```

---

# 30.18 Execution-contract wrappers

## 30.18.1 Logical-plan replay wrapper

```python
def replay_logical_plan(ctx: SessionContext, payload: bytes):
    from datafusion.plan import LogicalPlan

    plan = LogicalPlan.from_proto(ctx, payload)
    return ctx.execute_logical_plan(plan)
```

## 30.18.2 Physical-plan replay wrapper

```python
def replay_execution_plan(ctx: SessionContext, payload: bytes):
    from datafusion.plan import ExecutionPlan

    plan = ExecutionPlan.from_proto(ctx, payload)
    return ctx.execute(plan, partitions=plan.partition_count)
```

## 30.18.3 Substrait replay wrapper

```python
from datafusion.substrait import Consumer, Serde

def replay_substrait_bytes(ctx: SessionContext, payload: bytes):
    plan = Serde.deserialize_bytes(payload)
    logical = Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan)
    return ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical)
```

## 30.18.4 Safe bounded materialization

```python
def materialize_bounded(df, *, max_rows: int):
    return df.limit(max_rows).to_pydict()
```

## 30.18.5 Safe streaming execution

```python
def stream_batches(df):
    for rb in df.execute_stream():
        yield rb.to_pyarrow()
```

---

# 30.19 Failure modes by lifecycle stage

## 30.19.1 SQL → LogicalPlan failure

```text
parser error
unsupported SQL syntax
table not registered
function not registered
bad parameter substitution
DDL/DML blocked by SQLOptions
```

Mitigation:

```text
compile minimal SQL
verify table_exist
use param_values
disable DDL/DML for untrusted SQL
log schema/catalog context
```

## 30.19.2 DataFrame API → LogicalPlan failure

```text
bad column reference
ambiguous column
invalid expression
unsupported function call
incorrect UDF Expr usage
```

Mitigation:

```text
validate df.schema()
use col/lit
use df.col after joins
alias computed expressions
```

## 30.19.3 LogicalPlan → ExecutionPlan failure

```text
provider cannot plan scan
unsupported physical operator
missing object store
schema mismatch
custom provider dependency missing
```

Mitigation:

```text
inspect optimized logical plan
inspect provider registration
smoke ctx.table(...).limit(1).collect()
```

## 30.19.4 Execution failure

```text
file missing
credential failure
UDF runtime type mismatch
memory/spill failure
reader/writer failure
```

Mitigation:

```text
limit(1).collect()
execute_stream
explain(analyze=True)
direct UDF PyArrow tests
object-store smoke read
```

## 30.19.5 Serialization/replay failure

```text
in-memory record-batch table unsupported
missing registered table during replay
version mismatch
provider not installed
Substrait unsupported function/type
protobuf incompatibility
```

Mitigation:

```text
use file-backed fixtures
store context envelope
pin DataFusion version
validate replay in CI
prefer semantic output comparison
```

---

# 30.20 Testing patterns

## 30.20.1 SQL → DataFrame → LogicalPlan smoke

```python
def test_sql_plan_creation(ctx):
    ctx.register_record_batches("events", [[make_events_batch()]])

    df = ctx.sql("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM events")

    assert "Aggregate" in df.logical_plan().display() or "COUNT" in df.logical_plan().display().upper()
```

## 30.20.2 DataFrame API → LogicalPlan smoke

```python
def test_dataframe_plan_creation(ctx):
    df = (
        ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
        .filter(col("x") > lit(1))
        .select("x")
    )

    assert df.schema().names == ["x"]
    assert "Filter" in df.logical_plan().display()
```

## 30.20.3 LogicalPlan protobuf roundtrip with file-backed source

```python
def test_logical_plan_proto_roundtrip(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]}).write_parquet(path)
    ctx.register_parquet("events", path)

    df = ctx.sql("SELECT sum(x) AS sx FROM events")

    payload = df.logical_plan().to_proto()
    replayed = replay_logical_plan(ctx, payload)

    assert replayed.to_pydict() == df.to_pydict()
```

## 30.20.4 Substrait replay test

```python
def test_substrait_replay(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]}).write_parquet(path)
    ctx.register_parquet("events", path)

    payload = Serde.serialize_bytes("SELECT sum(x) AS sx FROM events", ctx)

    replayed = replay_substrait_bytes(ctx, payload)

    assert replayed.to_pydict() == {"sx": [6]}
```

## 30.20.5 Physical execution stream test

```python
def test_physical_plan_execute_stream(ctx, tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "events.parquet"

    ctx.from_pydict({"x": [1, 2, 3]}).write_parquet(path)
    ctx.register_parquet("events", path)

    df = ctx.sql("SELECT * FROM events")
    physical = df.execution_plan()

    stream = ctx.execute(physical, partitions=physical.partition_count)

    total = 0
    for rb in stream:
        total += rb.to_pyarrow().num_rows

    assert total == 3
```

# 30.21 Deployment checklist

```text
Plan creation:
  [ ] SQL path tested.
  [ ] DataFrame API path tested.
  [ ] Substrait replay path tested if used.
  [ ] protobuf replay path tested if used.
  [ ] unparser path tested if used.

Context reconstruction:
  [ ] table names recorded.
  [ ] table schemas/fingerprints recorded.
  [ ] source URIs/provider IDs recorded.
  [ ] object stores recorded.
  [ ] UDF/UDAF/UDWF/UDTF names recorded.
  [ ] DataFusion version recorded.
  [ ] config/runtime values recorded where relevant.

Serialization:
  [ ] avoid in-memory record-batch sources for protobuf roundtrip.
  [ ] use file-backed fixtures for serialization CI.
  [ ] pin DataFusion version for exact plan artifacts.
  [ ] compare semantic outputs, not only serialized bytes.

Execution:
  [ ] collect only for bounded outputs.
  [ ] execute_stream for large outputs.
  [ ] ctx.execute only for physical-plan workflows.
  [ ] ctx.execute_logical_plan for logical replay.
  [ ] partition_count inspected for physical replay.

Security:
  [ ] untrusted SQL runs read-only.
  [ ] untrusted Substrait/protobuf plans use scoped contexts.
  [ ] replay contexts register only approved tables/functions.
  [ ] plan artifacts sanitized before external sharing.
```

---

## 30.22 Section compression for LLM agents

```text
Plan creation:
  SQL -> ctx.sql(sql) -> DataFrame -> df.logical_plan()
  DataFrame API -> DataFrame -> df.logical_plan()
  Substrait -> Consumer.from_substrait_plan(ctx, plan) -> LogicalPlan
  LogicalPlan protobuf -> LogicalPlan.from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  ExecutionPlan protobuf -> ExecutionPlan.from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  LogicalPlan -> Unparser(...).plan_to_sql(plan)

Plan stages:
  df.logical_plan() -> unoptimized LogicalPlan
  df.optimized_logical_plan() -> optimized LogicalPlan
  df.execution_plan() -> ExecutionPlan

LogicalPlan:
  display()
  display_indent()
  display_indent_schema()
  display_graphviz()
  inputs()
  to_proto()
  from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  to_variant()

ExecutionPlan:
  display()
  display_indent()
  children()
  to_proto()
  from_proto(ctx, bytes)
  partition_count

Execution:
  ctx.execute_logical_plan(logical_plan) -> DataFrame
  ctx.create_dataframe_from_logical_plan(plan) -> DataFrame
  ctx.execute(execution_plan, partitions) -> RecordBatchStream
  df.execute_stream() -> RecordBatchStream
  df.collect() -> list[pyarrow.RecordBatch]

Contracts:
  DataFrame remains lazy until terminal call.
  collect buffers all output.
  execute_stream streams incrementally.
  physical plans are config/hardware/provider-sensitive.
  replay requires equivalent SessionContext.

Limitations:
  LogicalPlan/ExecutionPlan protobuf currently does not support tables created in memory from record batches.
  Substrait is more portable than DataFusion protobuf but still needs compatible catalogs/functions/providers.
  Unparser output is generated SQL, not guaranteed original SQL.

Best practices:
  store plan artifact with context envelope.
  use file-backed fixtures for proto tests.
  use scoped contexts for untrusted plan replay.
  compare semantic outputs in CI.
  reserve ctx.execute(...) for physical-plan workflows.
```

# DataFusion Advanced — 31) Plan lifecycle II: plan auditing, linting, and governance

## 31.0 Core governance invariant

LLM-generated DataFusion work should not flow directly from prompt → SQL/DataFrame → execution. It should flow through a **plan governance gate**:

```text
LLM/user/query-builder output
  -> DataFrame / SQL
  -> LogicalPlan extraction
  -> plan artifact generation
  -> schema/config/version attachment
  -> policy lint
  -> semantic tests / bounded execution smoke test
  -> approved execution path
```

DataFusion exposes the necessary inspection surfaces: `DataFrame` is lazy and represents a logical plan; execution occurs only at terminal operations such as `collect()`, `show()`, or `to_pandas()`; `LogicalPlan` and `ExecutionPlan` expose display, traversal, Graphviz, protobuf serialization, and partition-count APIs; and `EXPLAIN` / `explain(analyze=True)` expose plan and runtime metrics. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/user-guide/dataframe/index.html)) ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html)) ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/sql/explain.html))

---

# 31.1 Governance artifact model

## 31.1.1 Artifact categories

```text
Plan artifacts:
  logical plan text
  optimized logical plan text
  physical plan text
  Graphviz DOT
  DataFusion LogicalPlan protobuf bytes
  DataFusion ExecutionPlan protobuf bytes
  Substrait bytes
  Substrait JSON
  unparsed SQL

Context artifacts:
  DataFusion version
  SessionConfig values
  RuntimeEnv values
  catalog/schema/table bindings
  object-store schemes/hosts
  registered UDF/UDAF/UDWF/UDTF names
  source schemas and fingerprints

Policy artifacts:
  lint findings
  allow/deny decision
  severity
  reviewer / automated gate
  waiver references
  semantic test results
  plan-shape test results
```

A `LogicalPlan` is a relational-operator tree that transforms input relations into output relations and can be created by SQL planning, DataFrame API, or programmatically; it exposes display, Graphviz DOT output, schema display, protobuf serialization, child inputs, equality, and `to_variant()`. Physical `ExecutionPlan` exposes display, children, protobuf serialization, and `partition_count`. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

---

## 31.1.2 Canonical plan artifact envelope

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
import datafusion
import hashlib
import json


def sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def sha256_bytes(payload: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SourceBinding:
    table_name: str
    catalog: str | None
    schema: str | None
    provider_kind: str
    schema_fingerprint: str | None = None
    uri_redacted: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FunctionBinding:
    name: str
    kind: str  # udf | udaf | udwf | udtf
    volatility: str | None = None
    implementation: str | None = None  # builtin | python | rust | unknown


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PlanArtifactEnvelope:
    query_name: str
    query_purpose: str
    datafusion_version: str
    session_config: dict[str, str]
    source_bindings: list[SourceBinding]
    function_bindings: list[FunctionBinding]

    logical_plan_text: str
    optimized_plan_text: str
    physical_plan_text: str

    logical_plan_hash: str
    optimized_plan_hash: str
    physical_plan_hash: str
    physical_partition_count: int

    graphviz_dot: str | None = None
    graphviz_hash: str | None = None

    substrait_json: str | None = None
    substrait_json_hash: str | None = None
    substrait_bytes_hash: str | None = None

    unparsed_sql: str | None = None
    unparsed_sql_hash: str | None = None

    lint_findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    approved: bool = False


def write_artifact(path: str | Path, artifact: PlanArtifactEnvelope) -> None:
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(asdict(artifact), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
```

---

# 31.2 Plan hashes

## 31.2.1 Logical / optimized / physical hashes

```python
def plan_hashes(df) -> dict[str, str]:
    logical = df.logical_plan().display_indent()
    optimized = df.optimized_logical_plan().display_indent()
    physical = df.execution_plan().display_indent()

    return {
        "logical": sha256_text(logical),
        "optimized": sha256_text(optimized),
        "physical": sha256_text(physical),
    }
```

## 31.2.2 Hash policy

```text
Use hashes for:
  artifact identity
  CI drift detection
  audit records
  production incident correlation
  plan comparison without logging full sensitive plan text

Do not treat hashes as:
  semantic equivalence proof
  cross-version stability guarantee
  cross-config stability guarantee
  security boundary
```

Physical plans are more environment-sensitive than logical plans because they depend on data organization and hardware/runtime configuration; DataFusion’s explain usage docs distinguish logical plans from physical plans and note that physical plans account for data organization and hardware configuration. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/explain-usage.html))

---

# 31.3 Graphviz artifacts

## 31.3.1 Logical Graphviz DOT

```python
dot = df.logical_plan().display_graphviz()
Path("artifacts/plan.logical.dot").write_text(dot)
```

`LogicalPlan.display_graphviz()` returns DOT-language graph output intended for Graphviz-compatible visualization. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/plan/index.html))

## 31.3.2 Explain Graphviz

```python
from datafusion import ExplainFormat

df.explain(format=ExplainFormat.GRAPHVIZ)
```

`ExplainFormat` supports `INDENT`, `TREE`, `GRAPHVIZ`, and `PGJSON`; Graphviz emits DOT-format graph output. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/dataframe/index.html))

## 31.3.3 Graphviz governance policy

```text
Graphviz artifacts:
  useful for human review
  useful for architecture/debug documents
  useful for LLM-generated query approval flows

Risks:
  can expose table names
  can expose paths
  can expose predicates
  can expose literal values

Policy:
  store internally by default
  redact before external sharing
  attach DataFusion version and query hash
```

# 31.4 Substrait artifact envelope

## 31.4.1 Export Substrait

```python
from datafusion.substrait import Producer

plan = Producer.to_substrait_plan(df.logical_plan(), ctx)
substrait_bytes = plan.encode()
substrait_json = plan.to_json()
```

DataFusion Python’s Substrait module provides `Producer.to_substrait_plan(logical_plan, ctx)`, `Plan.encode()`, `Plan.to_json()`, `Plan.from_json(...)`, and `Serde` serialization/deserialization helpers. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/substrait/index.html))

## 31.4.2 Envelope

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SubstraitArtifact:
    producer: str
    datafusion_version: str
    logical_plan_hash: str
    substrait_bytes_hash: str
    substrait_json_hash: str
    substrait_json: str
    required_tables: list[SourceBinding]
    required_functions: list[FunctionBinding]
```

## 31.4.3 Policy

```text
Use Substrait artifacts for:
  plan exchange
  plan persistence
  logical compatibility tests
  cross-process planning/execution separation

Require:
  context envelope
  source table schema fingerprints
  function bindings
  DataFusion version
  artifact hash

Do not assume:
  every DataFusion function maps portably
  Python UDFs are portable
  replay works without context reconstruction
```

Substrait is designed as a format for describing compute operations on structured data for interoperability across languages and systems, but a consumer must still support the relations, types, functions, and extensions used in the plan. ([substrait.io](https://substrait.io/))

# 31.5 Unparsed SQL artifact envelope

## 31.5.1 Export unparsed SQL

```python
from datafusion.unparser import Dialect, Unparser

sql = (
    Unparser(Dialect.default())
    .with_pretty(True)
    .plan_to_sql(df.logical_plan())
)
```

`datafusion.unparser` supports converting DataFusion logical plans to SQL; `Unparser.plan_to_sql(plan)` returns SQL text, and dialect factories include default, DuckDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. The underlying Rust `plan_to_sql` can error when a plan cannot be converted to SQL. ([datafusion.apache.org](https://datafusion.apache.org/python/autoapi/datafusion/unparser/index.html)) ([docs.rs](https://docs.rs/datafusion/latest/datafusion/sql/unparser/fn.plan_to_sql.html))

## 31.5.2 Envelope

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UnparsedSQLArtifact:
    datafusion_version: str
    dialect: str
    pretty: bool
    plan_stage: str  # logical | optimized
    source_sql_hash: str | None
    logical_plan_hash: str
    unparsed_sql: str
    unparsed_sql_hash: str
```

## 31.5.3 Policy

```text
Use unparsed SQL for:
  lineage
  human review
  pushdown experiments
  SQL-only downstream consumers

Do not assume:
  emitted SQL equals original SQL
  emitted SQL preserves param_values
  emitted SQL is valid in every target engine
  optimized-plan SQL is readable or stable

Validate:
  parse in target engine
  run against fixture data
  compare semantic output
```
